From the Vaiṣṇava [lineage] comes the master of all mantras; from Sāvitrī come the supreme mantras; and from Gāṇapatya come the great mantras, as well as those of Ramā and Yāmuna.
The great mantras of Pārvatī, as well as those of Maheśvara, the mantras of the Kṣetrapālas, and also the Ādī-mīna; 21.
Recited and offered as oblations on this inexhaustible day, it bestows all accomplishments; they become immediately perfected—of this there is no doubt. (22)
By performing even a single Akṣaya day with devotion and other virtues, one attains the inexhaustible fulfillment of all desires; of this there is no doubt. || 23 ||
Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter, which yields all desires, in this manual concerning the son of Daśaratha, which is a compendium of the meaning of the Vedas.
[Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter in the glorious *Anuttarabrahmatattvarahasya*, the *Dāśarathīya Tantra*, which is a compendium of the meaning of the Vedas.]
The Blessed One said:
Now, therefore, I shall again fully declare the practice of the glorious eight-syllable mantra, which bestows the siddhis of the Nāgas; listen with a concentrated mind. (1)
Having spoken thus, while the sun was situated in the sign of Leo,
he went to the bank of the Gautamī, where three and a half crores of holy fords (tīrthas) are located.
At the beginning there shall be the Puṣkara-yoga, and at the end likewise for twelve days;
during the Mahāpuṣkara-yoga, one should worship the deities together with the sages.
In the waters of the Godāvarī, which possess the qualities of the illusory power of Śrī,
there is the presence of all the gods and the assembly of all the sages.
When Jupiter enters the zodiac sign of Leo, there is the presence of the sacred pilgrimage site of Samaya;
for twelve days, there is a gathering at Puṣkara.
On that supreme Mahāpuṣkara-yoga at the Gautamī river,
even a single day there possesses the splendor of a hundred suns.
Whether during the Mahāpuṣkara conjunction or even when joined with the Mahāyāya conjunction,
having bathed and performed recitation and other rites, one is liberated from all sins.
There is no one equal to this performer of merit upon the surface of the earth,
even among all ritual procedures involving mantras, fire-oblations, recitations, and the like.
It is said that even at each individual Dīna, great siddhi is attained;
for one who, with a mind fixed on the Supreme, bathes here at Māhāpuṣkara in the morning and evening, [great success is achieved].
Then, having rubbed his limbs with cow dung, the wise man should perform the daily fire-oblation every day after the thousand-rayed sun has risen and the [morning] rites have been completed.
Having arrived at the bank of the Gautamī, he worshipped the goddess Gautamī with perfumes, flowers, unbroken grains, and other offerings, as well as the Lord, the Teacher (Uragācārya).

Having bathed with devotion according to the prescribed rite along with its ancillary parts in the waters of the Godāvarī, and having received the permission of the preceptor, he performed the installation of the venerable eight-syllabled mantra together with its ritual application.

Having worshipped Gautamīdevī and the Teacher of the Gods (Bṛhaspati) as well, one should recite [the mantra] three hundred times more than that for each of the thousand lords; day after day, Gautamī should be saluted with devotion by one who desires the attachment of the goddess Dārvālī.
One should daily worship the glorious eight-syllabled mantra (aṣṭākṣarī-vidyā), accompanied by all the ritual placements (nyāsa), according to the command of one's own preceptor.
One should recite three hundred times the most excellent mantra among the Lakṣmī-mantras;
one should offer oblations three hundred times with the final [mantra] mixed with the three sweets.
Combined with bilva leaves and mixed with iron filings, one should offer a hundred oblations with the glorious eight-syllable mantra and the Śrī-mantra. (16)
Then, with each individual mantra of the Lord’s rays, he offered an oblation of clarified butter into the sacrificial fire-altar named Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa at Ayodhyā.
One should worship Śrī-Śrī-Yatī with the preliminary rites of the five limbs and the enclosures;
one may worship either at the Śālagrāma stone or at the discus-marked stone.
Then, in the *laghucakra*, one should constantly worship the venerable Śrīyati according to the sequence, offering flowers mixed with *bilva* leaves. || 20 ||
One should daily worship with three hundred offerings, accompanied by *tulasī* leaves, *ūrva*, *śrī*, *śrāśa*, *brahma*, and *cidyā*. (21)
One should worship the pair of the teacher’s sandals in his presence;
having worshipped them with various movements of the breath, one becomes a giver of hundreds of gold coins in the Nandana garden.
One should offer twelve niṣkas,
or else one pair of the teacher’s sandals, or even a single niṣka.
Having offered [the oblation] on each individual day, one should present it to the preceptor;
in the absence of the preceptor’s sandals, one should respectfully offer the mantra of the sandals.
Having recited [the mantra] twenty-eight times, one who is free from greed should offer a forest at the lotus-feet of his own preceptor every single day.
In the absence of the teacher, one must certainly entrust [the teachings] to the teacher’s son; one must certainly prevent even a grandson from withholding that [knowledge]. 26.
The teacher’s wife, or even the wife of a fellow student, on the first day, at midday, or even on another day. (27)
Having given fine silken garments along with pure collections of ornaments,
the wise man, skilled in mantras, must certainly act for the sake of the complete success of the entire sacrifice.
Having accomplished [the rite] on each individual day, and likewise on the auspicious day,
one should perform the previously mentioned fire-oblations, recitations, and so forth, in their proper sequence.
One should offer oblations of clarified butter from a tawny cow, or even that from a cow alone, into the fire while reciting the one hundred and eight verses and mantras situated in the *Śrīhṛdaya*.
Having performed the expiatory oblations (prāyaścittāhutis), one should perform the oblation of "offering unto Brahman" (brahmārpaṇāhuti).
Then, having worshipped one's own preceptor, who is identical in form to the venerable Guru and is the very embodiment of Hari.
With garments, ornaments, sacrificial rings, earrings, and so forth, one should worship a pure Śālagrāma stone, even if it has been fashioned by insects. || 32 ||
One should offer it along with abundant sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā) and other gifts; in the absence of many jewels and such, one is glorified by giving even a small amount. || 33 ||
One should certainly give twelve niṣkas as an auspicious priestly fee (dakṣiṇā), or else one may give six niṣkas, or even three niṣkas as the fee.
O child, accompanied by a calf and provided with a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), even a single milch cow abounding in milk should be given to the preceptor.
On each and every day here, the observer of the vow should feed Brāhmaṇas; or else, he should daily worship a single woman who has recently given birth, as well as images of Śrī.
Twelve married women and twelve Brahmins as well should be fed on the following day by the yogin at Mahāpuṣkara.
The wise person should daily drink the auspicious essence washed from the lotus feet of the teacher, for the sake of attaining the vision of Brahman. (38)
Having thus performed this vow with devotion during the great yoga known as Puṣkara, even by hosts of great sinners who have committed [sins] over ten million lifetimes, [the goal is attained]. (39)
Then Vimukta beheld Hari directly, the Lord of Śrī,
who bestows the perfection of the glorious eight-syllabled mantra— a perfection difficult even for the gods to attain.
O Lord of the Earth, place your trust even on this day;
for that great preliminary rite (puraścaraṇa) with all its constituent parts which was previously described by me has been performed.
The fruit of that [practice], along with its ancillaries, is obtained; there is no doubt in this matter.

O Lord of the Earth, today I shall [expound] the Mahāyāya, which bestows the fruit of liberation while living and grants the attainment of the glorious eight-syllabled mantra. 49.
Through the conjunction with Mahāpuṣkara, this glorious *Ācāryatoyaṇa*—

This bestows the attainment of the state of the Blessed One upon all people;
it should be situated on ground rich with stones and timber, either in the form of a bow or as a pillar. (51)
During the auspicious twelve-day period of the Mahāpuṣkara yoga, one should perform the gift of a white horse; there is no greater fruit than the gift of a horse.
The constant giving of palanquins, the Holikā offering, and gifts at night, as well as the daily giving of many garments and the gift of grain day after day. (53)

Having recited the previously mentioned document and made the formal declaration (saṃkalpa) in the presence of the auspicious Guru, one should thereafter seek refuge at the lotus feet of the Preceptor (Ācārya). 55.
O King, he should send a cow with its calf to the teacher's house;

Or, with the permission of the teacher, one may receive from other Vedic scholars as well;

Having offered a heap of fruits during the Mahāpuṣkara yoga,
he becomes a possessor of supreme liberation, endowed with all prosperity and the attainment of sovereignty.
Having performed the preparatory rite (puraścaraṇa) for the glorious eight-syllable vidyā with devotion during the Mahāpuṣkara yoga here, one shall attain supreme perfection.
When this king of mantras consisting of eight syllables is perfectly accomplished, one is highly exalted;
indeed, with one's own eyes, one beholds Śrī, the Lord of Fortune, face to face.
Through the vision of the Blessed One, he was endowed with a portion of the Blessed One; having become pure within his own body, he became a treasure-house of all prosperity.

that conjunction at sunrise is to be known as the yoga named Udvaya.
One who obtains the conjunction of the planets at the thousand-rayed [sun] is greatly honored;
if it occurs on a Monday, a great prosperity arises.
A bath in the ocean there necessarily destroys sin;
therefore, having bathed in the great ocean at the time of sunrise, [one attains purification]. 67.
Having become composed, one should install the Lord of Lakṣmī— who resembles the Preceptor— into the fire (jātavedas) for the sake of the consecration ocean.
Then, having performed a single oblation with the *vṛhadāvaraṇa* mantras,
he should offer oblations of sesame seeds mixed with cow’s ghee using the glorious eight-syllable mantra.
Having offered more than three thousand oblations,
one who is thus honored should reverently offer three hundred oblations of cow-derived clarified butter with the Śrī-mantra.
Then, having performed each oblation with the Bhagavadraśmi-mantras,
perform the fire sacrifice (homa), and thereafter offer the expiatory oblations (prāyaścittāhuti).
Having offered the oblation with the *brahmārpaṇa* mantra and having respectfully bowed to the fire,
one should worship the venerable Śrīyati three hundred times with the *brahmavidyā*.
Having respectfully prostrated with eight limbs before the two lotus-feet of the Ācārya-Cāraṇa, and having worshipped him with garments, ornaments, and other offerings. (73)
Having folded it many times and made it fourfold and even,
he should give it to the preceptor along with a large sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
I have described to you the excellent, middling, and inferior sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā).
O Lord of the Earth, one should give the fee for the gift of land in accordance with that [scale]. 75.
One should certainly give a Śālagrāma stone along with a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) into the two ears of the preceptor; from that, there arises auspicious liberation from the cycle of rebirth.
One should also give jewel ornaments for the ears of the preceptor;
one must certainly give two cows along with a proper sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
Having performed great acts of charity while possessing wealth,
one should subsequently feed the Brahmins and then feed the married women.
Then, the preceptor’s wife should offer a pair of auspicious garments;
she should also offer a bronze vessel for the purpose of eating, along with a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
One should offer sixty-four palas, or even twenty palas, to the Vāsinyīs;
having performed this at Ardhodaya, one should likewise perform it at Mahīdaya.
He attains the perfection of the glorious eight-syllabled mantra immediately;
from that time forward, he beholds Hari in his dreams.
He shall certainly attain the fulfillment of his heart's desires, which are difficult even for the gods to obtain;
O King, there is no doubt in this matter. (82)
The fruit that one obtains by giving a thousand loads of gold on the shore of the Ardhodaya ocean, that same fruit is obtained by giving even a single niṣka.

O King, at the conclusion of the homa of the glorious eight-syllable mantra, when the moon rises during the conjunction of the full moon, one obtains here the fruit of that [rite] along with its ancillaries, which is even greater; of this there is no doubt. (84)
From that time forward, even the gods, beginning with the king of the gods (Indra), will undoubtedly be constant granters of boons to him on earth. 85.
In the month of Vaiśākha, the lunar day of Lā (the first tithi) joined with Tuesday,
and further conjoined with the Caturdaśī-vatīpāta and the Svāti constellation, [is auspicious].
This is the Lakṣīnsiṃha yoga; it is said to occur in the evening.
This yoga is obtained on earth once every twenty-four years.
One should perform the ritual prostration before sunset, three *ghaṭikās* prior; then, having put on two garments, one should diligently offer libations to the ancestors.
Having performed the evening twilight devotions and having prostrated before the teacher, [he should do so] in the presence of the teacher, or else before his son or even his wife. 89.
Having paid homage and diligently offered libations to the ancestors,

having made the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*), restrained his breath (*prāṇāyāma*), and remained silent, he immediately performed the complete ritual placement (*nyāsa*) one thousand three hundred times.
One who is firm in their vows should master the glorious eight-syllabled mantra;
for among all the mantras of Lakṣmī, this mantra is therefore the most desired.

Having performed the rite of the three hundred [oblations] for the three hundred-fold Jātavedas, and having consecrated the Lord of the World, he was worshipped there with offerings by the attendants.
With the glorious eight-syllable mantra, he should offer one hundred oblations of clarified butter from a cow,
mixed with the three sweets, poured with devotion.
One should offer oblations with clarified butter one hundred and eight times for the sake of prosperity;
one should offer the most beloved Bhagavadraśmividya one by one.
Having performed the expiatory oblation and having performed the oblation dedicated to Brahman,
he should prostrate himself like a staff before the lotus feet of the preceptor.
A vessel made of bell-metal, filled with sugar syrup, measuring either twenty-five *śalās* or twenty *śalās* in capacity; || 96 ||
A pair of garments suitable for use as an undergarment and an upper garment,
weighing either forty palas or twenty palas.
Having approached the two teachers, he offered excellent Haricandana wood—
thick and very sweet— and presented a heap of nutmeg fruits.
One should give wealth measured by a year's worth of food to the feet of the teacher, or twelve niṣkas, or six niṣkas, or even six hundred niṣkas.

Furthermore, if on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight in the month of Vaiśākha, it should coincide with Tuesday, the Svātī nakṣatra, and the Vyatīpāta yoga, that is the rare and unattainable Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha-yoga. || 1 ||
Having recited the eight-syllable mantra one hundred and eight times, and having offered it at the pair of feet of the Guru in the evening during the Vyatīpāta yoga,
Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha shall be pleased. Then,
having presented the fruits arising from that offering, along with a pair of garments, sandalwood paste, jaggery, and a vessel of water— || 2 ||
"O you who possess abundant and capable wealth, you shall certainly attain the perfection of the eight-syllable mantra.
I, being well-pleased, shall grant you the accomplishment of all powers and the vidyā known as Lakṣmībālā."
Having enjoyed prosperity accompanied by excellent sons and grandsons, long life, health, and infinite happiness,
as well as divine and human pleasures, she goes to the abode of Vaikuṇṭha at the end of her life.
Thus, for the sake of accomplishing the eight-syllabled lore (aṣṭākṣarī-vidyā),
one should become constantly intent on effort and immerse oneself in the southern wealth.
A sacrifice with very meager sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā) may bring ruin to the patron (yajamāna);
this applies to sacrifices such as the Agnihotra, as well as rites such as recitation (japa) and oblation (homa).
One should always perform the Brahma-sacrifice and other rites even with a small sacrificial fee;
one is highly honored when accompanied by a fruitful fee, whereas [the rite] without a fee is fruitless.
In the absence of material wealth, how can there be dharma? And in the absence of dharma, how can there be happiness?
Therefore, one who delights in dharma should constantly strive to acquire it by means of forest-dwelling.
The father, the mother, the teacher, his wife, and he himself—
having performed even hundreds of tasks, yoga should be practiced day after day.
Having distributed barley even to Śūdras and others,
he honored his wife, sons, and so forth, who were to be supported on that day.
One should not act upon the words of women, for women are of dull intellect;
desiring his own welfare, a king should abide by the command of his preceptor, which is not subject to change.
Every year, having performed some form of *puraścaryā*,
the practitioner should give all his possessions as a sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), or at least an amount equal to his annual food expenses.
In the year of the worship of the glorious Eight-Syllabled Mantra, success arises;
and in that year, as well as in every subsequent year, there shall be a solar eclipse constantly.
In that case, the *puraścaraṇa* must certainly be performed with devotion;
having necessarily performed the *puraścaryā* there on a solar festival day. (14)
Or by giving even two gold coins (niṣkas), one may attain success;
when the aforementioned rare conjunctions (yogas) are attained, one is greatly honored.

In that regard, one is surely glorified after performing the preliminary rite (puraścaryā) along with its constituent parts; having abandoned stinginess regarding wealth, one should give a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) according to one's means.

Having performed the preparatory rite (puraścaryā) for mastery over the glorious eight-syllable mantra renowned for granting the great siddhis, one is glorified when the opportune moment (yoga) is attained. || 17 ||

Endowed with immediate success through the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) consisting of the Sogada [mantra], and joined with a portion of the Blessed One, he protects the world immediately by means of his roar. 18.

Those who have performed the worship of the glorious eight-syllabled mantra (aṣṭākṣarī-vidyā) along with its ancillaries and ritual fees, having observed the vow for nine nights, become illustrious. (19)
There is no doubt that he obtains the fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices, augmented by a sacrificial fee of gold numbering a thousand crores. || 20 ||
During the auspicious nine-night period of the Navarātra, by performing the rite of *puraścaraṇa*, one has undoubtedly attained the fruit of the horse-sacrifices (*aśvamedha*). || 21 ||
I shall now proclaim another vow that bestows the fruits of the four aims of life;
it is the essence of all the Vedas and is well-guarded even among the Shastras. (22)
In the month of Kārttika, Mārgaśīrṣa, Megha, or Phālguna, or likewise in Vaiśākha or Śrāvaṇa, on the first Friday; || 23 ||
O Lord of the Earth, having undertaken the vow, one should observe it for three years,
or twelve years, or until the end of the Brahmins' lives.
On every Monday, month after month, he is honored;
together with his companions, he recites the glorious eight-syllable mantra according to his ability.
Having consecrated the fire according to the rules, one who is firm in his vows should offer three hundred oblations of clarified butter with the glorious eight-syllable mantra.
One should also offer clarified butter one hundred and eight times with the Śrī-mantra,
and offer one oblation for each of the Bhagavad-raśmi-vidyās.
One should worship with three hundred flowers or else with bilva leaves; or alternatively, with *johvā* and *prāvāla*, using the *Śrī-Śrī-Brahmavidyā* mantra.
Or one should worship with one hundred and eight tulasī leaves; one must certainly feed her with various kinds of food and delicacies, just as a king honors his beloved queen.
On a Saturday, one certainly obtains either two pairs, or even a single pair,
or half a *niṣka* of gold.
Then one should offer excellent gold to the preceptor;
likewise, one should constantly give water to a descendant of Bhṛgu, as well as abundant wealth.
On the first day of the month of Bhārgava (Jyeṣṭha), every month, one should listen to the Śrāvaka; or else, every month on that same day, the wife of the teacher should be fed.
On a Saturday, a wise man should certainly offer gold coins, such as a *niṣka* or more, and he should also honor [the deity] with food offerings and the like.
The wise man should satisfy them with food and also give a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) to the couple;
he should sit facing the wife of the guru in the presence of Lakṣmī and Lakṣmīśa.

Having made a formal resolve (saṃkalpa) with reference to the preceptor’s wife, he should then offer the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) at the feet of the preceptor on the first day of the lunar fortnight or on a Friday.
O King, one may then give the intended wealth to one who has no son;
however, one should not act in this manner on the first Friday. (36)
During these five days as well, one should feed two pairs of lovers;
one should give a pair of cows according to one's capacity, along with a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
Desiring the supreme and very great accomplishment of the glorious eight-syllabled vidyā, one should certainly perform this vow; thus one attains success.
Or even if one is afflicted by impurity due to birth or death, or by other such troubles,
when a Saturday arrives, one should petition the all-pervading Guru.
The vow should be performed by the preceptor himself, or else by his son;
in that case, twice the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) must be given by the wise man.
Having performed this Bhṛguvāra-vrata, which is dear to Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa, one certainly attains great perfection; there is no doubt in this matter. (41)
One who is enraged by the observance of the Bhṛguvāra vow is indeed honored [by his enemies] even before a year has passed;
through the grace of the preceptor, he becomes filled with prosperity, wealth, grain, and other riches. (42)
Having attained immovability, one becomes endowed with pride, equal fortune, and excellence;
likewise, long life, great health, prosperity, and even the qualities of the sages are attained. (43)
There is no doubt in this matter: he shall not be separated from sons, grandsons, and the like, nor from his wife, children, kinsmen, tears, or wealth. (44)
One shall not be separated from one's beloved or kinsmen due to the observance of the Friday vow (bhṛguvāravrata), provided one desires great success and supreme, imperishable glory. || 45 ||
O Earth, this vow of Friday must be performed by those who have reached the end of their bodies; it should be observed by ten ancestors and ten descendants.
Accompanied by him, you shall undoubtedly go to the divine abode of the Blessed One, which is filled with celestial flowers and adorned with divine splendors. 47.
O you who have been afflicted by many diseases, the accomplishment of the glorious eight-syllabled mantra has been declared by me;
if there shall be success in the accomplishment of the glorious eight-syllabled vidyā, [then you shall be freed]. 48.
Even those born in the lineage of the venerable Vāmanas enter [into this state] when there is doubt regarding the Vedas concerning the secret of the unsurpassed Brahman-reality;
thus ends the thirtieth chapter in this work by the son of Daśaratha. 49.
[Thus ends the chapter on the Vedārthasaṃgraha in the glorious Anuttarabrahmatattvarahasya, the Tantra of Daśaratha.
The Blessed Lord said: One who has thus attained perfection through the glorious eight-syllable mantra is honored in this manner.
Thereafter, one should accomplish all rites performed for specific desires.
Mounted upon the son of Vinatā, possessing eight arms and endowed with splendor, he bore a bow,
shield, sword, mace, trident, discus, and quiver.
Having meditated upon Nārāyaṇa and having recited the eight-syllabled mantra a thousand times,
whatever poison there may be— whether stationary, mobile, or artificial— [is neutralized].
That body perishes immediately upon reaching [the deity],
provided one has fasted on that day when a solar eclipse occurs.
Beginning from the time of touching [the image] until the time of release,
he should reverently touch the various forms of the Brahmi alphabet while muttering the glorious eight-syllabled mantra.
O King, having drunk that, even one of dull intellect, or one who is deaf or mute,
shall become a master of all sciences within the space of a month.
Or, having observed the vow and chanted the mantra one hundred thousand times at a cow-pen on the seashore,
one should diligently offer ten thousand oblations with *palāśa* flowers.
Though appearing dull-witted, he was endowed with wisdom, a treasury of poetic talent,
a master of all four Vedas, and possessed of the power of speech.

For one who stands in the midst of a Tulasī grove and recites [the mantra] a hundred thousand times with restrained vows, there arises a mastery over the scriptures as if they were already heard from a teacher.
Having offered ten thousand oblations with dūrvā grass, one becomes free from all diseases,
attains long life, and may die at will.
On a Saturday, having properly touched an *aśvattha* tree with one's hand one thousand three hundred times, while maintaining all the ritual placements (*nyāsa*).
Having chanted the glorious eight-syllabled mantra, one does not die by any deaths;
having consecrated water twenty-five times daily with this mantra, one should drink it.
One shall be liberated even from terrible diseases by constantly and with devotion consecrating [the water] twenty-five times.
One who eats [on this day] obtains the recollection of past births and the vision of Brahmā; on the Vyatīpāta yoga occurring every month, one attains the splendor of the Lord of Lakṣmī.
Having recited the glorious eight-syllabled mantra one thousand three hundred times, accompanied by all the ritual placements (nyāsa), one should then recite the glorious mantra three hundred times.
Then, one should offer three hundred oblations with sesame seeds mixed with cow's ghee, or with pure ghee alone, while reciting the glorious eight-syllable mantra.
One should offer one hundred and eight oblations of clarified butter with the Śrī-mantra,
and then offer one oblation for each of the mantras of the Bhagavat-daśamīvidyās.
One should worship with one hundred and eight flowers using the *hastavidyā* mantra;
then, one should offer a *niṣka*, or half a *niṣka*, to one's own preceptor.
Having practiced the vow in this manner for one year,
even the great traveler who journeys through the sky is liberated from all diseases.
Having obtained wealth, grain, and unshakable prosperity,
she was the very embodiment of all sciences upon the earth and possessed a most beautiful form.
O son, at the end of the body, you will go to the abode of the Lord; of this there is no doubt.
Seated at the foot of a bilva tree, [you shall recite] the king of mantras of the Lord of Śrī.
Having recited [the mantra] one hundred thousand times and then performed ten thousand oblations with *alābu* leaves smeared with ghee, one shall attain the fortune of sovereignty.
Having recited the auspicious and glorious eight-syllabled mantra one hundred thousand times on a riverbank or in a cow-pen, [one should then offer oblations] with lotus leaves soaked in ghee.
Having offered a yūta-oblation, he becomes equal in splendor to the king of kings;
on the full moon day of Mārgaśīrṣa, being pure and with the permission of his teacher—24.
Having bathed in the morning, with a purified soul, and having completed his ritual duties, he [should recite] the glorious eight-syllabled mantra (Aṣṭākṣarī) together with all the nyāsas. || 25 ||
Having performed the recitation one thousand three hundred times while observing the vow,
one should then recite three hundred times the single Śrī-mantra prescribed for the horse and other [vehicles].
One should worship three hundred *sālagrāma* stones with flowers using the *Śrī-Śrīśa-Brahmavidyā* mantra; these stones are known as the city of Ayodhyā. (27)
Having installed the great discus of the Lord of the Universe,
which is difficult to comprehend, he manifested Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa together in both places as one.
Having honored him with the five services, one should worship him with the Brahma-vidyā;
and having performed the evening twilight devotion (sandhyā) when the moon is full, one should worship at sunset.
One should respectfully offer food made of cow's milk mixed with the three sweets into the fire for one hundred times,
using the glorious eight-syllable vidyā.
Then, one should offer ghee one hundred and eight times with the Śrī-mantra;
furthermore, one should offer it once each with the vidyās of the rays of the Lord.
Then, having offered the three objects of worship to the illustrious Lord of Lakṣmī, the bestower of wealth,
he offered a golden coin into the lotus-feet of the Preceptor.
Then, having run forth as if naked, the observer of the vow should subsist on milk;
he may eat sacrificial food (haviṣya), or fruit, or even [the remnants of] the two fires. 33.
Having fed them, one should offer the prescribed sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) and a water-pot;
thereafter, one should eat the desired food together with one's kinsmen.
Having thus observed this vow with devotion for even a single year,
one beholds the Blessed Lord together with Śrī with one's own eyes.
By the grace of the Lord of Men, he attains unshakable prosperity, abounding in wealth, grain, elephants, horses, and cattle, and filled with jewels. || 36 ||
Free from disease, long-lived, and resembling the sun in brilliance, he was a great poet endowed with sons, grandsons, great-grandsons, and further descendants. (37)
Endowed with twenty generations of his lineage, he shall obtain all enjoyments free from distress;
there is no doubt in this matter regarding the abode of the Blessed One.
The pure-souled person who performs this Paurṇamāsī vow with devotion for a full year transcends birth in the cycle of existence.
And [he attains] delight in the sovereign powers such as *aṇimā* and the rest, as well as the speed of thought, yoga together with its eight limbs, and even freedom from old age and death. (40)
O protector of the earth, one certainly attains [the fruit]; there is no doubt in this matter.
The meritorious Paurṇamāsī vow, when joined with a specific lunar mansion (nakṣatra) and day, is especially efficacious. || 41 ||
I shall explain in brief that which bestows immediate possession [of the deity],
occurring on the full moon day of Caitra when it is conjoined with the constellation Citrā and the lunar mansion Svāti.
The full moon day is to be known as great, for it shatters all obstacles;
having bathed there at dawn with a concentrated mind by the permission of the preceptor, [one should perform the rites]. (43)
Having gratified the ancestors with water mixed with black sesame seeds, he should then properly seat them upon their seats;
then, with the permission of the preceptor, he should offer there the sacrificial food (naivedya) together with all its accompaniments.
One should recite the glorious eight-syllabled mantra one thousand three hundred times; having recited it three hundred times, one should respectfully recite the glorious Manu-mantra as desired.
One who desires victory should worship the full moon within the blazing Jātavedas (the sacrificial fire) while reciting the threefold Atharvaṇa hymn dedicated to Śrī Hṛdaya.

Then, with devotion, one should offer oblations consisting of honey, the three products of the cow (gavya), and clarified butter, soaked in these, three hundred times while reciting the glorious eight-syllable mantra.
One should offer one hundred and eight oblations of clarified butter into the fire with the Śrī-mantra,
and likewise offer flowers with the twelve-syllable mantra of Śrī-Śrīśa.
Having worshipped the feet of the preceptor, one should then offer as a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) wealth amounting to three niṣkas, or two niṣkas, or even one niṣka.
On the auspicious full-moon day, one who subsists on milk or sacrificial food (vāhaviṣya) should feed three couples;
or alternatively, on the following day, one should feed two couples.
By performing it in this manner, the practitioner obtains the fruit of the preliminary rite (puraścaryā).
Having performed this very vow on the occasion of the sun’s transit (saṃkramaṇa), [he attains the same result]. 52.
One obtains the three fruits at Puraśvatthūya; of this there is no doubt.
Performing this very vow during an eclipse of the moon or sun, [one attains the same]. 52.
The practitioner attains the twelvefold fruit of the *puraścaryā* rite;
by means of this [method], he shall certainly become a possessor of *siddhi* in a single day. 53.
The full moon day of Vaiśākha, conjoined with a Monday and the Viśākhā nakṣatra,
is proclaimed as the great Vaiśākhī.
There, having paid homage to the teacher, having bathed elsewhere and being restrained in his vows,
and having performed his daily rites, he [should approach] the [goddess] conjoined with the nyāsa.
One should recite the glorious eight-syllabled mantra one thousand three hundred times;
thereafter, for three nights, one should diligently practice the desired glorious mantra.
Having worshipped the Brahmavidyā with three hundred flowers or leaves,
one should cast [the mantra] into the blazing fire while the moon is eclipsed.
With the venerable eight-syllabled mantra, he respectfully offers milk-porridge mixed with the three sweets,
and with the Śrī-mantra, he offers clarified butter as an oblation three hundred times.
Then, one should perform an oblation with the king of mantras using rays that have become single;
this should consist of forty palas of clarified butter, or twenty palas.
Having offered the salutation to Hari at the lotus-feet of the preceptor,
and having provided a comfortable bed along with a sacrificial fee according to one's capacity.
Having worshipped two fruits of the *panasa* tree that have been shaken from a heap of fruit,
one should give a sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) consisting of either one gold coin (*niṣka*).
Auspicious curd mixed with various kinds of foods, edibles, ghee, and honey should be served;
two pairs [of guests] should be fed, while others are treated as if they were nectar itself.
Then, together with his kinsmen, he should eat that food himself with devotion.
This is the auspicious twofold preliminary rite (puraścaryā) for the glorious Aṣṭāṅga-vidyā. 63.
He has accomplished it; of this there is no doubt. I speak the truth, the absolute truth:
he has done exactly so, in due order, accompanied by the six auspicious signs.
One obtains the imperishable fruit of the eightfold *puraścaryā* if one performs this [observance] there indeed on the day of the full moon during an eclipse. 65.
Having performed this very vow, one attains the great accomplishment of the glorious eight-syllable vidyā, which is difficult even for the gods to obtain. (66)
When the sun enters a new sign on an incomplete day, a gift should be given that is tenfold;
and when it coincides with a lunar festival (parvan), a gift should be given that is thirtyfold.
The full moon day in the month of Jyeṣṭha which is joined with a Saturday and the Jyeṣṭhā nakṣatra is the great Jyeṣṭha-pūrṇimā.
On a day endowed with the lunar phases (parvan),
having received the permission of the preceptor and having bathed at dawn, one whose intellect is purified should give the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) according to the qualities of the preceptor.
Having performed the necessary daily rites (āvaśyaka-karma) and being endowed with all the ritual placements (nyāsa),
one should recite the venerable Dṛṣṭākṣarī mantra one thousand three hundred times according to the prescribed method.
Then, having recited the desired mantra of Lakṣmī thirty thousand times, the practitioner [should proceed].
Then, at evening twilight, having approached the kindled fire,
one should recite three hundred times the glorious eight-syllable vidyā, saturated with the three sweets.
One should offer milk-rice (pāyasa) and ghee one hundred times with the *aty-aśrī* mantra;
one should offer clarified butter three times with the mantras of the rays of the Lord (*bhagavad-raśmi-vidyā*).
Thereafter, one should worship three hundred [deities] with the twelve-syllable mantra of Śrī Śrīśa,
and offer a niṣka of gold or wealth at the lotus feet of the preceptor.

Having also offered a bunch of grapes together with the fruit of the *phalavrata*, one should present it as an ornament for the venerable wife of the preceptor, with a mind focused on the Blessed One. (74)
O Lord of the Earth, on that very day, the wise should feed a couple with gold equal to a *niṣka*, or half a *niṣka*.
May he himself also enjoy the earth together with his kinsmen;
through this vow, the fruit of the three *puraścaryās* is produced. (76)
If there is a transit [of the sun] there on the full moon day, O Prajāpati, [then that is the occasion]. (78)
Having performed this special rite for the glorious *Aṣṭārṇa-vidyā*,
one should give a gift of three *niṣkas* to the lotus-feet of the preceptor.
One obtains the eternal fruit of twenty-four *puraścaryās*.
On the full moon day of the month of Āṣāḍha, it is conjoined with the deity Viśvedevas. (80)
That great [festival] occurring on a Sunday is proclaimed as the Mahatī;
having considered it superior even to Dvaipāyana, one should perform it with devotion. (81)
One must certainly perform there the vow that grants all perfections;
having bathed at dawn on the full moon day of Āṣāḍha, one of purified intellect— || 82 ||
Then, having performed the morning twilight devotion (saṃdhyā) and completed the daily fire-oblation (nityahoma),
she should also offer libations (tarpaṇa) while remaining endowed with all the ritual placements (nyāsa).
One should recite the glorious eight-syllabled mantra one thousand three hundred times;
one should recite the Lakṣmī mantra three hundred times, as it is most desired and excellent.
And having recited the Bhagavadraśmisūkta,
he should then perform the evening twilight ritual (sāyaṃsaṃdhyā), mixing [the water] with the three sweets.
One should offer milk-rice (pāyasa) three hundred times with the eight-syllable mantra of Śrī;
one should then offer clarified butter one hundred and eight times with the mantra of Śrī.
One should offer oblations into the fire with the *Nagavadraśmi* mantras;
one should worship [the deity] three hundred times with flowers and other offerings using the *Brahmavidyā*.
One observing the vow should subsist on milk or even on water;
then one should offer wealth three times to the pair of lotus-feet of the Guru.
On the following day, one should feed a pair of couples with various kinds of foods and edibles;
by doing so, one obtains the full fruit of the *puraścaryā* along with its ancillaries. || 89 ||
If one performs this vow with devotion after transferring [the merit] into the glorious eight-syllable Vidyā, the accomplishment of nectar is produced. (90)
One certainly attains the fruit arising from the triple circumambulation;
if there should be an eclipse of the moon during that time, it becomes as efficacious as the nectar of immortality.
By performing this very vow for five years, one attains that same eternal perfection which arises [from it]. (92)
When the full moon day arrives at Śrīvana, it is joined with the constellation Puṣya; it is said that Mūratī is conjoined with the constellation Īdavāsa. 93.
His merit is beginningless, bestowing inexhaustible bliss and happiness;
having bathed there according to the command of the Preceptor and performed his daily religious duties for the sake of dharma, [he attains this]. (94)
Seated on a seat, having performed the placement of ashes and the *mātṛkā* (syllabic) assignment,
one should mutter the glorious eight-syllabled mantra one thousand three hundred times.
One should recite the desired mantra three hundred times; thereafter, when the sacrificial fire has been kindled at the time of the evening twilight, one should proceed.
One should offer three hundred oblations of milk-rice mixed with the three sweets using the glorious eight-syllable mantra, and then offer auspicious clarified butter using the Lakṣmī mantra.
Having offered a single oblation of ghee with the Bhagavadraśmi-mantras,
one should worship with three hundred flowers or leaves using the Brahmavidyā and other mantras.
Having given even a single niṣka of wealth to the feet of the teacher, one will certainly obtain the fruit of the *puraścaryā* along with the removal of sins. 99.
O King, if the transit of the sun occurs there, one attains the fruit of *puraścaryā* performed alone; of this there is no doubt. (100)
If the drawing of the Soma juice occurs there, it is declared that [the fruit] is obtained by one who has fasted for three nights while worshipping the Moon-crested Lord. || 1 ||
In that regard, having first performed the preliminary rite (puraścaryā) as previously described,
one should then offer to the Guru a quantity of wealth equal to one year’s worth of food.
Having given a pure Śālagrāma stone, or one with three marks on its right side,
or else from the hand of the preceptor, it is the supreme [gift] accompanied by the *samāhati* mantra.
The pure-souled one attains success through the hundred-fold *puraścaraṇa* rites performed during the months of Āśvina,
Kārttika, and Mārgaśīrṣa, as well as those which are complete when performed in Bhādrapada.
When it is joined with a Monday, it is declared to be "Great" (mahatī). There, having completed the daily obligatory rites in the morning according to the teacher's instruction, [one should proceed].

Having performed the recitation of the glorious eight-syllabled mantra one thousand three hundred times, accompanied by all the ritual placements (nyāsa), one should then recite the glorious mantra three hundred times.
Then, at the evening twilight, he should offer with devotion an oblation of milk-rice (pāyasa) soaked in the three sweets, cow products, and clarified butter (ājya) into the consecrated fire.
One should offer three hundred oblations following the eight-syllable Śrī-mantra;
O King, one should then offer one hundred and eight oblations with the Śrī-mantra itself.
One should respectfully offer oblations with clarified butter for each of the rays;
one should worship with three hundred *tulasī* leaves by means of the *Brahmavidyā*.
Having offered at least one niṣka of gold and other gifts at the feet of the preceptor,
he should thereafter subsist on milk or fruits during that day.
Whoever, while observing the vow, should feed two couples,
he obtains the fruit of the preliminary practice (puraścaryā) and attains eternal perfection.
If there is a transit [of a planet] there, one obtains the fruit arising from the threefold preliminary practice (puraścaryā), provided that an eclipse of the moon occurs.
Having offered three *niṣkas* or two *niṣkas* at the feet of the preceptor,

one obtains the fruit arising from twenty-one preliminary rites (*puraścaryā*), as well as the fruit arising from three [additional] cycles of practice, provided that an eclipse of the moon occurs. (13)
If the full moon day in the month of Āśvina is conjoined with the Aśvinī asterism and joined with a Thursday, it is declared to be a most auspicious and great occasion.
Having performed the auspicious rites such as the recitation and fire-oblation (homa) of the venerable eight-syllabled mantra according to the prescribed method,
and having begun as before, one should give the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) to the preceptor.
By reciting it on the following day for two days, or by reciting it for three nights accompanied by a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā),
he attains the fruit of a threefold preliminary rite (puraścaryā) along with its ancillaries through the mantra.
Having performed this vow with devotion on the occasion of a solar transit (saṅkrānti), one shall obtain the complete fruit of five rounds of purificatory rites (puraścaryā). || 17 ||
If there should be an eclipse occurring at that time, one should perform auspicious rites such as recitation (japa) and fire-offerings (homa),
and then offer three niṣkas at the lotus-feet of the preceptor.
He then obtains the inexhaustible fruit of eleven *puraścaryās*.
On the full moon day of Kārtika, conjoined with the constellation Hasta, || 19 ||
The Kārttikī full-moon day conjoined with Monday is remembered as the most excellent;
having obtained permission from one's teacher, one should there complete the daily rites.

One should recite three hundred times the glorious eight-syllabled mantra, together with its own Śrī-mantra, which consists of one thousand three hundred [syllables] and is joined with all the nyāsas.

The most excellent practitioners, having beheld the glorious eight-faced one, should offer oblations of iron filings soaked in the three sweets (honey, ghee, and sugar) during the day alone, three hundred times with the mantra. (22)
Then, one should offer ghee one hundred and eight times with the Śrī-mantra;
each devotee of the Lord should likewise offer oblations of clarified butter with the Raśmi-mantras.
One who would worship the *dhātrī* tree with *dhātrī* fruits and the knowledge of Brahman should place a heap of *dhātrī* fruits in the presence of the preceptor.
Having given a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) to the feet of the Guru amounting to either one niṣka or two niṣkas, along with a citron fruit, || 25 ||
In that very place, one should feed five couples with the thought that they are the Blessed Lord;
then, having seen the full moon, one should offer the arghya three times to the God.
Having honored the teacher’s wife with garments and ornaments, perceiving her as Śrī,
one attains even the most exalted success through the procedure of the glorious eight-syllable mantra.
O King, one certainly attains that which is difficult even for the gods to obtain;
if the sun's transit (saṅkramaṇa) should occur there on the earth. || 28 ||
Having performed the recitation of mantras, fire oblations, and other rites with the venerable eight-syllabled vidyā,
one should give double the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) at the lotus-feet of the preceptor.
One shall obtain the fruit of twelve-fold *puraścaryā* along with the Āgamas;
during a lunar eclipse, one should perform this very vow with great devotion.
Having performed this and offered oblations to the preceptor and others, one shall obtain the fruit of sixty-four preliminary purificatory rites (puraścaryā) in a single day. || 31 ||
The full moon day of Mārgaśīrṣa,
conjoined with the constellation Jyeṣṭhā and the day of the week presided over by the Earth (Saturday), is proclaimed as Mahatī.
There, at the command of the teacher, having completed the daily rites in the morning,
[he performed] one thousand three hundred and fifty complete nyāsas.
Having recited the glorious eight-syllabled mantra over the consecrated fire,
[he should offer oblations] mixed with the three sweets, cow products, and clarified butter, along with sesame seeds and *vṛṣa*.
With the glorious eight-syllable mantra, one should offer three hundred oblations of ghee for the destruction of sins;
with the Śrī-mantra, the wise man should offer one hundred and eight oblations of ghee.
Then, with the rays of the Blessed One, one should divide the oblations of clarified butter into three parts;
[one should offer] food for the triad of couples consisting of eatables, soups, ghee, and so forth.
One should offer abundant wealth at the lotus feet of the preceptor;
even a commoner, O King, should give what can be afforded.
Or, having offered even a mere *niṣka* of gold to the preceptor’s wife,
one should then perform the evening *saṃdhyā* and recite the *Śrīhṛdayastava*.
He attains the fivefold, glorious, ultimate, and supreme perfection of the eight-syllable mantra,
which has been fully awakened through the eightfold preparatory rite (puraścaryā).
Even in that case, O Lord of the Earth, if there should be a transference [of the soul],
one should worship well with bilva leaves three hundred times with the Brahmavidyā mantra.
Having given double the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), one attains great siddhi; if there should be a lunar eclipse there, it becomes as sweet as nectar.
He is unobtainable by those born of the earth; thus he was reflected upon.
Having performed the fire-oblation with a sacrificial fee as prescribed in the *Candracūḍāmaṇi*, [he attained him]. || 42 ||
One who performs the *puraścaraṇa* rite during the movement of the Sun in the month of Puṣya, while reciting the *Aghora* mantra, certainly and inevitably obtains a hundredfold fruit. (43)
The great *vācaspatya* [samādhi] has been declared as prescribed;
having obtained the permission of the teacher and having completed the twilight devotions (*saṃdhyā*) here, [one should proceed]. (44)
Then, having completed the daily fire-oblation (nityahoma), one should recite the glorious eight-syllabled mantra one thousand three hundred times, accompanied by all the ritual placements (nyāsa).

Having respectfully recited the Śrīmanu mantra three hundred times, the preceptor, having consecrated the fire according to the rite in the presence of the virtuous, [performed the funeral rites] for the deceased horse. 46.
One should offer three hundred oblations into the fire with the glorious eight-syllable mantra, using sesame seeds and bilva leaves soaked in honey, ghee, and sugar.
Then, one should offer one hundred and eight oblations with the Śrī-mantra;
thereafter, one should perform three offerings of clarified butter (ājyāhuti) with the Bhagavad-raśmi-vidyās.
Thereafter, one should worship with three hundred blue lotuses while reciting the *Brahmatīdyā* mantra;
or else, one should offer two pieces of gold at the feet of the preceptor.
O Lord of the Earth, if the sun’s transit occurs there,
this yoga is declared to be unattainable by name, known as Cūḍāmaṇi.
Having offered five hundred oblations of ghee and milk-rice into the fire,
and having placed three niṣkas as a sacrificial fee at the lotus-feet of the preceptor, he performed the rite.
O King, one shall obtain the fruit of twenty-four *puraścaryās* along with the ancillary rites,
even if a meritorious lunar eclipse (*mṛgāṅka-grahaṇa*) should occur.
One should especially perform the auspicious recitation, fire-oblation, and other rites of the glorious eight-syllable mantra within the pure maṇḍala.
Or, having placed a beautiful Śālagrāma stone accompanied by two earrings as a fee of three niṣkas at the feet of the preceptor, [he should offer it]. (54)
One is honored with the complete fruit of sixty-four preliminary rites (puraścaryā), along with its ancillaries;
there is no doubt that one attains the supreme perfection (siddhi) here in this very life. || 55 ||
Twelve pairs, or three couples, should be fed;
the full moon day of the month of Māgha is conjoined with the lunar mansion of the ancestors (Maghā).
The Mahatī is proclaimed as being attached to the Indra-vāsara;
even here, having obtained the permission of the Guru, one must perform the necessary rite.
Having performed the entire placement (nyāsa) consisting of one thousand three hundred [syllables],
one should offer the oblation into the glorious fire with the venerable eight-syllabled mantra one hundred and thirty times.
Thereafter, one should offer clarified butter one hundred and eight times with the Śrī-mantra;
then, three couples should be fed with various foods, drinks, and other delicacies.
Then, having performed the evening twilight devotions (saṃdhyā) and having offered the threefold arghya water to the Sun,
one should subsequently worship him with three hundred blue lotuses while reciting the Vahni-vidyā.
Having given gold equal to one's weight at the lotus-feet of the preceptor,
one obtains here the eternal fruit of the *puraścaryā* along with all its ancillaries.
If one performs this vow here upon the occurrence of a solar transit (saṃkrānti),
the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) should be threefold; by placing it at the lotus-feet of the preceptor,
one obtains the supreme fruit of six purascarana rites, provided that the recitation is performed there in the presence of the Lord of Nectar (the Moon).
This [practice], which is obtainable even from a yogi named Caṇḍacūḍāmaṇi, is now respectfully stated according to the daily recitation taught in the Nayacandracūḍāmaṇi. 64.
In this matter as well, one who desires great accomplishment must certainly perform it;
he attains the fruit of sixty-four *puraścaryās* along with its entirety. (65)
That full moon day of the month of Phālguna which is conjoined with the asterism Bhaga-dvaivata (Punarvasu) and joined with Sunday is declared to be "Mahā" (Great).

O Lord of the Earth, having bathed here with the permission of the preceptor and having completed the recitation [of the mantra], one should perform the two rites of *japa* and *homa*, just as in the month of Māgha.
The fruit of *puraścaryā* performed for a mortal is as described; that same fruit is indicated here as well, O Lord, there is no doubt about this. (68)
Having performed this as described with one full left hand full of earth, he becomes one who has attained the vidyās. || 69 ||

In that regard, the full moon day (paurṇamāsī) occurring in each respective month, which is not accompanied by the Kṣaya [of a lunar day] and is endowed with the Brahmā-rasa, is proclaimed as "Mahatī" (the Great).
Desiring the unsurpassed perfection of the glorious eight-syllable vidyā,
one should perform the vow with devotion on a single full-moon day.
The practitioner shall become endowed with a portion of the Blessed One;
whatever auspicious acts—such as recitation, fire-offerings, and so forth—are performed with all their constituent parts, they [become effective] in those [places].
Whatever has been spoken by me, having performed it with devotion and all its constituent parts,
no knowledge fails to attain success, nor does one's desired goal remain unaccomplished.
Among thousands of various paths, it repeatedly casts one into the hells and other miserable states, mingled with the results of past births and actions. (74)
If one desires to attain mastery over the glorious eight-syllable vidyā, one should remain intent upon it;
for through the attainment of the glorious eight-syllable mantra, one shall become like a vessel of nectar.
Endowed with a portion of the Blessed One's power, he may attain death at his own will;
even when an unattainable yoga has been reached, he may beg from Śūdras as well.
Having given the teacher's fee (dakṣiṇā), one should perform the recitation (japa), fire-oblation (homa), and other rites;
it should be given immediately, for by giving it, one is honored in heaven.
One who desires the accomplishment of knowledge should not beg for a debt,
nor should one ask for even a mouthful of food from the family of a teacher.
Even if it must be acquired through great effort, wealth equal to the weight of one's father and mother in gold should be given to the preceptor.
One who desires supreme accomplishment must immediately offer the substance intended by the mind at the lotus feet of the preceptor. (80)
One who desires success and has conquered the senses should not practice deceit;
for that supreme ornament which is adorned with a pair of earrings [is not for the deceitful]. 81.
Having bestowed [this] upon the ears of the teacher during the yoga of the manifestation of glory,
one attains immediate success and does not depart from heaven even after seeing the lords of the gods.
When struck with the *uttamā* [mudrā], it immediately grants all success; when struck with the *dakṣiṇā*, it is said to bestow half-success merely by the measure of a month. (83)
If given within two months, she bestows the success of dharma;
if given after three months, there is no doubt that she grants only a mere fraction of the result. (84)
By whatever means possible, circumambulating the lotus feet of the Guru in their presence yields fruit immediately, or at least within a month. 85.
This [mantra], complete with the syllable *Imāram* and intended for the noble one, is highly honored;
it is known as the glorious *Aṣṭākṣarī*, which bestows fruits when practiced. 86.
In this compendium of the Vedas concerning the secret of the supreme reality of Brahman, this thirty-first chapter has been declared, which bestows the desired fruit. (87)
[Thus ends the thirty-first chapter in the glorious *Anuttarabrahmatattvarahasya*, the *Dāśarathītantra*, which is a compendium of the meaning of the Vedas.]
The venerable Śrī Ṛṣyaśṛṅga said: Having spoken thus much, the all-pervading Lord Rāma, son of Daśaratha,
spoke again to Kuśa in the presence of the celestial sages.
The Blessed Lord said:
Listen, O Śaṅkara, Lord of Gaurī, to the further sādhana of the eight syllables,
by hearing which even a dull-witted man attains this most exalted perfection of the mind.
The great preliminary rite (puraścaraṇa) for the glorious eight-syllable vidyā is declared to be sixteen hundred thousand recitations, which is the cause of immediate accomplishment.
Because they were constantly accumulated through the Dharma and because their lifespans were exceedingly long,
success was achieved simply by that preliminary practice (puraścaraṇa) during the Kṛta Yuga and other ages.
In this terrible Kali age, due to the absence of stability and other virtues of the mind, and because of the abundance of the creepers of diseases and defects, it is likewise so. (5)
On this very day, success should not be sought by the wise; for as long as the illustrious eight-syllable vidyā has not been mastered on this earth, [no success shall be attained].
Even by performing ten million recitations and other rites of the glorious eight-syllable mantra,
not even a fraction of the merit of serving the Lord of Lakṣmī arises.
Therefore, one must perform the *puraścaraṇa* with devotion;
by performing the *puraścaraṇa* rite, one certainly attains success.
Likewise, during the conjunction of Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa, at the time of the lunar eclipse, during the Navarātra vow, and through the performance of the puraścaraṇa rite; || 9 ||
Success is inevitably attained through this king of mantras which bestows accomplishment,
when the nine-night vow has been undertaken, as well as during an eclipse of the sun or moon.
One should never perform the Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa yoga, nor the Vaṃdhya yoga, nor the Mahāpuṣkara yoga, nor even the Trayoga, nor the Ardhodaya yoga. (11)
The supreme seed-syllable of Siddhikāmodā should perform nine midday oblations;
that which was previously mentioned as the purificatory rite (*puraścaraṇa*) consists of sixteen hundred thousand [recitations].

Having thus performed this [practice] when yoga is unattainable, one should become exactly like that; for in all cases where yoga is unattainable, the preliminary service (puraścaryā) is prescribed as follows.
I have performed the preliminary rite (puraścaraṇa) by reciting [the mantra] one hundred and sixty thousand times;
on the third lunar day of the waning moon, the merit is ten times greater than that. || 14 ||
Success is inevitably attained through the grace of the preceptor, even by performing the ablution and other rites for a single day that is never-ending. (15)
By offering three apīnīska fruits, one shall immediately attain success;
what need is there to mention when this is combined with a yoga occurring on the new-moon day of the month of Vaiśākha? (16)
The preliminary rite (puraścaryā) for the eight-syllable mantra of Hari, which is difficult even for the gods to accomplish, was indeed spoken on the first day of the month of Vaiśākha. || 17 ||
The threefold accomplishment is now described:
by means of recitation, fire-offerings, and so forth, it is performed daily by the preceptor for the sake of the distressed. (18)
May she, whose well-performed merit bestows the fruits of the four aims of life, and who [attains] even more of these sciences through the instruction of her preceptor, [be victorious]. 19.
Accompanied by his ascetic power, he enters the body of his own disciple;
when the disciple's eyes have become clear, he imparts the sacred knowledge into his ears.
Half of the merit derived from recitation, fire-offerings, and other rites goes to him;
one should therefore bestow the most excellent sacrificial fee upon the lotus-feet of the preceptor.
He accepted a hundred years' worth of wealth as the highest sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā); it is ordained that with a middling fee, the result is indeed middling.
By giving an inferior sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), one may obtain only slight success;
therefore, [one should place] the two auspicious feet of the teacher [upon one's head]. 24.
By whatever means possible, one should respectfully acquire wealth and,
having given the highest sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), [receive it] from the lotus-like mouth of the teacher.
Having acquired all branches of knowledge along with their respective essences, they did not immediately attain any great mastery over those very sciences.
On the final day of the month, when the teacher has bestowed [the mantra] upon the disciples, one attains the supreme perfection of the glorious eight-syllable vidyā and other siddhis.
Out of complete grace, the network of vidyās that bestows fruit should be given to one who gives away all his possessions or even his very life with effort.
The knowledge should be received from the preceptor on the final day of the month of Vaiśākha,
because through the austerity of the teacher, the disciple attains perfection.
If a true disciple should offer even his own life,
from that moment on, he remains a true disciple at the lotus feet of the teacher.
One may give away one's body, wealth, and even one's sons and daughters during planetary conjunctions such as the eclipses; such success is declared to be the attainment of success itself.
On the third [lunar day] known as Akṣayā, vision is attained according to the method taught in Siddhipura;
likewise, through the fire-oblation (homa), great accomplishment (mahāsiddhi) is achieved on the day of the exhaustion of the essence of the sacrificial altar.
Then, having given the desired fee to the teacher, and thereafter having offered pairs [of items] and given a sacrificial fee to those who have been worshipped; || 33 ||
The auspicious eight-syllable mantra, joined with the ritual placement (nyāsa), should be recited one thousand three hundred times, or one hundred and eight times. (34)
The Śrī-mantra or one's own chosen mantra should be recited exactly one hundred times;
likewise, the six-syllabled Vaiṣṇavī Mahāvidyā of Vāsudeva. (35)
Thereafter, one who desires success should perform the recitation one hundred and eight times;
he should eat only fruits and cold water, observing the vow and subsisting on sacrificial food (viṣya).
One should recite the *hṛdaya*, the *stotra*, and the *tantra* during the night;
thereafter, one should partake of the Guru’s grace (*prasāda*). On the following day, Gīrī becomes manifest.
In the temple of the preceptor or in one's own home,
the moon-adorer (the practitioner) [should perform the rites] after the preliminary practices (puraścaraṇa) have been completed.
A disciple should everywhere eat the food left over by the guru with reverence;
by this, there is the destruction of all sins and the attainment of supreme perfection. (39)
It is known, there is no doubt in this; you are Satya, as declared by both of us.
Penance is obtained from the mouth of the Guru by disciples who are the foremost among practitioners.
When the yoga of the unattainable has been attained, the net of vidyās that bestows fruit should be gathered once more, after having given the supreme dakṣiṇā.
When the time for initiation has arrived, even if one's life-breaths have reached the throat,
the net of knowledge must not be given by an unwise person who would destroy the ascetic merit of another.

This [teaching], which should be given only at the request of many, is to be obtained through yoga and brings forth glory—[it is] studied by one who possesses firm devotion to the lotus feet of the Guru at all times. (43)
Immediately thereafter, one should devoutly meditate upon the glorious eight-syllabled mantra (Śrīmad-aṣṭākṣarī-vidyā);
by reciting it one hundred and eight times, one shall obtain the fruit of the rite.
Now I shall describe the procedure for the fire-oblation (homa), which grants all accomplishments instantly;
it was taught by Nārāyaṇa to his high-souled father.
Having worshipped the Śāligrāma stone discus and the discus of Ayodhyā with the twelve-syllable mantra, one should then recite the eight-syllable mantra.
One should offer one hundred thousand oblations of cow-derived clarified butter, ten thousand at a time;
one attains mastery over the powers such as atomization (aṇimā) and the rest—of this there is no doubt.
Having recited [the mantra] one hundred thousand times while remaining pure, and having offered ten thousand oblations of oranges mixed with ghee, one obtains long life and abundant food.
Having consumed it together with rose-apple (jambīra) mixed with ghee and the three sweets (trimadhu), one who was previously unfortunate shall become fortunate and like unto Kāma. || 49 ||
Having struck [the image] with coconuts mixed with ghee and the three sweets (trimadhu),
one who is united with a portion of the Lord becomes radiant like the sun.

Having offered ten thousand fruits of the date-palm soaked in honey and ghee, even one who is dull-witted will become equal to Vācaspati, the lord of speech, through the fear of [the goddess] Parvatī. 51.
Endowed with large, very sweet, and *catakūla* fruits mixed with honey, and joined with a portion of the Blessed One, he becomes radiant like the sun. (52)
There was no doubt that he would rule the earth, for he was free from disease, having become tall through the fruits of barley which were drenched in honey. (54)
Having offered oblations of bilva fruits mixed with cow's ghee and the three sweets (trimadhu), one obtains an inexhaustible flood of wealth and jewels; of this there is no doubt. (55)
There is no doubt that you will become a lord equal to the king of kings;
having offered with devotion milk-rice mixed with ghee and the three sweets, you shall attain this.
The King of Kings becomes terrifying through the ignorance of the Goddess of Fortune;
however, by offering plantain fruits mixed with ghee, honey, and milk, he is pacified. || 57 ||
One obtains ten thousand sons endowed with a portion of your own power.
Having offered oblations with Tulasī leaves and beautiful blue lotuses, he purified himself. || 58 ||
One who does not gamble attains a splendor equal to that of the King of the Gods;
[one who offers] grapes mixed with cow's ghee, honey, and curd attains that same splendor. (59)
Having offered ten million oblations with pieces of sugarcane smeared with ghee and mixed with the three sweets (honey, sugar, and ghee), one certainly attains the state known as Nidhana. || 60 ||
Having offered a million oblations, he beholds with his own eyes the Lord of Śrī;
[he does so] with auspicious fruits produced from milk-trees, measured by sixty.
Having offered ten thousand oblations mixed with cow’s ghee and honey,
and having attained the eightfold yoga, one certainly becomes a sky-walker.
One should offer oblations in the fire with lotuses soaked in cow's ghee and saturated with the three sweets;
one attains the desired mind, of this there is no doubt.
Having offered ten thousand *caṃpaka* flowers fumigated with cow’s ghee, honey, and sesame seeds,
one becomes like the Lord of Wealth (Kubera) in speech and power.
Having offered Madanikā flowers mixed with cow’s ghee, honey, and sugar, one who performs ten thousand oblations will certainly attain a golden body. (65)
By offering ten thousand oblations of *jānī* flowers smeared with honey and anointed with cow’s ghee,
the practitioner becomes known as one possessing the splendor of the sun.
Then, with Karavīra, Dhūnaka, ghee, honey, and curd mixed together, he sprinkled [the image] twice; thereafter, it became like gold in its splendor.
Whether stationary or moving,
one certainly destroys poison by offering oblations of guggulu mixed with clarified butter, honey, and wine, while reciting the Śucī hymns.

Furthermore, one who desires the attainment of all auspicious fortune should offer ten thousand oblations of sugar-cane pieces mixed with cow's ghee and the three sweets (honey, sugar, and ghee). || 69 ||
Having offered oblations in all the worlds,
one attains supreme well-being by respectfully reciting the glorious eight-syllabled Vidyā one hundred thousand times.
One is liberated even from incurable diseases and sins; there is no doubt about this.
He who recites two hundred thousand times the glorious eight-syllabled mantra— || 71 ||
By reciting [the mantra] four hundred thousand times, one obtains the eternal fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices, as well as great and imperishable prosperity.
Having recited the glorious eight-syllabled mantra six hundred thousand times while controlling the senses, one attains all auspicious fortune from the Lord of Creatures (Brahmā).

Having recited the glorious eight-syllable mantra twelve hundred thousand times, one will certainly become the leader of the supernatural powers such as atomization (aṇimā) and the unseen (adṛṣṭa). 74.
Resembling the brilliance of refined gold or the hue of a blue jay, it certainly bestows the fortune of sovereignty;
of this there is no doubt. (75)
By reciting the glorious eight-syllable mantra one hundred and sixty thousand times,
one certainly becomes the master even of treasures such as the conch and others.
Through twenty-one fearful signs, Svāyaṃbhuva Manu himself directly bestowed upon him his own form, granting him a lifespan of one kalpa that was unshakable.
It bestows the sovereign power of the qualities such as atomization (aṇimā) and so forth; of this there is no doubt.
[One should recite] twenty-five hundred thousand times this glorious eight-syllabled mantra of mine.
Having been proclaimed throughout all worlds and worshipped even by Śakra and others, having attained divine vision, he becomes one who can assume any form at will. (79)
By reciting it thirty-two hundred thousand times, one becomes a master of the Siddhas. || 81 ||
By reciting the mantra two million three hundred and twenty thousand times, one becomes the lord of the Gandharvas;
by reciting it two million six hundred thousand times, one becomes a possessor of great vidyā.
By forty lakhs [of recitations], he becomes heroic in form;
by fifty lakhs of recitations, he becomes unconquerable by the Siddhas. (81)
He was self-controlled, radiant with splendor, and accompanied by celestial maidens. || 82 ||
Having recited twelve lakhs [of the mantra], one of great and supreme intelligence, having become free from old age and death, certainly attains divinity. || 83 ||
By reciting [this] eighty times, one becomes equal to Brahmā, free from old age and death, and partakes in the sovereignty of creation as his food. || 84 ||
Having recited it ninety lakhs of times, one who is praised by Bhīma shall become free from old age and death and attain the world of truth (Satyaloka). || 85 ||
Then, with devotion, he recited the glorious eight-syllable mantra one million times;
consequently, Dakṣiṇāmūrti, whose body was radiant, became free from the fear of his enemies.
He is free from old age and death, possessing a lifespan of five hundred years;
likewise, he attains the sovereignty of the powers such as atomization (aṇimā) and the eightfold group beginning with the sandals (pādukā). (87)
One who is firm in their vows shall attain omniscience, charm, and the power to assume any form at will by performing one hundred and eight lakh recitations.
He is free from old age and death through the glorious eight-syllable mantra; his lotus feet are worthy of worship even by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa. (89)
Having become Mārāyaṇa in person, he attained even the power of moving through the sky,
as well as the eightfold yoga, omniscience, and mental agility.
Having obtained the power consisting of the ability to enter the bodies of others and so forth, which is unshakable,
he was accompanied by a thousand maidens.
By this very path, one ascends to honor;
having become the foremost among servants, he becomes great before the Blessed One. 92.
O King, in the presence of the supreme abode of wisdom, the other gods rejoice; there is no mantra equal to the eight-syllabled one, and there is no deity equal to Nārāyaṇa. (93)

In the month of Vaiśākha, on the day called Kṣaya, when the sun rises as it enters the zodiac sign of Aries, a Brahmin attains such success through recitation, fire-offerings, and libations performed under that specific conjunction as he does not attain elsewhere. 94.

He who is intent on the worship of the feet of the Teacher, who performs the ritual dismissal (vinyāsa) along with the recitation of the eight-syllable mantra—he alone is Nārāyaṇa, the bearer of the two [feet], the venerable, the worthy of worship, and the most exalted Guru. || 95 ||
A person should not let even a single day pass fruitlessly without having entered the ocean of the waters that are the pair of the Teacher’s feet. 97.
By all means, the fruit alone is that which must be accomplished; for the Lord of Creatures bestows the fruit through the mantra of eight syllables.
One who recites this mantra along with its ritual placements (nyāsa) attains Nārāyaṇa himself through the very dust of his feet.

Thus, in former times, the high-souled Daśarathi, that great chariot-warrior, related this secret which was spoken by the Blessed One Nārāyaṇa to the leader of the immortals, and which was told to the king as the most supreme and pure. 99.
Thus ends the thirty-second chapter in this *Daśarathīya-tantra*, a compendium of the meaning of the Vedas, which contains the essence of the Upanishads. 100.
[Thus ends the thirty-second chapter in the Śrīmadanuttarabrahmatattvarahasya, the Dāśarathīyatantra, which is a compendium of the meaning of the Vedas.]
The Blessed Lord said: Listen, O King, descendant of the protector of the earth, how in ancient times he beheld a great tortoise of divine luster in the ocean.

"O you who do not take refuge in this [world], O you who are unconquerable, O purifiers of the three worlds!
You are blessed," thus was the sage Nārada addressed by the Waters.
The waters are the source of forest produce and grain; the broad earth is the source of wealth and our refuge.
Nārada said to her, "O Vasundharā, you are indeed blessed. (4)
O high-minded one, I did not give birth to this Brahmin sage who was struck by wealth; rather, it was the blessed Gāyatrī, the support of all, who brought him forth.
Thus addressed, the mountain said, "You are most blessed.
The gods and the mountain replied, "We are indeed blessed."
O sages, another god, the Grandfather (Pitāmaha), who is the creator of the universe and the source of great laughter,
approached Brahmā and said to him, "You are blessed."
The Lord said, "I am fortunate that you have drunk [this] great yellow [elixir].
Thus, all the worlds are created by the eternal one through his dancing.
"O Sage, those other Vedas are being protected and withdrawn by you.
Thus addressed, Nārada prostrated himself like a staff before the Vedas.
"Blessed are you, whose intellect perceives the creation, sustenance, and dissolution of the universe of the Omniscient One;
and the Vedas also declare that we nine are blessed, having attained Nārada. (10)
"Indeed, we were born for the purpose of carrying the Lord at the sacrifice;
you, however, are more fortunate than the sacrifice," so said Nara to them.
They said: "O fortunate ones, we have been constantly worshipping here the Blessed One, the God of gods himself, the Lord of Śrī."

He is the essence of sacrifice, the Person of Sacrifice, the Lord of the two bay horses, Nārāyaṇa, the all-pervading one; he is the Master consisting of all knowledge, the Lord of the three worlds, and the Sovereign.
He alone is our blessed Supreme Self, the eternal;
having gone into the presence of the Grandfather (Brahmā), that Supreme Self was praised by him.
Then Nārada, the soul of the universe, said to the Lord of Śrī, who was thus performing his duty: "O fortunate one, you have indeed accomplished what was to be done; come now with Dakṣiṇāmūrti."
Having heard those words of the Blessed One, Nārada, the son of Brahmā, said:
"O Blessed One, how may I become blessed by means of this discourse on the desire for sacrificial fees? (16)
Thus addressed there, the Blessed One spoke to Nārada, the joy of the Brahmins,
who was the very embodiment of Lakṣmī’s proximity, seated in the presence of the Goddess.
"O Dakṣiṇāsīha, whatever word was spoken by me, these Vedas shall declare;
it is certain that they have emerged from my mouth. (18)
Having spoken thus, the all-pervading Lord, together with Ramā,
arrived while riding upon the serpent-vehicle and said, "Eat."
The Vedas said, "Brahmā has also spoken; he has spoken that truth. He spoke it clearly. || 20 ||
Having composed your mind, listen, O son of Brahmā;
we have been created by the Blessed One, O sage, for the sake of the welfare of the world. (21)
"Whatever we say, all that must necessarily be accepted by you twice-born ones; do not be dejected, for our command is most powerful. (22)
He who disregards our command and desires to dwell upon the surface of the earth will inevitably sink into the most terrible hells until the moon and stars cease to exist.

The Sādādevī [scriptures] should be studied along with the six ancillaries (ṣaḍaṅga) in both the pada and krama recitations; they should also be performed as complete sacrifices, free from all defects and devoid of obstacles. || 24 ||
I believe that daily obligatory rites, occasional rites, and rites performed for specific desires must always be performed accompanied by sacrificial fees.
One should always practice the *vihī* posture and avoid the *niṣīddha* posture;
this is the supreme word spoken by the Supreme Self regarding those who desire the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*). 26.
Every rite devoid of *dakṣiṇā* is fruitless; likewise, a sacrifice performed with very little *dakṣiṇā*, or even one entirely lacking *dakṣiṇā*, is in vain. (27)
