furthermore, he who makes a gift of a horse to a twice-born śrotriya [attains this same reward].
Having reached the world of Savitṛ, a man who has given an elephant as a gift to one who knows the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences shall enjoy divine pleasures until the end of the kalpa.
He who gives a palanquin equipped with all necessary furnishings shall ascend half of Indra’s throne, endowed with every enjoyment.
He who gives a milch cow with her calf to a twice-born man ascends an excellent celestial chariot and goes to the world of truth (Satyaloka).
Having given a two-faced cow along with its limbs and accompanied by a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), one attains the world of Śiva, accompanied by a hundred divine maidens. || 12 ||
On this very day, one is liberated from great sins, minor sins, and the like;
mounted upon an excellent celestial chariot, one is praised by siddhas, gods, and sages.
Honored by a thousand celestial maidens, he shall dwell in the world of Brahmā;
O observer of noble vows, he performs the great gifts, foremost of which is the Tulāpuruṣa.
Having established [it] in the divine state of Brahman, he is worshipped by all the deities;
[he who gives] land the size of a *gocarma*, even if it is filled with bitter crops. || 15 ||
He who gives for the sake of the twice-born is liberated from all great and minor sins, and he enjoys all pleasures that are difficult even for Indra to attain. || 16 ||
Accompanied by Kubja and endowed with valor, he ascended the celestial Puṣpaka chariot, praised by the gods who performed auspicious rites and attended by hundreds of divine maidens. || 17 ||
Having offered [the oblation], he goes to the supreme abode from which he does not return;
O twice-born ones, the brahmins are worthy of honor by all castes and are the most excellent on the surface of the earth. 18.
Among them, those learned in the Vedas are the best; even among them, the men of realized knowledge are superior;
and even more superior than the men of realized knowledge are said to be those who perform sacrifices with abundant sacrificial fees.

O King, those who know the Brahman are superior even to performers of sacrifice; they are worthy of worship and are highly honored. One should offer some small gift on a single day to one who knows the Brahman.
O beloved, he who bestows inexhaustible wealth upon thousands of Brahmās and Viṣṇūs grants that which bestows great happiness for ten thousand kalpas.
Having rescued King Mahī from the ocean of hell, he restored him along with his ornaments, jewels, and his entire lineage.
He gave with great respect the wealth required for the marriage even to a poor brahmin, [bestowing upon him] that supreme abode of Viṣṇu, which is endowed with eternal bliss.
Having given [this], one obtains the fruit previously described; there is no doubt in this matter.
Having married a hundred Brahmins and having given them very abundant wealth, || 67 ||
Having given away abundant wealth and even his very life, he will certainly go to the abode of Viṣṇu, of this there is no doubt;
[this is true] for those who daily give to hundreds of thousands of knowers of Brahman. 68.
Having offered a hundred thousand pieces of gold and a collection of pearls and other gems, and having married a thousand poor people with heaps of wealth; (69)
Even by offering gold coins at the lotus feet of the preceptor,
one obtains a fruit even greater than that and becomes a servant of the Blessed One.
O King, he by whom the twelve-syllable Śrī-Śrī-thati mantra is bestowed is called a true Ācārya by those who know the highest truth of all principles. || 71 ||
O illustrious one, he by whom the fifteen-syllable mantra of Śrī, endowed with a garland of rays, has been bestowed is even more excellent than the [other] teacher. (72)
To those to whom the auspicious and glorious eight-syllabled mantra, accompanied by the rays of the Blessed One, is given out of grace, they become manifestly one with the Blessed One. (73)
The Great Ācārya, the Lord, is said to be even greater than those two;
he alone is directly Brahmā, he alone is the infallible Lord.
Know him to be Nārāyaṇa; do not entertain any doubt in this matter.
[I am] the auspicious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇī, the mantra of the sovereign of the queens of kings. (75)
The wise say that he who bestows this [mantra], which is hidden in all the Vedas and celebrated in all the scriptures, is a true Ācārya. || 76 ||
This very one is the creator of the world—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara;
he is the omniscient one, the bearer of light, the sun, the giver of cows, gold, and liberation.
O King, know that whatever gold or even a *cihluka* measure of it is given to the teachers, it brings a thousandfold reward, and indeed more than that. (78)
Know that the preceptor alone is the most excellent of vessels and the most excellent of sacred fords; he is the very form of the Blessed One, visible to the eye. (79)
Whether it be a thousand golden Mount Merus or a hundred offerings on a scale, by the gift of even a single *niṣka* to the lotus-feet of one's own preceptor [one attains such merit]. (80)
The ancient sages who knew Brahman have declared that disparaging others, ingratitude, and piercing the vital secrets of others are not equal [to other sins]. (81)
Harshness, cruelty, consorting with the wives of others, the desire to seize the property of others, and the reviling of the deities; || 82 ||
Deceiving men through deceit, performing deficient ritual acts, killing, listening to the censure of one's teacher, and likewise transgressing his command; || 83 ||
O King, constant lack of faith in the Vedas, the Purāṇas, and the treatises on Dharma is a sign of those destined for hell— even if only one of these traits is present.
One should know that for those liberated from hell, there are no [further] marks;
their true being resides in the cries of compassion, which is the remedy for the next world.
Speech that is truthful, real, and beneficial; the perception of the authority of the Vedas; the worship of gurus, gods, sages, and perfected beings; and association with the virtuous. || 86 ||
Even a wise Buddha honors hospitality, the practice of non-violence, and a mind of loving-kindness,
as well as other divine, virtuous actions, and whatever beings exist.
These are the signs of men who have fallen from heaven and are not destined for it;
this has been told by me to you, O King, as you requested.
Now you have seen all that place where those who enjoy the fruits of their own actions—both the meritorious and the sinful—are burned; it is like this. 89.
"Indeed, you have seen hell; therefore, go elsewhere.
Then, placing him in front, the good king prepared to depart.
Then, a cry was uttered by all the men:
"O Lord of Gods, show us favor! Stay for just a moment! (91)
Struck by the deep and heart-stealing sound resonating from your limbs,
the Piśācas fled in all directions from your five limbs, utterly destroyed.
"O tiger among men, O high-minded one, perform this act of compassion.
Having heard these words of theirs, O King, he went toward that man.
He asked: "How is it that even joy remains for them? What great meritorious deed have I performed in Satyaloka? (94)
"Proclaim that which bestows nourishment and joy upon him.
Yāmya said:
Then, with the remaining food, one should satisfy the ancestors, the gods, guests, and servants. || 95 ||
Since nourishment has been attained and that which was offered was directed by the mind,
the wind, through contact with your limbs, bestows delight.
O King, the torments [of hell] do not afflict one who has committed evil deeds, because you have performed sacrifices such as the Aśvamedha according to the prescribed rules. (97)
O King, by the grace of the true guru, you have constantly worshipped the glorious eight-syllabled mantra together with the rays of the Lord.
She is the supreme Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇī, the sovereign of the queens of kings, who embodies the condensed essence of all the Vedas and Vedāntas. 99.
O Teacher, having obtained your grace through your worship day after day,
you have daily enjoyed the wife, sons, and other belongings of the teacher, as well as whatever remained.
Was it out of devotion that you ate from the feet of the Teacher, or did you request all your possessions, such as jewels, pearls, gold, and the like? (101)
Therefore, for those who perceive reality, the instruments, weapons, fire, and so forth, as well as the causes of great suffering such as oppression, cutting, and burning, [are seen as such]. (102)
"Having become soft through your majesty, their pride has been taken away.
The king said:
If these seats do not cause any disturbance in my presence. || 103 ||
"Therefore, O gentle-faced one, you shall remain here like an unmoving pillar.
The gentle-faced one replied:
"Come, O Indra among kings, let us go to our own meritorious abodes, free from affliction."
"I shall not go to enjoy the pleasures born of illusion for those of evil deeds.
The king said:
That happiness is not obtained by men even in heaven or in the world of Brahmā. || 105 ||
It is my conviction that the attainment of nirvāṇa for all beings occurs in this manner;
therefore, I shall not go [to final rest] as long as these [beings] remain in suffering.
By his mere presence, the inhabitants of hell become happy;
fie upon the life of that man who does not grant refuge to one who has come seeking it! 107.
He certainly favors even the faction of his enemies;
yet through sacrifice, charity, and asceticism, he finds no prosperity for himself in the next world. 108.
For one whose mind is intent on protecting the distressed, there arise sons who are dear, as well as the suffering born of them, which is most intense and grants great pain. (111)
By giving the gift of life to these, others obtain a happiness superior even to the bliss of heaven;
for many who are suffering may thus attain such joy.
"What could have been gained by me from her? Therefore, go to Vraja without delay.
The man said:
O Śakra, neither this Dharma nor you have come to me;
we must certainly depart from here, therefore, O King, please go. (113)
Dharma said:
"O Naya, I have not been led by you; you have served me perfectly. || 114 ||
This celestial chariot has now ascended turbid; please depart for your own abode.
The king said:
"O men in hell, being tormented by Yama by the thousands,
you cry out 'Save us!'— yet I do not go there."
Indra said:
In this world, the attainment of hell comes through sinful and evil deeds;
however, O King, you must go to heaven by means of meritorious action.
The king said:
If you know the true nature of dharma, O Śatakratu, speak it as if you were Rati himself.
"You ought to tell me the extent of that land.
Dharma said:
They appeared like stars in the sky above the ocean of Adhīndra. || 118 ||
O King, just as the grains of sand in the Ganges when it rains are beyond counting, so too are the living beings within the various wombs.
Likewise, even the measure of the merit of this glorious eight-syllabled lore, when accompanied by the Raśmimālā, cannot be reached. (20)
Constantly worshipped by you through rites such as japa and homa,
she is the supreme sovereign of the lords of kings, known by the name Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇī.
O Teacher, though [this knowledge] is secret, it has been properly served by you through your grace;
day after day, I desire [to dwell] at your two lotus feet, O Teacher. (122)
O Great King, you have offered jewels, pearls, and other such gifts;
you have constantly presented a hundred cows at the lotus feet of the Preceptor.
A pair of auspicious earrings was placed by you many times upon the two ears of the Teacher, as were rings, ornaments, and the like. (124)
Having been adorned by you with divine and auspicious ornaments,
she was worshipped as the very embodiment of Mahālakṣmī, together with her husband and her attendants.
The sons and grandsons of the teachers have been properly satisfied by you;
by this good deed, they have not gone to the dissolution of their torments.
O King, by pleasing your preceptor, ten thousand generations of your mother’s lineage and ten thousand generations of your father’s lineage have reached the world of Brahmā.
This compassion of yours today, while you are transforming this hellish state,
has itself reached the number of one hundred thousand.
Therefore, O best of kings, go now to my abode to partake of that;
these [others], however, shall exhaust their own karma-born sin in hell.
The king said:
How will those who pride themselves on their association with the virtuous feel any longing [for them], if no excellence arises in them through that very proximity? (130)
Therefore, O Lord of the gods, if the authority of the Vedas is accepted, whatever merit I possess exists solely through the worship of the feet of my teacher. (131)
"By that [merit], let those who have fallen into the hells and are tormented be liberated. Dharma and Śakra said to them:
Thus, O Lord of the Earth, a more excellent state has been attained by you. || 132 ||
And having escaped from these hells, those evildoers were liberated.
The son said:
Then a rain of flowers fell and honored him from above. || 133 ||
The messengers of the Blessed One, marked with signs such as the discus and the conch, arrived;
having placed him upon a celestial chariot, they provided him with this abundance of divine enjoyments.
O ascetic, we—myself and others who have fallen from our status as lords of men—are going to the abode of the Blessed One, where the Lord of Śrī is present in person. (135)
Then, directed by the fruits of their own karma, they entered various wombs;
having attained knowledge born from past experience, it was thus described by me. (136)
"Beyond this, O highly fortunate one, what else shall I tell you?
[Thus ends the thirty-first chapter in the Uttarabhāga of the *Śrīmadanuttarabrahmatattvarahasya*, the *Dāśarathīyatantra*, which is a compendium of the essence and meaning of the Vedas.]
The father said:
Thus has been described the continuous state of cyclic existence (saṃsāra), which, like a water-wheel, revolves incessantly along the path of its own nature. || 1 ||
All this has come upon me in such a manner;
what is the use of speaking of the distress caused by my son while this situation remains as it is?
The son said:
If, O dear one, you trust my words without hesitation,
[I shall grant] the supreme Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā, Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇī.
Having obtained [this] through the grace of the teacher, you shall become liberated while living,
after first reciting the glorious eight-syllabled mantra day by day.
Thereafter, reciting the mantra day after day according to one's capacity, the Queen of the Kings of Queens bestows the eightfold sovereign powers in this world and fulfills all desires.
Endowed with a portion of that very attainment, you shall reach the state of the Blessed One’s abode,
from which one does not return to this earth, to this world crowded with suffering.
The father said:
The glorious eight-syllabled mantra (Aṣṭākṣarī) has been described by you as bestowing all perfections;
the Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā has been described by you as bestowing even greater fruits.
Tell me the entire greatness of the sons resulting from these two sciences,
as well as the fruit of Vedic study even for one who has not studied the Vedas.
"Even after performing the great sacrifices, how is the imperishable fruit of those rites obtained by men? Tell me all of that in its entirety. (9)
The son said:
Listen, dear one, for I shall explain that which you ask about,
for the benefit of all the world and as a means of crossing the ocean of existence.
Having become a twice-born, always endowed with the Vedic sacraments,
he, firm in his vows, should constantly perform the twilight worship at the three periods of the day.
The Veda, along with its six auxiliary limbs and the Pada and Krama recitations, should be studied constantly;
and one should offer oblations into the fire perpetually, both morning and evening, with a self-restrained mind.
One should perform the Brahmayajña and other rites day after day;
the Dharmaśāstras and Purāṇas should be studied day after day. (13)
One of self-restraint must fix one's mind solely on the Dharma as declared in the Śruti;
these [other] duties of a householder are causes for the destruction of one's merit. || 14 ||
The arising of right knowledge is necessary for men to ward off evil;
furthermore, sacrifices accompanied by complete sacrificial fees must certainly be performed.
Bestowing the fruit of imperishable heaven and averting all sins, the immortals enjoy there the eternal and inexhaustible bliss of heaven. (16)

That very [fruit] is enjoyed continuously by those performers of meritorious deeds who are free from sin, and by the performer of sacrifice who is endowed with the complete ritual limbs and sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā). || 17 ||
By one devoted to the study of the Vedas and whose soul is intent upon the Sāvitrī mantra,
there shall be unsurpassed and imperishable bliss in heaven for four hundred yugas.

In this world, one who is devoted to the Agnihotra sacrifice and remains pure through the Vedas morning and evening enjoys in the realm of Mahendra with a splendor equal to that of Mahendra himself. (19)
Constantly devoted to the gift of food, having enjoyed the supreme bliss of heaven, he returns once more to the earth and remains ever engaged in virtuous deeds. (20)
Again he enjoys the happiness of heaven, and again he takes refuge upon the earth;
devoted to the recitation of the *sāvitrī*, he is a worshiper of his father and mother.
He was devoted to the study of the Vedas and intent upon knowing their meaning; on this earth, he was a performer of sacrifices accompanied by the auxiliary sciences and ritual fees.
Constantly devoted to the gift of food and always intent on speaking the truth,
he reaches Satyaloka and enjoys inexhaustible happiness until the end of the kalpa.
Having reached the surface of the earth, he was born into the auspicious lineage of great sages; he had mastered all branches of knowledge and was a worshiper of the lunar days.
One who honors mother, father, gurus, and brothers; one who sustains kinsmen; one devoted to virtuous deeds and self-controlled—such a person attains the world of mortals at the end of the body. (25)
Having remained there for a very long time, he was born once again on the surface of the earth into a family of great sages, becoming thoroughly proficient in all branches of knowledge.
Having attained the recollection of his former births through constant service to the teacher,
and having acquired the knowledge of Brahman, he reaches that supreme abode of Viṣṇu.
Furthermore, one attains liberation free from rebirth; of this there is no doubt.
Having been born in various wombs, even after experiencing hundreds of births, [one eventually reaches this state]. 28.
Having enjoyed pleasures on earth and having experienced all manner of torments,
he dwells for a long time within wombs, defiled by excrement, urine, and other impurities.
Having remained there and emerged from the opening of the womb, it attains the earth by the power of karma,
passing through infancy, youth, childhood, and adulthood in due order.
Having experienced this, one meets death on earth through the power of time;
then, by the force of merit and demerit, one attains either the happiness of heaven or the suffering of hell.
Having enjoyed [the fruits] again and again, he proceeds from the remainder of his karma that leads to rebirth,
after having performed the action enjoined in the Vedas with the realization that it is an offering unto Brahman.
After five births, he shall become one who has attained the state of Brahman,
devoted to Vedic conduct and a worshiper at the feet of his teacher.
Constantly chanting the Brahmavidyā, the twelve-syllable mantra of Śrī-Śrīśa,
one thereafter assumes a divine form and dwells in the world of Brahmā until the end of the kalpa.
Having constantly recited the eight-syllabled mantra that bestows prosperity, one who serves the preceptor will undoubtedly go to that supreme abode of Viṣṇu. (35)
Having recited the auspicious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇī, the Queen of the Queens of Kings,
[one should worship her] with one's life-breaths, wealth, intellect, speech, body, and even with the mind.
Constantly and with devotion serving the pair of feet of the teacher, he is accompanied by a thousand members of his lineage and endowed with divine enjoyments. || 37 ||
Having arrived in person at the city of Ayodhyā, which is the abode of Lord Bhagavat, he [attains] the root of service to the Guru, as well as enjoyment and liberation upon this earth. (38)
Or, having given away even his entire wealth, as well as charming maidens,
he himself became one who possesses nothing, having made them his servants.
Whether remembering the great vidyā of Rājarāja once or every day, one necessarily attains union with Brahman in a single lifetime. (40)
Disregarding the preceptor— who is omnipresent and visibly the very form of the Lord— every day,
we shall go even with thousands of great gifts.
Even by those who have mastered the Vedas, the supreme goal cannot be attained;
nor should one ever, anywhere, speak a false word to the true Guru.
One should not hear censure of one's mother or father from anyone on earth; nor should one instruct one's parents or one's own teacher if they are reproachers [of others]. (43)
One who is incapable [of giving] on this earth should depart after covering his ears;
having abandoned wealth, grain, jewels, elephants, horses, and so forth upon the earth. (44)
Having made a solemn vow to the teacher, one who desires to attain the goal should avoid even a single false word in the presence of the teacher. (45)
Through the accumulated merit of his births, the practitioner becomes purified;
he places a vessel of pure gold in the presence of the pair of feet of the Guru.
Furthermore, that which has been promised by word of mouth as being like the taste of Mount Mandara shall be given within a month; beyond that period, it must be accompanied by interest.
It should be given a month in advance, or even three days before the month.
Or, prior to five months, it should be given together with the interest. || 48 ||
Beyond that, twice as much should be given after one year, and likewise three times as much after [three] years. || 46 ||
Having offered wealth resembling that of the gods at the feet of the Teacher, one is liberated from its punishment; this remains true even at the end of the aeon.
Even after committing a thousand thefts of gold, one attains purity by performing the expiation prescribed in the Śruti; do not entertain any doubt in this matter. (48)
If you desire great accomplishment, be free from doubt regarding the mantra. || 50 ||
One should avoid from afar association with those who revile their teacher;
even conversation with such revilers of the teacher should be abandoned. (51)
Wherever there is a discourse praising the teacher and extolling the virtues of his Dharma, one must certainly go there and listen with reverence. (53)
Rising early every morning and endowed with firm devotion,
one who makes the pleasing of the teacher his sole aim shall attain perfection.
Or a pair of earrings adorned with gold and jewels,
or likewise a pair of bracelets, or even a pair of armlets.
One should give either two karṣas or one karṣa of gold to the preceptor’s wife, whether every six months or once a year.
Having directly enjoyed the splendor of Mahendra on earth with the thought that it was Mahālakṣmī herself,
he shall, at the end of that, attain the supreme and eternal state.
One should honor the teacher’s sons, grandsons, and others as one would the teacher himself;
for the reality of the teacher is concealed within all the Vedas and Śāstras. (57)
On this earth, devotion alone to the pair of feet of the Teacher is the great seed of worldly enjoyment and liberation; nothing else has been declared by the wise. (58)
Thus, day after day, the one firm in devotion to the lotus feet of the Teacher,
having recited the supreme Rājarājeśvarī at the auspicious moment of the venerable Eight-Eyed One (Śiva), [attained success].
Even by recollecting [this] but once, one will become Brahman.

[Thus ends the thirty-second chapter, titled "The Majesty of the Knowledge of the King of Kings," in the Uttarabhāga of the *Vedasārārthasaṃgraha*, the *Dāśarathīya Tantra* concerning the secret essence of the unsurpassed Brahman-reality.]
The son said:
Listen, my dear, I shall proclaim the supreme mantra of the Queen of the Kings of Kings:
first is the seed-syllable of the Triple Veda (trayī), and immediately after that, the seed-syllable of Śrī.
After that, one should recite Lokeśvarī, Vāmārāja, and the three *kūṭas*;
then again, having uttered Śrī, there follows the glorious eight-syllable mantra.
The auspicious Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, the king of kings, proclaims: "This Vidyā, when recited, bestows enjoyments, celestial realms, and noble status upon devotees. (3)
She is the sovereign queen of all vidyās, the mistress of all lion-thrones, the destroyer of heaps of great sins, and the bestower of the fruits of all merit. || 4 ||
She consists of all the Vedas, she takes the form of all the Purāṇas and Smṛtis, she embodies the conclusions of all philosophical systems, and she is the embodiment of Yoga.
She consists of all ritual actions, she is the embodiment of all sacred fords and sacrifices;
she is the sovereign queen of all sciences and the warder-off of all calamities.
The first seed-syllable of all four Vedas,
which is of the nature of the Supreme Brahman, has been proclaimed by me through my waves of grace.

This Vidyā, consisting of three seed-syllables, bestows the fruit of pure liberation, immediately pierces through the mass of sins, and subsequently brings about the fortune of the three powers (triśakti).
She who deludes the three worlds, who brings the fortune of all men under her control, who bestows all prosperity, and who grants the fruits of the perfection of all vidyās. || 9 ||
Then there is Śrī Mahāvidyā Trikūṭā, the Supreme Sovereign,
who bestows the great perfection of speech, like the surging waves and billows of the Gaṅgā.
She bestows the sovereignty of the eight supernatural powers beginning with atomization (aṇimā),
shatters all obstacles, grants the eight perfections such as the magic pill and the sandals, and provides both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
The single-syllabled [mantra] of Śrī is the supreme knowledge, whose form is consciousness;
it bestows eternal bliss and great spiritual accomplishments, and it is the destroyer of poverty.
The glorious eight-syllabled mantra bestows enjoyment, heaven, and liberation;
it is the knowledge of Brahman, endowed with the three powers and the consciousness of the three Śrī-kūṭas.
She who is known by the name Rājarājeśvarī is remembered as Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇī;
even the sages do not know this Rājarājeśvarī.

In the Āgamas, it is proclaimed that for the Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā, there is no requirement for the placement of mantras on the limbs (tāṅga-nyāsa), the hands (kara-nyāsa), or preparatory rites such as puraścaraṇa. (15)
The ancient supreme seers have declared this to be a perfected vidyā,
which belongs eternally to the son of Rājarāja Manu, even by remembering it but once.
From the complete recitation of all four Vedas along with their auxiliary limbs, he obtains the full fruit of a hundred sacrifices; of this there is no doubt.
The fruit that results from giving a great gift to a thousand people during a conflict at Kurukṣetra is indeed obtained by remembering this King of Kings’ Vidyā even once. 18.
He performed a thousand Vājapeya sacrifices along with their constituent parts and sacrificial fees;
there is no doubt about this, for it is stated in the Smṛti that he was a knower of royal science.

Whatever fruit one might obtain by circumambulating the earth every single day, that is obtained all at once through the mere recollection of the Great Knowledge (Mahāvidyā), O King of Kings. || 20 ||
Whatever fruit one obtains by bathing in all the sacred fords, such as the Gaṅgā, one obtains that entirely by a single recollection of the Mahāvidyā, O Rājarāja. (21)
Whether it be a thousand wish-fulfilling gems, or a hundred *pārijāta* trees, or a thousand *kāmadhenu* cows, or a hundred *kalpa* trees; || 22 ||
The supreme Rājarājeśvarī is the sixteenth digit of the great vidyās of the King of Kings; by remembering her even once, [one attains the goal]. 23.
That state which a practitioner attains cannot be reached even by those performing austerities, nor can it be attained through millions of great gifts. (24)
The destination that has been proclaimed for one endowed with the eightfold yoga is attained by remembering this royal science even once. (25)
This beautiful one, known as Vallabhā, is the sovereign of the throne of knowledge;
some great sages call her the Mahānārāyaṇī Vidyā.
The ancients have declared the unsurpassed knowledge of Brahman;
we shall now proclaim that which is called the King of Kings, the bestower of all accomplishments.
The manifest speech (vaikharī) is declared to be the Mother (mātṛkā), consisting of the fifty letters;
from her arise the Vedas, all the Śāstras, and the vast collections of Purāṇas and Āgamas.
Vaikharī is born from the Mātṛkā; Vaidavari is the supreme Kalā. She has the form of the three peaks (Kūṭas), she is Śrī, the fifteen-syllabled Lakṣmī. || 29 ||
The eighteen branches of knowledge have also arisen from a portion of her alone—
namely, the Brahmavidyā, the Triśakti, and that which is conjoined with the three Śrīkūṭas.
The supreme mantra of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇī, the sovereign of the queens of kings, bestows all perfections whether remembered but once or daily. || 31 ||
All the Vedas have been studied by you, and sacrifices with their proper fees have been performed;
there is no doubt that food has been eaten by you every single day. (32)
Whatever fruit is obtained by the twice-born through one hundred thousand recitations of the Gāyatrī, that same fruit is certainly attained by remembering this King of Kings' Vidyā just once. (33)
That fruit which is obtained by reciting the fifteen-syllable Śrī-mantra one hundred thousand times is attained daily by one who has partaken [of this]; there is no doubt in this matter. || 34 ||
By remembering her even once, Sundarī shall obtain from Vallabhā the glorious eight-syllabled mantra (aṣṭākṣara) together with all its ritual placements (nyāsa).
Whatever fruit a twice-born man obtains by reciting [the mantra] fifty thousand times along with its ancillaries,
that same fruit they obtain from the pure recitation of the Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā.
Having given a thousand cows along with the ancillary ritual fees (dakṣiṇā),
and having recited the mantra of the King of Kings even once, one enjoys the fruit of that [merit].
Then indeed, the eternal, auspicious Mahāvidyā Rājarājeśvarī, who is the cause for the perfect realization of the universal self, appeared. 36.
The fourteen worlds, including all things moving and unmoving, constantly abide within the body of even the son of a king of kings. (37)
Wherever on earth there is the great lore of the king of kings that protects the subjects,
that very place is Alakā, the banks of the Nandā, and the hermitage of Dadhica.
Wherever one who chants the mantra of Rājarājeśvarī may dwell in a hermitage, there indeed reside the sacred fords such as the Jāhnavī and others. (39)
Neither consecration nor initiation is required for the Rājarājeśvarī when she is seized;
rather, service at the feet of a true teacher always bestows all perfections.
The earth, consisting of the seven continents, girdled by mines of precious metals, endowed with wealth, grain, elephants, horses, and the like, and filled with jewels; || 41 ||
Even after giving [these], the disciple, together with his wife, sons, and others, should daily remain intent upon service at the lotus feet of the preceptor. (42)
Even by giving ten thousand cows or even ten million pieces of gold daily at the auspicious pair of lotus feet of the Preceptor; || 43 ||
One should always be intent on service with one's speech, wealth, and intellect, even toward a giver of all jewels who bestows them by the millions. (44)
The auspicious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇī-vidyā, which bestows a thousand villages upon the giver and makes one a sovereign queen over kings, must never be given to anyone under any circumstances.
Ten million great vidyās, complete with their ancillaries, ritual placements (nyāsa), and so forth, were chanted by him; through this recitation, he became the Lord of the Ageless Queen.
The bestower of the Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā alone is the Great One;
he himself is the supreme Brahmā, Rudra, Viṣṇu, and Prajāpati. (47)
That Blessed One, Nārāyaṇa, does not exist apart from the Supreme; having served him for a thousand years with prayers and offerings day after day, he attained wisdom. (48)
O venerable one, that auspicious Queen of the Kings of Kings must certainly be obtained by the giver of everything, even at the cost of his own life, for the sake of the maidens.
This auspicious Mahāvidyā Rājarājeśvarī must not be given away without having first performed a thousand *puraścaraṇa* repetitions or a hundred horse-sacrifices.
The teacher does not merit even a sixteenth part of a mere fragment of compassion;
one must remain in the presence of the teacher and perform service for the teacher. 51.
Service to the teacher must be performed; the words spoken by the teacher must be remembered.
Proximity to the pair of the teacher’s feet bestows all perfections. 52.
That alone is the divine field which removes all sins and bestows worldly enjoyment, heaven, and liberation— that indeed is the Badarī forest.
That very place is the bank of the Jāhnavī, that very place is the bank of the Yamunā;
that very bank of the Goddess of Speech is declared to be Kurukṣetra.
That very Naimiṣa forest is a preeminent sacred site (tīrtha) to be praised;
it should be visited by one of self-restraint who desires the fruit of bathing in all sacred sites.
One who desires the supreme perfection of the glorious eight-syllable mantra and other such attainments must drink the water from the pair of feet of the Guru, which has been purified by me. 56.
One should give the teacher’s fee (dakṣiṇā), consisting of wealth, gems, and so forth,
for the sake of propitiating the Mother while reciting [the mantra], adorned with auspicious ornaments of Brahmā.
The teacher’s wife, who is always Mahālakṣmī herself, must be worshipped by one who desires the favor even of the gods, such as Brahmā and Viṣṇu. (58)
The sons of the teacher are to be honored with garments, ornaments, and so forth;
[this yields] the fruit of the constant recitation of all four Vedas.

The fruit of the Aśvayuj sacrifice, when constantly accompanied by the prescribed limbs and sacrificial fees, as well as the fruit of the gift of a thousand cows, when accompanied by the sacrificial fees, [is attained].
The *puraścaraṇa* of the ten-syllabled mantra beginning with *Śrī-Śrī*, of the glorious eight-syllabled mantra, and of the fifteen-syllabled mantra of Śrī, is auspicious and fruitful. (61)
One who desires [this] should recite daily the auspicious Rājarājeśvarī mantra ten or twelve times; when recited thus, it bestows the fruit of all that has been performed.

One who desires the supernatural powers such as atomization (aṇimā) and the rest, as well as the eightfold sovereignty beginning with the sandals, and likewise dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa, should observe his vows with self-restraint.
A pure person should recollect the Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā even once;
[thereby] they will attain the power of entering cities and bodies, as well as the ṣaṇmudrās, such as the cīriṇī and others.
It is accomplished for one who recites even once the mantra known as Suṃdarīvallabhā,
because the great Praṇava-mantra is the primordial source of the Vedas.
Through daily remembrance, the Supreme Brahman manifests directly;
through the daily remembrance of the Vidyā of Lakṣmī, who possesses the three powers, on this earth.
Mahālakṣmī, the mother of the world, Pārvatī, the beloved of Śaṅkara,
is indeed the art of desire (Kāmakalā), the manifest Śakti, the supreme sovereign lady.
When pleased, they become bestowers of boons upon this devotee; of this there is no doubt.
Now follows the fifteen-syllable mantra of Śrī, complete with three peaks (trikūṭa). 68.
The earth-plane is the first city; the second is the realm of Bhuvaḥ;
the third is declared here to be the city known as the heavenly world (Svargaloka). (69)
The triad of fires, the three Vedas, the triad of powers, as well as the triad of Brahmā, Īśa, and Viṣṇu, and also the triad of vowels; 70.
Furthermore, in the third Puṣkara, it is said that the threefold splendor of Hari resides in the triad of his steps; this is the ancient teaching that bestows the desired blessings of Śrī.
This is the primordial name of the illustrious Goddess, "Tripurā," which is most exalted; this unsurpassed name is also found within the Vedāntas and the Śrutis.
The word "Sundarī" follows, enchanting all who hear it;
among other divine maidens, there exists no one known by the name Sundarī. (73)
"Subhagā-sundarī"—this is remembered as the first name of Śrī;
"Lalitā," the great name of Śrī, bestows all fruits. (74)
These names of the Goddess Śrī are secret even within the Vedas;
moreover, the word "Mahat" (the Great) expresses the supreme transcendence of the Goddess Śrī over the entire universe.
At the end of the word "Mahātripura," the phrase "Sundarī Śriyaḥ" must not be uttered; this is to be kept secret even from one's own son at all times.
"Mahāśrīsundarī" and "Mahātripurasundarī"—these two names of the Goddess Śrī are said to be most exalted. (77)
This very [goddess] is the embodiment of the three Vedas (trayī), possessing the form of the letters *ā*, *sṛ*, *kā*, *va*, and *r*.
By the constant remembrance of her, Umā, Lakṣmī, and Sarasvatī [are attained]. 78.
Durgā, Bhadrakālī, and the other goddesses become bestowers of all perfections upon him;
moreover, the four Vedas are studied by him day after day.
Those hundred crore great sacrifices, complete with full sacrificial fees, and even those seven crore great mantras, though recited thousands of times—[are all surpassed by this]. (80)
Therefore, every day there arise sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā) accompanied by gold;
from that [arises] the auspicious Ekākṣarī, the direct and beautiful digit of consciousness (citkalā) of the Goddess Śrī. 81.
The Supreme Goddess, the Mother of the Universe, who consists of the Supreme Brahman, is to be known as the power of consciousness (cicchakti), as Śrī, as Gati, and as the supreme power Nārāyaṇī. 82.
This supreme Śrī is the power of consciousness (cicchakti) distinct from the Supreme Brahman;
by constant meditation upon her, one becomes a person whose very nature is consciousness (cidrūpī puruṣaḥ). 83.
She who is denoted by the word "Śrī" is Śrīdevī, Lakṣmī, Tripurasundarī, Mātṛkā, Mahālakṣmī, Lalitā, and Parameśvarī. (84)

O great sages, this divine Śrī, who is the sovereign splendor of the kingdom of Consciousness (cit), is expressed by the three syllables [of the mantra] and is the supreme embodiment of the three Vedas (trayī). 85.
At the end of that is the auspicious Bhagavad-vidyā, the glorious eight-syllabled mantra (Śrīmadaṣṭākṣarī).
The glorious eight-syllabled mantra is to be addressed as Brahmanārāyaṇa by name. (86)
The all-pervading, free from fear, the cause of creation, maintenance, and so forth;
consisting of all knowledge, the seed of all things, that which is beyond the supreme. 87.

This supreme and glorious eight-syllabled mantra bestows heaven and the higher realms upon those who are devoted, grants all perfections to those who recite it, and has the syllable *praṇava* as its inherent beginning. 88.
This [mantra], endowed with the great seed-syllable of Guptalakṣmī, bestows the fruit [of one's desires].
Preceded by the *praṇava* (Oṃ), it consists of the three powers (*triśakti*) and is joined with Śrī and Suṃdarī. (89)
The glorious eight-syllabled lore is known by the name Sundarīvallabhā;
she is remembered as Rājarājeśvarī by name, consisting of all vidyās.
This knowledge, which protects the universe, was obtained through the grace of the teacher;
it bestows abundant qualities, sovereignty, and a captivating web of sciences.

O Arvāṇa, the eternal Vidyā of the Sovereign of Kings, which is the essence of the great Vedas and consists of the nature of Truth, Bliss, and Consciousness, bestows jewels, wealth, grain, and prosperity upon the worlds day after day; that very Hari, the Infallible One, is indeed the treasures such as Śaṅkha, Padma, and the rest, for they dwell within His waters.
The eight supernatural powers, beginning with *aṇimā* and *mahimā*, enter his body; and beings such as Añjana and others attain perfection through him—of this there is no doubt. (96)
Even for thousands of millions of births, there shall be remembrance [of the truth] for that pure person who recites the Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā every day. (97)
The great sages, Vasiṣṭha and others, worship Hari;
Śakra, the Lord of Wealth, and the other chief lords of the quarters serve him. || 98 ||
The Siddhas and great sages such as Nārada and others honor him;
Lakṣmī herself resides in his palace until the dissolution of all beings.
The servant girl dances upon her tongue and Sarasvatī dances as long as she offers gold at the lotus feet of the Preceptor.
Now, indeed, the preliminary rites (puraścaryā) for which have been described are as follows:
the gold-ness of gold [is established] by means of thirty-three marks. 101.
Thus, whether at a transit [of the sun], on the new moon day, or even on the full moon day; or when the sun is eclipsed by Rāhu, or during a lunar node (parvan). || 102 ||
On the fifth lunar day, or on a Saturday, or during the conjunctions of Jupiter and the Sun or Jupiter and the Moon,
or on the twelfth day of the month of Kārtika, one should perform the rites for the two vidyās known as Rājarāja and [the other].
Having offered three hundred oblations of clarified butter into the two feet of his own preceptor, he then gave one gold coin into the lotus-like feet of the preceptor’s wife.
Having offered gold there, one indeed performs the *puraścaryā* that yields fruit, which produces immediate conviction. || 105 ||
The power of this Itthasasyā bestows all perfections immediately;
it cannot be described even by words and is beyond the scope of the Vedas.
Having abandoned all the Vedas and whatever Dharmaśāstras there are, having abandoned all the Purāṇas and even all the Upaniṣads; || 107 ||
Having set aside the Bhagavadraśmi-sūkta, the Raśmi-sūkta of Śrī, and even the entire network of Nyāsas, one should [worship] this Rājarājeśvarī.

By chanting the *Lakṣmīnārāyaṇī*, one obtains the fruit arising from the study of the Vedas, the fruit of reciting the Vedas in their entirety (*vedapārāyaṇa*), and the fruit arising from the study of the Śāstras. || 109 ||
The fruit of bathing at all sacred fords, the fruit of studying the Vedānta, the constant fruit of a hundred sacrifices, and the supreme fruit of all acts of charity [are obtained thereby]. (110)

The auspicious fruit of the preliminary rite (puraścaryā) for the glorious eight-syllabled mantra (aṣṭākṣarī-vidyā), and the fruit of the preliminary rite for the Śrī-vidyā along with its ancillaries, [are attained] day by day. 111.
He obtains [this]; there is no doubt here—do not entertain any uncertainty in this matter. || 111 ||

The high-souled son of Atharvan, having seen this great mantra— the essence of the three Vedas— along with the Vedas, the scriptures, and the collections of Purāṇas, spoke thus, having attained his purpose and appearing in the form of the Lord.
The blessed, high-souled son of Dharma, having performed his recitation, subsequently attained the state of a beast;
yet that very same blessed Mukunda became a great soul once again through the power of knowledge. 113.
Śrīrāma, Śrīpati, Śrīśa, Śrīmān, Śrīyavallabha, as well as Śrīkānta, Śrīmahāyogī, and Śrīnārāyaṇa—thus he is called. (114)
No word equal to the word "Śrī Nārāyaṇa" exists;
by remembering and recollecting the name of Śrī Nārāyaṇa day after day, [one attains liberation]. 115.
Liberated from heaps of sins, he is undoubtedly liberated while living; there is nothing today equal to Nārāyaṇa for destroying the fear of death.
"It does not exist, it truly does not exist, it simply does not exist; this is the truth, I speak the truth.
Nārāyaṇa is supreme to the Vedas; Nārāyaṇa is supreme to the sacrifices. (117)
Nārāyaṇa is the supreme scripture; Nārāyaṇa is the supreme tradition.
Whether he be an outcaste, a dog-cooker, or even a pañcamas, [he is Nārāyaṇa]. (118)
Indeed, by remembering the name "Śrī Nārāyaṇa" at the end [of one's recitation], one attains liberation;
even that must be obtained from the mouth of a teacher, O Guru, and not otherwise. (119)
They call this supreme five-syllabled knowledge Nārāyaṇī;
even one who is pure becomes impure, yet by constantly remembering these five syllables, he remains pure.
One attains the supreme goal, which is difficult even for yogis to reach; how much more so for those whose souls are devoted to the recitation of the glorious eight-syllable mantra? 121.
The power of the Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā for those whose souls are devoted to its recitation and fire-offerings cannot be measured even by Brahmā himself. 122.
Even one who merely remembers this Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā even once every day shall become worthy of worship by the gods as well as by the great sages of restrained mind.
Having obtained this Rājarājeśvarī through the grace of the teacher, whoever constantly remembers her ten or twelve times [a day], [attains success]. 124.
He is declared to be the Guru, the astrologer, and the practitioner;
he is the sacrificer, the most excellent of the twice-born, the ascetic, and the high-minded one;
he is the purified soul, the lord of the earth, as well as the brother and the father. (125)
He alone is the mother and the kinsman; he is the performer of the Agnihotra, the supreme ascetic;
he is Mahā-Vāsudeva, he is the yogi, and he is the great sage.
He is remembered as the Brahman-sage and the Creator; he is Viṣṇu and he is Śiva.
He alone is the all-pervading Lord who effects the creation, maintenance, and destruction of the worlds.
That very lineage of his is celebrated throughout the world of mortals as long as it endures; his mother alone is constantly proclaimed as blessed upon the face of the earth. (128)
For one who has thus performed his duty, his kinsmen become purified in that [state];
he attains liberation, there is no doubt, and he becomes great.
What is the use of speaking much more on this matter? I shall state the summary of the meaning of the Vedas: there is no knowledge equal to the Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā. 130.
Yamā, Aindrī, Mahālakṣmī, Dhanadaśrī, Acancalā, Yāvāruṇī, and Rājyalakṣmī—she is established as all these. (131)
Whatever knowledge exists among the Gandharvas, among the weapons, among the sciences, and among the deities—
whatever knowledge resides in the mouth of Brahmā, may that knowledge be present in his mouth.
Or rather, its preliminary practice (puraścaryā) is said to consist of the teacher’s fee (dakṣiṇā). || 134 ||
The fruit that has been proclaimed by the great sages in the Āgamas as resulting from ten million oblations of the fifteen-syllable and the eight-syllable Śrī-mantras— [is obtained here]. (135)
It is taught that when recited alone, the fruit of this royal vidyā is attained;
[so too is it] for the glorious eight-syllabled vidyā in rites such as the preliminary service (puraścaryā).
Having performed the preliminary rites (puraścaryā) and other rituals for the fifteen-syllable mantra of Śrī,
one should likewise offer oblations twelve times with the Vidyā known as Rājarāja.
One obtains the eternal fruit of the preliminary rite (puraścaryā) involving the number of the sun;
with his two eyes, he beholds that Supreme Brahman upon the surface of the earth. 138.
The world-protectors of King Kiṅkara [bestowed] even heaps of cintāmaṇi jewels,
a thousand kalpa-trees, and likewise a hundred kāmadhenu cows.
It bestows the eightfold eternal sovereignty beginning with *aṇimā*;
this alone is the most formidable, and this alone is the most sublime. (140)
This alone is the supreme knowledge; this alone is the supreme goal;
this alone is the highest good; this alone is the supreme fruit. || 141 ||
This alone is the supreme initiation; this is the highest great yoga; this alone is the ultimate state of union; this indeed is the great vow.
"This alone is the supreme Brahman; this knowledge is most exalted.
Considering it to be the Vidyā of the Queen of the Queens of Kings, one should constantly remember it thus. (143)
Even for the Queen of Queens of Kings, the worship of the Guru must be performed;
these two alone are the great seeds of liberation, and no other exists.
Having spoken thus to his father, Sumati, the best among the knowers of Brahman,
followed the high-souled Yājñavalkya accompanied by his own father.
Having offered everything— cows, buffaloes, and so forth, as well as wealth, jewels, and the like— to Yājñavalkya, he gave him the entire wealth of his possessions as the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
Having performed service to his feet with devotion for three years, by means of wiping away the remnants [of his food] and massaging his feet, and so forth. (147)
His two servants, through such tasks as washing his clothes, kept him awake;
and his wife, having become his maidservants, honored him with ornaments and other offerings.
And having gratified his sons by requesting them for heaps of wealth,
they both received the Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā from the mouth of their preceptor.
Constantly devoted to the service of their guru, they shall attain prosperity endowed with the eightfold qualities,
as well as all blessings and the eternal vision of Brahman.
Having uplifted a thousand families, they attained the supreme state.
Śrī Kapilācārya said:
The power of the Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā is exceedingly vast; alas, it cannot be described even by me, let alone by others. 152.

[Thus ends the thirty-third chapter in the Uttarabhāga of the *Śrīmadanuttarabrahmatattvarahasya*, the *Daśarathīya Tantra*, which is a compendium of the essential meaning of the Vedas, concerning the majesty of the *Rājarājalakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-vidyā*.]
The venerable Kapilācārya said:
This essential summary has been spoken by me for the sake of the sons of Daśaratha;
among the Āgamas and Purāṇas, there is nothing superior to this.
This yogi Nārāyaṇa, the Blessed One, the Supreme Lord, having become the son of Daśaratha on earth, is called Śrī Rāma. || 2 ||
This supreme power (Kalā), Śrī herself, has arisen manifest from the ground of being;
sporting with her, he is called Śrīrāma.
The Supreme Person (Puruṣottama) is to be expressed by the Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā;
indeed, His first name, Śrī Nārāyaṇa, is celebrated in the Śruti.
The supreme Brahman named Nārāyaṇa is the compendium of Vedānta;
Nārāyaṇa is the supreme Brahman, Nārāyaṇa is the highest.
Nārāyaṇa is the supreme light, Nārāyaṇa is the supreme Self;
[He is attained] through the stores of merit accumulated over many births which destroy all sins.
Through the constant recollection of Nārāyaṇa, firm devotion arises;
this second [practice] also grants both worldly enjoyment and liberation by piercing through all that is primordial.
The name "Śrī Rāma" has been correctly perceived within the Vedas by the great seers;
his third name is declared to be "Vāsudeva."
There is nothing other than the three syllables [Nārāyaṇa] that bestows all fruits;
even one joined with great sins, by remembering Nārāyaṇa even once— || 9 ||
Even Ajāmīla, the lowest of the twice-born,
who had fallen away from the study of the Vedas and was long associated with hunters, attained the supreme reality.
By constantly remembering the name of Śrī Rāma through the instruction of a companion,
Vālmīki became renowned as the manifest lord of the lineage of sages.
O highly fortunate ones, those who take refuge at the feet of Vāsudeva are free from fear;
they have attained the supreme state that is difficult even for Śakra and the other gods to reach.
This highly fortunate Sītā who has appeared from the surface of the earth is Śrī Devī herself,
the mother of all, consisting of fifteen syllables.
The first power is called by the name Śrī, while in the second, the name Mahālakṣmī is proclaimed. || 14 ||
The third secret name is said to be Mahāśrīsundarī;
the fourth shall be Sītā, and after that, Jānakī. (15)
O best of the twice-born, although Nārāyaṇa and the Goddess Śrī possess many names, all of them shall today be taken away by Hara this very instant. (16)
These names of the Unborn One grant liberation immediately;
first is the name Śrī Nārāyaṇa, and then Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa.
Then, having approached the Lord Śrīśa, he sang the name of Śrīvāsudeva;
therefore, the auspicious eight-syllabled mantra (Aṣṭākṣarī) conjoined with "Śrī" should be recited. 18.
The Ātharvaṇī [Vidyā], even if recited only once, grants all accomplishments daily; for the reciter of the Rājarājeśvarī, there is no need for new vows or fasting. (19)
The study of the Vedas does not depend on inference, nor does sacrifice;
likewise, the study of the *Raśmimālā* does not depend on the *Nyāsa*, for it is not so.
It is said that by the mere remembrance of the fifteen-syllable Śrī-mantra, the glorious eight-syllable mantra, and the Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā, perfection is attained.
She is the Vidyā of the Queen of Queens, the embodiment of all Vidyās;
she consists of all Yoga and is the very essence of all Dharmaśāstras. || 22 ||
She consists of all sacred fields, she embodies all holy fords and sacrifices, she is supreme;
she consists of all the Vedas, and she is the embodiment of Brahman and all the great seers. || 23 ||
Consisting of the entire universe, her very nature being the seat of all powers,
she is this supreme Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇī, the sovereign of the kings of kings.
The sustainer of all the worlds, the sovereign of the lion-throne of knowledge,
having obtained me through the grace of the Preceptor, [I have been worshipped] twenty-eight times daily.

Whether ten or twelve times, the best of practitioners who should thus recollect [the mantra] while talking—the fruit of such recitation is declared to be meditative absorption (samādhi) even during sleep. (26)
The circumambulation of the earth is said to be his movement; of this there is no doubt.
The entire craft of forming mudrās is certainly his creation. (27)
Eating, the daily fire-sacrifice, prostration, and sitting in meditation;
meditating on the Lord with the mind—this activity is called austerity. (28)
Therefore, such knowledge must certainly be protected even at the cost of one's life, just as a treasure is guarded from a thief. (29)
One's entire possession should be given away—beasts, jewels, wealth, and so forth;
even daughters endowed with beauty and well-adorned should be given.
Even one's sons, endowed with learning and humility, should be given away;
likewise, one's own virtuous wife, though young and beautiful in all her limbs. (31)
That royal fortune, though as fickle as a lightning flash, must be bestowed upon the seeker;
even one's own head, together with one's life-breaths, must be given away upon the surface of the earth.
This great vidyā of the king of kings must never be given to anyone—not even to a king who bestows his kingdom, nor to a brother, a son, or a kinsman. (33)
This most exalted Vidyā of the Queen of Queens should not be given away, even at the cost of one's life, all one's possessions, wife, sons, or daughters. (34)
Dependent upon the feet of the teacher, he acts upon the surface of the earth,
free from envy, devoid of egoism, having conquered anger, and with his senses subdued.
One who is always devoted to serving the pair of the teacher’s feet is to be accepted as a disciple along with his entire retinue; no one else is so, even if he bestows a kingdom.
A father gives limitedly, a mother gives limitedly, and a son gives limitedly;
but the teacher is said to be the giver of immeasurable desired objects both in this world and the next. (37)
Having transgressed the command of the teacher even once upon this earth, one is long deprived of friends, sons, wife, and the like. (38)
Having become one who is devoted to suffering, he shall become a mute at the end of his body;
thereafter, for a thousand births, he shall be a dog and then a donkey.
Without transgressing the command of the teacher, with an undistracted mind and constant devotion, may I abide here, endowed with all sovereign powers and taking refuge in eternal bliss. (40)
Accompanied by a thousand generations of his lineage, he will certainly attain liberation,
whether in the presence of the pair of feet of the Ācārya or even at Cihnuka.
When a promise is made by the best of the twice-born, such as "I shall give a thousand pieces of gold" or "I shall provide food," that is declared to be a great debt.
It should be paid within that month; beyond that, it is accompanied by interest.
By means of those three [methods], it should be recovered along with the interest.
Beyond that, it is ordained that twice the amount should be given; after six months, it is remembered as triple;
at the end of a year, it is multiplied [fourfold]; and beyond that, there is no atonement.

Whosoever among practitioners on this earth desires supreme happiness here and hereafter, inexhaustible great sovereignty, and the perfect attainment of identity with Brahman— [should practice this]. (45)
He who desires to avoid supreme suffering and the torments of hell should become a servant at the pair of feet of the Teacher day after day.
Having transgressed the command of the teacher, one must remain upon this earth;
for the killing of a father or mother is said to be equal to the slaying of a Brahmin.
It is declared that for those who transgress the command of the guru, there is no atonement;
yet he remains constantly endowed with happiness through his wife, sons, family, and so forth. (48)
O sons of Brahmā, pearls, jewels, the Ganges, horses, and other riches would be found at every step through the grace of the compassionate Ācārya; it cannot be otherwise.
If there is great compassion for the disciple every day on this earth,
then here [in this world] one attains all sovereignty, and liberation is eternal.
He constantly recollects the Vidyā of the Queen of Queens, obtained from his preceptor Pūrṇakaruṇā, which bestows all spiritual accomplishments.
For him, enjoyment becomes yoga, sin becomes merit,
and even saṃsāra becomes liberation through the recitation of the Queen of Mantras, O King of Kings.
O sons of Brahmā, for one who remembers Rājarājamahāvidyā,
even the status of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, and others is not difficult to attain.
The teacher is equal to a thousand fathers and mothers;
indeed, there is no deity on earth equal to the teacher.
O King of Kings, if there were a merit equal to a thousand horse-sacrifices written upon a leaf, it would then be comparable to this great vidyā. || 55 ||
Then there exists a Great Knowledge (Mahāvidyā) equal to the King of Kings; likewise, there is a gift equal to the Meru of jewels that destroys evil. 56.
Then the Great Vidyā, the Queen of Queens, is described as being peerless;
for what sacred ford equal to the Ganges exists that removes all sins? (57)
If there exists a sacred field equal to Śeṣācala that bestows all perfections, or if there exists a sacred field equal to Vārāṇasī that grants liberation; [58]
O King of Kings, if even a single portion of the Baharī forest were to grant immediate fruit, then it would be equal to the Great Vidyā.
What is the use of saying more here? She is the supreme sovereign of the kings of kings; she is declared to be the essence of all vidyās and the illusory power (māyā) of all Brahman.
Therefore, whoever constantly remembers this Great Vidyā, which has issued from the lotus-like mouth of the Teacher and is full of compassionate grace; || 61 ||
The person who directly manifests as Nārāyaṇa himself [attains] the greatness of the Great Vidyā of the King of Kings, which destroys intoxication. 62.
Thus, a little has been spoken by me; now I shall describe the means of accomplishment (sādhana).

[Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter, titled "The Majesty of the Rājarāja-vidyā," in the latter portion of the *Śrīmadanuttarabrahmatattvarahasya*, the *Dāśarathīya-tantra*, which is a compendium of the essential meaning of the Vedas.]
The Blessed One said:
O daughters of Brahmā, endowed with purity, listen as I shall describe the procedure for the performance of the great vidyā of the King of Kings, which bestows the desired results. || 1 ||
Having risen during the Brāhma-muhūrta, while still remaining on one's bed,
one should meditate upon the pair of feet of the Guru within the auspicious aperture of Brahmā.
In the lotus of a thousand petals blooming within the aperture of the heart,
[he is] like pure crystal, endowed with hands granting boons and fearlessness.
With a serene countenance and peaceful, adorned with divine ornaments,
he is composed of both male and female, or indeed assumes the form of Brahmā.

Having meditated upon the high-souled Ācārya—who is omniscient, a treasure-house of compassion, and who is either the very form of Maheśvara or directly identical with Nārāyaṇa—(one should proceed). || 5 ||
Then, having bowed again and again with reverence to that pair of lotus feet,
[he was nourished] by the drops of nectar falling from the pair of those feet.
Having meditated upon oneself as immersed [in light], one is liberated from all sins;
[one perceives] from the base [of the body] up to the aperture of Brahma (brahmarandhra) a radiance possessing the splendor of hundreds of millions of suns.
Having meditated upon that supreme consciousness, blazing and resembling molten gold,
his body was turned tawny by the mass of its splendor.
Having seen the pair of Śrī-pādukās placed upon the lotus-feet of the Ācārya— whether they be made of gold or silver— and having recited the Pādukā-mantra, [one should worship].
Seeing Tulasī, a Vedic scholar, a pair [of lovers], the seven great sages, a great river, a flickering fire, and having remembered the Lord of Śrī; 10.
Having washed his hands and feet, he should then recite the Brahma-vidyā;
or else, having risen during the Brāhma-muhūrta with a restrained mind.
Having first seen the clarified butter from the mouth of the preceptor, one should bow to the two lotuses;
in the absence of the guru, one should bow to the Śrīpādukā mounted upon his feet.
Then, after looking at a river or similar object,
one should recite the mantra twenty-eight times, or twenty times, twelve times, or even ten times.
Thereafter, one should mutter the Brahmavidyā, then the twelve-syllable mantra of Śrī and the Lord (Śrī-Śrīśa),
and recollect the Bhagavadraśmi Sūkta either three times or once.
Thereafter, one should remember the garland of rays of Śrī in three ways; or else, one should recite once the hymn (sūkta) called "The Garland of Rays" of Śrī, which was previously described.
Then, one should recollect the Mahāvidyā of the Lion-Throne even once;
having chanted the fifteen-syllable mantra of Śrī twenty-eight times, [one attains success]. 16.
One should recollect the hymn beginning with "Suprabhāta," which is dear to the Blessed One.
May Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, the destroyer of Tripura, the Sun, the Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, Rāhu, and Ketu—all together—grant me a most auspicious dawn. (18)
May Bhṛgu, Vasiṣṭha, Kratu, Aṅgiras, Manu, Pulastya, Pulaha, Gautama, Raibhya, Marīci, Cyavana, and the great sage Vana—all together—make my morning auspicious. (19)
May Sanatkumāra, Kaśyapa, Nandana, Sanātana, as well as Āsuri and Piṅgala—the seven notes, the seven tastes, and the seven netherworlds—all together grant me a beautiful dawn. || 20 ||

May the earth with its fragrance, water with its taste, fire with its heat, wind with its touch, and ether with its sound—may all these together, along with the Great Principle (Mahat), grant me a beautiful dawn. || 21 ||

May the seven oceans, the seven principal mountain ranges, the seven purposes, and the supreme continents—beginning with the seven worlds starting from Bhūḥ—may they all bring about a beautiful dawn for me. (23)
Thus, at dawn, whoever remembers, recites, or listens with devotion to this excellent and wonderful [account], [attains the fruit]. // 23 //
May this dawn be auspicious and may evil dreams be destroyed through the grace of the Blessed One, O Truth! (24)
He who recites in the morning this work called *Suprabhāta*, which is dear to the Blessed One, shall become the presiding lord of all states and attain liberation. || 25 ||
If one is capable and pure, then by reciting the Dharma of the Blessed One, being liberated from all calamities, one shall become identical with Nārāyaṇa. || 26 ||
Having gone outside for the purpose of voiding urine and so forth,
he should then perform the cleansing of his teeth with a twig of the *khadira* tree.
Or, if one desires supreme good fortune, one should perform [the rite] with Apāmārga;
then, being composed, one should bathe in a river or in a lake. (28)
Having wiped his body with either wet or dry [cloths], he should then perform the twilight worship (saṃdhyopāsti), which destroys the entire flood of sins. (29)
He who, having abandoned the twilight worship (saṃdhyopāsti), performs [other] actions, is a Śūdra indeed; he is excluded from all Brahminical duties.
Because they are liberated for a long time, the sages become possessed of all-encompassing longevity;
Sāvitrī is the mother of all sciences and the supreme art.
Having thus worshipped her in every way, one should practice the meditation on the Vidyā;
he who recites the Gāyatrī, the mother of the Vedas, a thousand times—32.
O sons of Brahmā, know that this was produced from Vasiṣṭha;
one should recite it daily a thousand times, or perhaps five hundred.
The wise one should recite four hundred times, or three hundred, or always recite one hundred and twenty-eight times. (34)
The best of practitioners should daily perform one hundred and eight [recitations];
one should know such a person to be a Brāhmaṇa, a purifier in all rites. (35)
If one recites the Sāvitrī mantra two hundred times with devotion at a single session, he is called the most excellent of great men and the best of Brāhmaṇas. (36)
He who recites the Mother of the Vedas three hundred times at one time is called a sage by the wise; he is a purifier of the assembly and a protector.
Having daily practiced the four hundred [verses] of the Mother of the Vedas, that great sage is declared by the wise to be the most excellent among all the worlds. || 38 ||
If one who is pure should practice the *sāvitrī* five hundred times at a single sitting, he is called a great Brahmarṣi and is honored even by the gods. (39)
He who recites this Mother-mantra one thousand times at a single session is remembered as the Lord Nārāyaṇa himself in person. || 40 ||
He is indeed worshipped even by the Brahman-sages, such as Vasiṣṭha and others;
that purifier causes a thousand fallen ones to attain purification.
One should recite the Sāvitrī, the mother of the Vedas, either one thousand times, or three hundred, or four or five hundred, or two hundred, or even just one hundred times.

Having first performed the ritual assignment according to one's capacity, or else having offered a hand-gesture; or, having performed the recollection of the Mother-letters (mātṛkā) according to one's ability through silent recitation (ajapā)—43.

Having performed the Nārāyaṇī twilight devotion and having recited the auspicious and glorious eight-syllabled mantra according to one's capacity, one should then recite the hymn known as the Nārāyaṇa-sūkta.
Having heated it while facing the sun, piercing it once, twice, or even thrice—or five times on a Sunday—at the feet of one's own guru; || 45 ||
Having paid homage and propitiated the Fire, and having offered auspicious clarified butter twelve times with the Vedic mantras, one should subsequently offer it with the Śrīmadaṣṭākṣara-vidyā.
Having performed one hundred and eight oblations daily, or twenty-eight, he should then offer clarified butter with the Vaiṣṇava mantra dedicated to Vāsudeva.
Thereafter, one should offer clarified butter with the Śrī-dvādaśākṣarī mantra, or else with the Rājyalakṣmī mantra; or, according to some, with the [Śrīvidyā] mantra consisting of sixteen syllables.
Thereafter, one should offer twelve oblations with the Vidyā known as Rājarāja;
then ten or five oblations with the heart-mantras (hṛdaya) and the vyāhṛtis.
Having performed the oblation with the *brahmārpaṇa* mantra,
one should extinguish the fire upon the chest with the rays of the Goddess Śrī, using clarified butter as a single means, if one is capable.
Having repeatedly offered oblations of clarified butter with a ladle full of food,
one should offer it once more to the horse or to the preceptor while reciting the mantra beginning with "anākhya."
Then, having offered oblations to the Goddess Śrī with the fifteen-syllable mantra twenty-eight times, he should subsequently perform the rite with the Śrī-mantras.
Having offered even a single oblation with the vidyā known as Rājarāja,
one should offer twelve [oblations] with that [vidyā], and then offer with the vyāhṛtis.
Having restrained the vital breaths (prāṇāyāma) and being seated comfortably upon an easy seat,
one should utter the formal resolve for the recitation of the venerable eight-syllabled mantra.
Having performed the placement of the *chaṃda*, the *ṛṣi*, and so forth, one should then perform the entire series of placements (*nyāsa*);
or else, having placed the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), one should place the supreme Vaiṣṇava Mātṛkā.
Having performed the tenfold placement of the phonemes (varṇanyāsa) and thereafter having performed the Mātṛkānyāsa, which is the form of consciousness, one should meditate upon the Lord of Śrī.
One should recite the glorious eight-syllabled mantra (aṣṭākṣarī-vidyā) one thousand three hundred times,
or one thousand one hundred times, or even five hundred times.
One should recite four hundred, three hundred, two hundred, or one hundred [times] at evening,
at dawn, at midday, at the time of Brahmā (noon), or at night.
Even for one who has attained the state of Nārāyaṇa, there is the production of fruit through karma;
therefore, Nārāyaṇa is eternally remembered by the twice-born with devotion. (59)
Therefore, O you whose wealth is austerity, there is nothing more blessed in the world than the remembrance of Nārāyaṇa, which destroys sins and so forth. (60)
Even for one who has committed the acts of eating while fasting, urinating while standing, and so forth, this rite grants complete success;
even a killer of a Brahmin, a drinker of liquor, a thief, or one who violates the teacher’s bed [is purified].
Or, through contact with him, one becomes a destroyer of one's father and mother; therefore, having remembered Nārāyaṇa with great reverence, [one should act]. 62.
One who remembers Nārāyaṇa attains supreme peace, being liberated from heaps of sins; this is the highest gratification for those of dog-like conduct. 63.

Even those who are ineligible for [Vedic] rites and are tainted by sins do not remain without eligibility; they attain the supreme song, being liberated from heaps of sins through the remembrance of Nārāyaṇa. This is the Vedic statement regarding the four castes and the fifth [the *śūdras*].
The same applies to the *śruva* ladles as well. || 64 ||
The name of Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the primordial Brahman of Brahmā, the creator;
it is the eternal essence found within the Vedas and the Vedānta scriptures.
Even those born of the womb, by remembering the name of Śrī Nārāyaṇa at the beginning, having remembered it repeatedly,
shall abandon this body and attain the status of the twice-born.
Having subsequently become twice-born from the lotus-like mouth of the Noble One,
and having received the glorious eight-syllabled mantra, they attained an unsurpassed state.

Whatever state is attained by one chanting the glorious eight-syllabled mantra (aṣṭākṣarī-vidyā), even those who perform the Tulā-puruṣa sacrifice may reach that; what then need be said of the goal reached by seeing [the deity]? 68.
Even from the remembrance of Nārāyaṇa, humans attain the supreme goal;
however, the goal of the glorious eight-syllable mantra cannot be attained by those devoid of devotion.
This yogi Nārāyaṇa, dwelling in the midst of the Badarī forest, is known as the teacher of all worlds, whose soul is serene through the son of Dharma. (70)
At the time of saluting the ascetics, those desiring auspiciousness should here perform the worship of the illustrious eight-syllabled mantra for the sake of attaining the supreme goal.

Therefore, this eight-syllable mantra— which is a compendium of the Vedas, the Vedāṅgas, and the Vedānta— must necessarily be recited for the sake of attaining the status of a teacher and for the avoidance of the pit of hell.
Recitation that is non-Vedic is useless; giving and circumambulation are in vain;
the supreme Self is without a teacher, motionless, formless, and my very own, consisting of truth and bliss.
Stainless, without support, eternally pure, and eternal;

consisting of the four Vedas, the sun of the Word-Brahman (Śabdabrahman), and higher than the highest—the eight-syllabled mantra is the supreme reality to be expressed, whose essence is Brahman, as heard from the sacred revelation. (76)
Beyond the qualities (guṇas), yet the support of the qualities; worshipped by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva;
infinite, immovable, subtle, and beyond the reach of mind and speech. || 77 ||

Through the continuous practice of the venerable eight-syllabled mantra, the venerable eight-syllabled mantra becomes manifest; by reciting the venerable eight-syllabled mantra one hundred and eight times, it shines forth.
Day after day they are liberated even from sins such as the killing of a Brahmin;
one should daily join the supreme, glorious eight-syllabled mantra two hundred times.
By [the sins of] killing a Brahmin, drinking liquor, theft, violating the teacher’s wife, and by the accumulation of great sins such as the murder of father and mother; || 80 ||
One is liberated from the nets of minor offenses (upapātaka) and even from great sins committed in old age, youth, or childhood, while awake, dreaming, or in deep sleep. (81)
Even by those acts committed through mind, speech, or body born of ignorance, and by the nets of minor offenses (upapātaka) which are causes for attaining hell— || 82 ||
There is no doubt that he is liberated and attains the state of ultimate destruction;
one should constantly join the glorious eight-syllable mantra three hundred times. (83)
Whatever merit is found in all the Vedas, whatever fruit is found in all sacrifices, whatever is supreme among objects of veneration, and whatever fruit is found in all sacred fords; || 84 ||
Having obtained that inexhaustible fruit, he attains the supreme goal after death;
he who constantly recites the eight-syllabled Śrīvidyā four hundred times [attains this]. 85.
To him, the eight supernatural powers beginning with *aṇimā* always remain present;
likewise, the great goddess Lakṣmī, accompanied by wealth, grain, and other riches, remains steadfast.
Day after day, she indeed offered to him flowers that surpassed even the moon and the stars in brilliance. || 87 ||
Dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa are the fourfold aims of human life; there is no doubt that he alone is the performer of these—of this there is no uncertainty. (88)
Having constantly recited this supreme, glorious eight-syllabled mantra ending with "vam," one attains the unsurpassed sandals (pādukā) and other such supreme accomplishments (siddhis).
He inevitably attains sovereignty endowed with the qualities of the wish-fulfilling gem and other jewels; and the treasures, such as the Śaṅkha and others, remain at his disposal, never wavering.
And the servant of his tongue, the consort of Brahmā, expands there;
she protects him with great affection, just as Mahālakṣmī protects her son.
Having quickly become one who remembers his births, pure even at the time of death,
he is joined by twelve generations of his father’s, mother’s, and his own wife’s families.
At the end of his life, he indeed enters the abode of Hari;
being pure, he should recite more than a hundred thousand [names] every day.
The great yogin spoken of in the *Ṣaṣṭhaka* is the omnipresent Lord Nārāyaṇa himself;
he alone is called the ancient teacher and seer of the worlds.
Even by the mere sight of this [river], which purifies even the most sinful, one attains purification;
by conversing with those who have bathed there, the fruit of Agniṣṭoma shall be obtained.
Even those such as Mahendra and others, who are lords of the world in person, remain as servants;
so too do the Siddhas and even the Puruṣas. || 96 ||
Sages such as Viśvāmitra and others worship him;
even the gods, including Brahmā, Indra, and Yama, seek refuge in that destroyer of sins.
The Pārijāta and other trees, the herds of Kāmadhenu cows, and the mountains including the Pāriyātra—indeed, the great jewels and so forth dwell there. 98.
The goddess of liberation, Lakṣmī, dwells unswervingly in the lotus-hands of those born of that lineage; no doubt should be entertained in this matter. (99)
He alone is the Ordainer, Viṣṇu, and Śaṅkara-Parameśvara;
he alone is the performer of the world's actions and also its crusher. 100.
O Brahmins, constantly recite that very supreme eight-syllabled Śrī-mantra, which consists of one thousand three hundred [repetitions], and which liberates Hari, the Lord of the World. 101.
One who performs the Śrāddha daily shall obtain supreme merit;
it is not possible for me to describe its fruit, even with oceans, winds, mountains, and gods.
Having thus chanted the glorious eight-syllabled mantra day after day, as well as the great Vaiṣṇava six-syllabled vidyā of Vāsudeva; 103.
Then, having empowered it with the power of the Yakṣas, one should recite the twelve-syllable mantra of Rāśmāyā, or the Lakṣmī-hṛdaya-vidyā, or else the six-syllable Śrī-mantra. (104)
Or, for the eight-syllabled mantra of Mahālakṣmī, one should recite it one hundred and eight times.
If the practitioner is capable, he should do so daily; this brings about the attainment of prosperity and the destruction of the ten types of enemies.
Whether three hundred, two hundred, one hundred, or even fifty, or likewise twenty-eight times, he should recite [the mantra] after having purified his sins. || 106 ||
The sovereign queen of kings, the knowledge (vidyā) who sustains the beautiful creeper, the supreme Brahman-knowledge, the twenty-eighth [letter] of the Asurī-mātṛkā. || 107 ||
Thereafter, one should recite the *Lakṣmīnārāyaṇī* mantra one hundred and eight times, or indeed eight, ten, or twelve times. 108.
Whatever fruit is obtained from the daily recitation of the Vidyā known as Rājarāja for as many years as there are petals on a lotus,
that same fruit is obtained from the recitation of one hundred thousand times of the glorious eight-syllable Vidyā.
The sacrifice has been described in the scriptures by the ancient knowers of Brahman:
one should daily recite the great mantra of the Queen of Queens twenty-eight times.
