Having performed the propitiation of the limbs of this glorious eight-syllable Vidyā with the prescribed sacrificial fee,
one obtains the fruit of twenty-eight thousand recitations.
From the Vaidavārāyaṇa [tīrtha], which is numbered at twenty-eight, comes a fraction;
from the Mahādānas, numbered at twenty-eight, it is eight hundred thousandfold. (112)
O daughter of Brahmā, O king of kings, there is no doubt that one attains this great lore (mahāvidyā) daily through the constant practice of virtuous deeds. 113.
The fruit obtained from reciting the four Vedas in their entirety is attained by reciting this [text] twenty-eight times along with its ancillaries. 114.
By reciting [the mantra] ten times over the lineage of the great royal dynasty, one attains imperishability;
thus, O Vāma, one directly beholds the two who are measurable by Brahman at the gateway.
He is Nārāyaṇa himself, the omnipresent Lord, accompanied by the Sun;
likewise, he performed a thousand horse-sacrifices and ten thousand great gifts.
The section known as Bhūprādakṣiṇya-sahasrarājarāja-vidyā, along with the four Vedas, was weighed by Brahmā and found to be equal [in weight]. || 117 ||
Sundarī Vallabhā became the sovereign science (rājavidyā) superior to all kings;
she is known as Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā and Sundarīllābhā. (118)
The fruit of reciting [this] one hundred and eight times cannot be described even by hundreds of millions of lords of the kings of kings. (119)
O Brahmin, there is a purpose here: for the Queen of the Lord of Kings, having given birth, the impurity ceases immediately upon the death of the newborn. 120.
For him, there exists this fulfillment of the vow, even amidst suffering. || 120 ||

[Thus ends the thirty-fifth chapter, titled "The Majesty of Rājarāja-Āvadyā," in the latter portion of the *Śrīmad-anuttara-brahma-tattva-rahasya*, the *Dāśarathīya Tantra*, which is a compendium of the essential meaning of the Vedas.
The Blessed Lord said:
The sage of this [lineage] was Dharma, the son of Jarāsandha, a great yogi;
Sādhya was born from Nārāyaṇa, and the Lord Vibhu is omniscient. || 1 ||
Likewise Sammohana, Nandabhairava, Carvita, Gantau, Gayatram, Agayatra, and Daivata—these are the eight. || 2 ||
The great yogi, the all-pervading Lord who is the consort of Sundarī, has been described by Chaṇḍa;
the Lord is Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, beloved by the ancients.
For the sake of pleasing Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, this [work] has been brought forth by Niyoga;
there is neither *aṅganyāsa* nor *karanyāsa*, nor is there any other presiding deity (*aṅginī*).
In the past, she herself declared: "I am the supreme Kalā, the sovereign of the kings of queens, the supreme Vidyā consisting of the Parabrahman, Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇī. (5)
Or if one who is self-restrained and diligent remembers her constantly, for him I,
the great Śrī Sundarī, the beloved of the Blessed One, shall become a servant.
"O Vanmāra, may his dwelling be auspicious; thus has he been delivered from distress.
Thus did the Goddess Śrī sing this song upon hearing [the words] of the Lord of Śrī.
And you shall recite [the mantra] for a thousand horse-sacrifices with their complete sacrificial fees,
as well as for the enjoyment of the sovereignty of Mahāpura.
The Queen of the Kings of Kings, who is never to be forgotten, whether daily or even once,
is the imperishable cause for attaining the bliss of Brahmananda.
Preceded by the Ācārya-jñā [mantra], they obtained the Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā,
the glorious Aṣṭārṇa, and the fifteen-syllabled Śrī-vidyā.

O sons of Brahmā, even without the ritual placement (nyāsa) and even without the preliminary rite (puraścaryā), she becomes perfected for devotees, bestowing all spiritual accomplishments (siddhis). || 11 ||

Having understood the meter, the seer, and so forth, as well as the fivefold Brahman, the practitioner attains perfection by chanting the glorious eight-syllabled mantra, which bestows the power of the six syllables. || 12 ||
Having recited [the mantra] of Rājarājeśvarī at the two feet of her own preceptor,
she gave abundant sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā) consisting of wealth, grain, and other riches.
O son of Brahmā, even without the performance of *puraścaraṇa*,
one who has beheld the Śrīṣadṛṣṭākṣīrī [form] of Viṣṇu attains eternal perfection.
Beyond Vīrajāyā are Parepāpa and Sudhāma, the middle [worlds];
then Ratnadvīpa and Manoramya, where the assembly of swords is found at the end of Valāvu. || 15 ||
In the city of Ayodhyā, which was adorned with divine palaces and surrounded by rows of celestial sandalwood trees that were like wish-fulfilling trees, (he dwelt). 16.
It was situated many yojanas away, shining with palaces free from poison,
extending for many yojanas, and filled with all manner of delights.

In that pavilion situated in the midst of it, which was filled with those eternally liberated ones and surrounded by hosts of Siddhas and Sādhyas, and adorned with the blossoming flowers of the *taptajā* tree (the flame-tree).
In its center, within that most enchanting place inlaid with nine rubies,
the splendor of a thousand rubies radiates forth.
There, in that pavilion made of wish-fulfilling gems, O Blessed One, the Lord was seated,
having been attended on all sides by the most excellent servants.
It was beautified at its four gates by Brahmavidyā, Maheśānī, and others,
and graced by Umā, Gaṇapati, Kṣetrapāla, and Bhairava.
Having adorned it on all sides with conchs,
weapons, and treasures, he placed him in the center upon a beautiful lion-throne situated at the foot of a Pārijāta tree, which was set with the nine gems and embellished with refined gold.
There he saw the Great-Souled One seated, with a complexion as dark as the color of a black cloud.
Resembling ten million gods of love, with a beautiful face and four arms,
he wore a magnificent crown of gold set with the nine precious gems.
Her forehead was adorned with a beautiful tilaka mark, decorated with curved locks of hair;
her large eyes were like lotuses, and her eyebrows were like the bow of the God of Love. (25)
He was like a hundred rising suns, adorned with two *kunda* flowers,
possessing a smiling face and large eyes, and resembling a pomegranate tree with ten excellent teeth.
With a neck like a conch and a broad chest, adorned with saffron unguents, he was beautified by jeweled rings and a pearl necklace. || 27 ||

His chest was adorned with the Kaustubha gem, he was resplendent with a forest garland, his hands held the conch, the discus, the gesture of fearlessness, and the gesture of granting boons, and his breast bore the Śrīvatsa mark.
The all-pervading Lord, shining like lightning, wearing yellow garments,
seated in the vīrāsana posture, and the bestower of boons upon the most excellent of beings.
In Nārāyaṇa, who is intent on the welfare of the world, equal to Śrī, and infallible (acyuta),
he who protects from fear sits upon his left lap as a couch.
Mahālakṣmī, the mother of the world, whose splendor was established by her own deeds,
shone like ten million flashes of lightning and was enveloped in a pair of excellent garments.
Her head was covered by a crown set with nine rubies,
and her forehead was adorned with a tilaka of musk shining like a king of swans.
With her curly locks adorned with divine garlands, her limbs smeared with celestial sandalwood paste, she possessed eyes as long as lotus petals. || 33 ||
Her eyes were adorned with collyrium at the corners, her gaze like the petals of a blue lotus,
and she was decorated with golden earrings set with pearls as large as śukra fruits.
Adorned with jewels, pearls, and gold, provided with a pair of bracelets, joined with the staff of Yama, and equipped with a waistband and ornaments. || 35 ||
With a face resting [in composure], large-eyed, and with a countenance radiant as the full moon, she was exquisitely adorned with lips as beautiful as the fruit of the *kavī* tree.
Her teeth were adorned with rows as brilliant as diamond-seeds of the pomegranate;
her neck was graced with pearl necklaces, and her feet and other limbs were likewise decorated. || 37 ||
Four-armed, with a garland from a golden pitcher shining in her radiant hands, she is auspicious and adorned with golden cintāmaṇi jewels and other ornaments. || 38 ||
Adorned with bracelets, armlets, and jeweled ornaments,
her breasts were well-rounded, pure, and resembled golden jars.
She has a slender waist, adorned with a large, deep navel resembling a whirlpool;
she is graced by thighs as delicate as the pillars of a lotus stalk.
Adorned with golden anklets and finger-rings,
illuminated by precious ornaments, she was the bringer of universal sovereignty.
The sovereign lady of the city of Ayodhyā, the Mother of the Universe, the Greatly Auspicious Goddess Surī, is the consort of the Lord of Śrī in the south. (42)
The Mistress of the Universe possesses the splendor of a thousand rising suns, resembles the hibiscus flower, and is like a great ruby of deep crimson. 43.
Wearing divine jewels and garments, anointed with divine sandalwood paste,
she holds a sugarcane in her left hand and a noose and goad in her radiant hands.
Adorned with necklaces, earrings, bracelets,
and rings, she was endowed with a golden girdle-string and a bodice set with excellent gems.
Adorned with a golden crown set with the nine gems,
wherever that large-eyed lady was, she shone, beautified by her earrings.
Adorned with a necklace of pearls and gems, she was graced by a well-rounded pair of breasts resembling golden jars. || 47 ||
She is the embodiment of auspicious knowledge, the sovereign of the lion-throne, the enchantress of all, and the one who brings all worlds under her control. 48.
The deity who attracts the three worlds is worshipped by the multitude;
she is renowned as the fulfiller of desires and is praised by the wise. 49.
Surrounded by the divine powers such as Tripurā and Tripureśī,
she whose lotus feet are to be worshipped by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, and Indra.
The three powers, Lakṣmī, and the youthful Vāmabhagā are being praised;
she whose womb is the source of the Vedas is like lightning, resembling a thousand suns.
She holds a citron, a rosary, a lotus, and a golden water-pot;
she wears divine yellow garments and is adorned with a crown and other ornaments. || 52 ||
Adorned with a golden cintāmaṇi jewel, she was preceded by divine showers;
she was draped in divine garlands and cloths, and embellished with divine fragrances.
Her face was graced by the chewing of betel-leaf,
and she was adorned with a pair of eyes resembling those of a king of peacocks.
With golden earrings adorned by two earrings,
her beautiful face radiant with a gracious smile, she was like a blooming lotus.
Adorned with a girdle shining like a streak of lightning and set with jewels and pearls,
she possessed beautiful breasts resembling golden jars filled with nectar.
Adorned with pure pearls and a beautiful cloak of auspicious gems,
she was decorated with finger-rings, armlets, and divine bracelets.
She is Gaurī, Lakṣmī, and Mahāvārṇā; she is the personified Mother of the Vedas.
She is the embodiment of the powers of will, knowledge, and action, adorned with the supreme covering of the *kañcuka*s.
Adorned with rings, armlets, and divine bracelets,
she is the Mother of the Vedas, whose form consists of the powers of will, knowledge, and action, and who is the Supreme Form.
Her lotus feet are served by Brahmā, Rudra, Maheśa, and others;
she possesses the form of the three deities, she is the embodiment of the three Vedas, and she consists of the triple Veda itself.
She is the form of the three worlds and the one whose form is the three worlds; she is the triple Veda (Trayī) and the power (Śakti) of the Youth (Yauśa);

she is the supreme form and the form of the Lord (Patyu). She is the form of the three worlds, consisting of the triple Veda, the threefold energy (Triśakti), Lakṣmī, the Fortune of Sovereignty (Sāmrājyalakṣmī), the Sustainer of the Universe (Viśvaṃbhara), and the Threefold One (Triyā).

The two goddesses Nīlā and Mahī, who are auspicious to the three worlds and adorned with divine ornaments, hold a pair of chowries made of white and yellow threads in their left and right hands respectively.
With divine chowries in their hands, O Vimaladya, they are exceedingly compassionate;
they are endowed with divine ornaments and clothed in divine garlands and garments.
Behind Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of the worlds, whose eyes are as broad as lotuses, stand the auspicious goddesses with smiling lotus-faces. (63)
On both sides of the Lord of the Elements were Gaurī and Vāṣṇī, the two Savitṛs;
the all-pervading Lord was golden-hued, raining down jewels, and possessed a supreme white parasol.
Viṣṇu, accompanied by Lakṣmī, stood at the rear portion, the protector of the world;
the four Vedas in embodied form were stationed in his four directions.
The Lord, the Master of the Universe, consisting of sacrifice and all-pervading,
shines resplendent before him, accompanied by the Goddess of Imperial Sovereignty.
The sacrificial rites, joined with the sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā), embodied and consisting of the three Vedas, shine before him, assuming divine forms; thus it is said.
Accompanied by the goddess Mahāśrīsundarī and Mahālakṣmī, joined with the three powers (triśakti) and Lakṣmī, and endowed with the blue ground (nīlābhūmi). || 68 ||
He praised the Supreme Lord, the Master of the worlds, who was accompanied by his primary queen Vimalā and other consorts,
and who was being extolled by the four forms [of Brahmā].
It was adorned by the four directions with the illustrious Vāsudeva and others,
and was served by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, Indra, and the immortals.
He is surrounded by Ananta, Vihaga, Īśa, Vidya, Kona, and others;
he is the lord of all sacrifices, the immediate reality, the lord of the worlds, and the infallible Acyuta.
The supreme, all-pervading Puruṣa, situated within the solar orb, abiding in the midst of the lunar orb, and stationed in the center of the fiery orb.
I bow to Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of the World, the infinite Supreme Lord, whose form is truth, bliss, and consciousness, and who is established beyond the veil of darkness.
Upon his own body, the yogi should meditate on the Lord of Śrī as the object of meditation; with an upward gaze, he should contemplate the all-pervading Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of Śrī.

We take refuge in Hari, who is like refined gold adorned with the luster of excellent jewels, whose face is most beautiful, who is clothed in choice garlands, who commands Yama and others, and who is eternally peaceful, rich with a mass of hands shimmering in the sky, and possessing half of Lakṣmī. || 75 ||
The Yoginī, her limbs adorned with various ornaments, sits in a yogic posture; she holds a golden lotus with a stalk as beautiful as a mountain. 76.
O lotus-eyed Mahendra, we take refuge in Śama, Niśā, and Hara, who possess a garland of flames and are like a lotus. || 77 ||

We worship Him whose neck is adorned with rubies and pearls, who wears excellent garlands perfumed with sandalwood paste, and whose limbs are truly radiant, decorated with a crown and the discus; we worship Him who is the very abode of Lakṣmī.

I take refuge in Hari, the Great-Souled Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of Lakṣmī, the King of Kings, the Sovereign of the Goddesses—who holds in his hands a mirror, a conch, a lotus, and a rosary; who is adorned with a crown and other ornaments; whose body is like refined gold; who is praised by the lords of the gods; and who dwells eternally within the lotus of the heart.
By reciting the Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā even once, or daily, one obtains the auspicious fruit of the *puraścaryā* for all vidyās whatsoever. (80)
Having attained freedom from all sins upon hearing auspicious dreams,
and having obtained all blessings, he becomes a possessor of the perfection of union with Brahman.
One should worship the Preceptor alone, or Nārāyaṇa accompanied by Śrī, who is the Supreme Lord himself in embodied form.
One who possesses this great vidyā of the king of kings attains all perfections;
it is eternal and the cause of sovereignty over the three worlds. (83)
May the Queen of the Kings of Kings be eternally devoted to her own Nārāyaṇa;
this Sūkta of meditation is for you both, out of respect. 84.
This hymn, which destroys all sins and bestows the fruits of all ancient [rites],
should be recited daily with undivided devotion, or one should meditate upon it.
Having attained great perfection, he reaches the state of the Blessed One.

[Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter, titled "The Science of the King of Kings," in the latter portion of the *Śrīmadanuttarabrahmatattvarahasya*, the *Dāśarathīya Tantra*, which is a compendium of the essential meaning of the Vedas.
The Blessed Lord said:
I shall describe the method of worship for the benefit of those who possess the discus;
by following the procedure taught by me, O Yāmya, a person shall become liberated while living.
Having risen during the *brāhma-muhūrta* and recollected the feet of the Guru,
he then received the twelve-syllable mantra of Śrī Śrīsā from the Brahma-vidyā.
Having recited the *Raśmimālā-manusmṛti* here—whether in three, five, ten, or twenty-one ways—immediately thereafter, one should recite the *Suprābhāta-mahāstotra*. || 3 ||
O Śakti, at dawn,
recite with victory the divine, indestructible, and adamantine armor (kavaca) known as Nārāyaṇa, which is composed of Nārāyaṇa himself.
Whether at dawn, or in the morning, or at midday, or in the evening, or even at midnight, having approached [the deity] preceded by the conduct of the teacher (ācārya). || 5 ||

Having recited [this] there, one is liberated from all obstacles caused by vidyās and spirits; even by the dance of the gods, one attains great accomplishment that is difficult even for the three worlds to obtain.
Beyond that is the Raśmi Sūkta;
having recollected even once the fifteen-syllable Śrīsūkta, [one attains success]. || 7 ||
Having recited [the mantra] twenty-eight times, the practitioner should go outside;
then, having performed purification, bathed, and subsequently performed the twilight devotions (saṃdhyā).

Having completed the daily fire-oblation (nityahoma), he then bowed again to the sandals of the preceptor with palms joined in reverence, and [recited] the auspicious, glorious eight-syllabled mantra.
One should daily recite [the mantra] preceded by the ritual placement (nyāsa), one thousand three hundred times;
or alternatively, one thousand, five hundred, or even four hundred times according to the Atharva Veda.
One should always recite three hundred [times], or auspiciously one hundred and eight;
otherwise, there is no doubt that one will experience a downward course. || 11 ||
Having recited the twelve-syllable mantra of Vāsudeva, the six-syllable mantra of the Earth,
and the six-syllable mantra of Śrī according to one's capacity, one should then recite the twelve-syllable mantra of Śrī.
Or else, one should daily recite the fifteen-syllable Mahālakṣmī mantra one hundred and eight times, or twenty-one times.
One should recite the fourfold Lakṣmī-vidyā ten or twelve times;
the Rājeśvarī-vidyā and the Mahāsiṃhāsaneśvarī eight times.

One should daily recite one hundred and twenty-eight times, or twenty-eight times, or even three times; this is declared as the constant practice for the seeker of the Lakṣmī-vidyā. Alternatively, at the time of the Brāhma-muhūrta, one should meditate upon the sandals of the Guru.
Then, having recited the Brahmavidyā, as well as the Gāyatrī and the Mālāmantra,
he bathed, performed his twilight devotions (saṃdhyā), and then [recited] the auspicious and glorious eight-syllabled mantra.
The wise declare that the Vāsudeva Mahāvidyā, the Vaiṣṇava six-syllabled mantra, should be recited preceded by the nyāsa, or even without the nyāsa. (17)
Then, having consecrated according to one's capacity the twelve-syllable *kamalā* mantra, or having recited the *lakṣmī-hṛdaya-vidyā* one hundred and eight times; 18.
One should recite the Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā at the end of every sixteenth part of the day; having thus obtained the Śākta power, one should daily recite the mantra of the Blessed One.
Having recollected [the deity], having performed the twilight worship (saṃdhyā),
and having completed the daily fire-oblation (nityahoma), one should [recite] the supreme, glorious eight-syllabled mantra.
Having performed the six-limbed Mātṛkā-nyāsa preceded by the Keśava-nyāsa, one should mark [the body] with the Mātṛkā syllables and necessarily recite them every day. (21)
If one is unable even for this, then, having assigned the Vedic meters to the limbs of the deity,
one should daily practice the illustrious eight-syllabled mantra (Aṣṭākṣarī-vidyā) preceded by the command of the preceptor.
One should recite [the mantra] one thousand three hundred times every day;
or alternatively, one may recite five hundred, three hundred, or four hundred times.
Or, one should recite the *Lakṣmīhṛdaya-vidyā* twelve hundred times, or one hundred and eight times, according to one's capacity. (24)
The Queen of the Kings of Kings may become deluded by greatness.
O twice-born ones, by the daily recollection of the Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā,
one obtains a fruit equal to a thousand recitations of the Bhāgavadrashmisūkta.
One who knows a hundred thousand repetitions of the glorious eight-syllable mantra likewise obtains the fruit daily upon this earth; there is no doubt in this matter. (28)
Śrī Rāma.
O sons of Ānanda, I shall now declare the armor-mantra (varma) whose essence is Nārāyaṇa;
by reciting which daily, an intelligent person becomes attainable to Nārāyaṇa. (29)
The seer is Nāsiyaṇa-yogī, the son of Dharma, the Lord of the World;
the divine Gāyatrī is the meter; Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa is the deity. 30.
The Supreme Self, the Great Yogi, is proclaimed as the deity;
he who is born from the pair of lotuses [the eyes], dwelling in the heart and upon the chest.
One should place the glorious eight syllables of the mantra upon the face and the head; starting from the head down to the feet, one should likewise place the twelve-syllable mantra.
One should always place all the fingers, starting with the index finger, extended and emerging from the base of the thumb. || 33 ||
O Vāsudeva, one should place the syllables of the Great Knowledge (mahāvidyā) on the joints;
as before, one should place those beginning with the Praṇava at the bottom, ending with the word "Jñānam. (34)
Having placed *kāraṃ* in the heart, one should place *avikāraṃ* on the head;
likewise, one should place *ṣavaṇaṃ* between the eyebrows and *ṇakṣā* on the crest-lock (*śikhā*).

One should place the syllable *ve* upon the pair of eyes, the syllable *na* on the two hands, and the syllable *ma* as the weapon; having thus assigned these along with the *visarga*, one performs the six-limbed (*ṣaḍaṅga*) ritual.
That person, consisting of the essence of Nārāyaṇa, becomes the embodiment of the mantra;
he should meditate upon the Lord, the Master of the Universe, within the lotus of his own heart. || 37 ||
Having emitted the weapon-mantra *kārāṃ sarvasaṃcīrṇamakāram* along with its six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*),
that wise man should meditate upon the God of gods, the Lord of the universe, within the lotus of his heart.

He is to be meditated upon always as Nārāyaṇa, seated in the midst of the solar disc, resting upon the lotus-born Brahmā; adorned with armlets, makara-shaped earrings, a crown, and a necklace, he possesses a beautiful form and holds the conch and the discus.
Or one should meditate upon the all-pervading Nārāyaṇa, who is the Lord of Śrī as half of his body.
Her two hands trembled as she held the lotus, conch, and discus; she fell into a state of fear, her lightning-like luster fading like a mere fragment of a cloud.
With her left hand, she incessantly pressed against his lofty breast in an embrace, while her right hand clung to his body in a single, unified gesture of longing.
O lotus-eyed one, [you are] Lakṣmī. || 40 ||
This great mantra of the Triṣṭubh meter, proclaimed as a verse for meditation, [should be recited] while walking, standing, sleeping, sitting, or even while awake. (41)

Even while laughing, if one remembers this verse on meditation, one surely attains great fame; [so too does] the Queen of the Lords of Kings [attain it] in rites such as the recitation of mantras and fire-offerings. 42.
By performing rites such as the recitation and fire-offerings of the glorious eight-syllabled mantra (aṣṭākṣarī-vidyā),
and by meditating well while remembering this mantra, one attains the corresponding perfection.

Or else, one should meditate upon Nārāyaṇa, who is unassailable, accompanied by his Śakti, consisting of all knowledge and the splendor of fire; then, being self-restrained, one should recite the Nārāyaṇī armor-vidyā.
Oṃ.

O Hari, meditate upon me for my complete protection; He whose lotus feet are placed upon the head of the subduer of Yati, who possesses eight arms, and who holds a bow, arrows, a shield, a sword, a mace, a conch, and nooses. 45.

May He in the form of a fish protect me from the waters; may the foot of Varuṇa protect me from the hosts and from the noose; may Vāmana protect me on earth from the illusion of Māyā; and may Viśvarūpa protect me in the sky.
The dust raised by the hooves of his horses, thick as the waters of the ocean, spread through the quarters of the sky;
and as he advanced with his army, the rays of the sun, though piercing, were obscured by it.
May that Boar, who is the embodiment of sacrifice, who was raised up by his own power, and who bears the earth upon his tusk, protect me while I am intoxicated;
may he, together with Lakṣmaṇa, stand before me like Rāma on Mount Citrakūṭa, accompanied by Sītā.
May Nārāyaṇa protect me from the harsh desert of dharma; may Nara protect me from that [desert]; therefore, may Varāha protect me in yoga;
may the Brahmin [Dattātreya] protect me from the hair and so forth; may Sanatkumāra protect me with his splendor; and may Kapila, the elder brother, protect me.
Because of the bondage of karma. || 49 ||

May Sanatkumāra protect me from the god of love; may this Śeṣa protect me from the offense against the gods on the path; may the Lord of the gods protect me from the forest fires; and may Hari deliver me entirely from all hells.

The Blessed One Vanvantari, whose nature is fire, who has conquered his self like an elephant from the fear of a thorny path, protects the world from the end of the age through sacrifice; and the hosts of gods, free from internal strife, [protect] this embodied world from the power of anger.
May the blessed Dvaipāyana, who has awakened from the delusion of the multitude of heretics and risen above them,
go forth to protect the Dharma through his extensive incarnation during this impure age of Kali.
Keśava, pleased, struck me with his mace at the time of dawn in Vidarbha;
Nārāyaṇa, possessing great power, spoke thus at midday while seated upon a throne.

May the divine Mādhava, who is honey-sweet and fierce with the downpour of grain, protect me in the afternoon; may he, the Lord of the three abodes, protect me at midnight and at dawn, even when alone and without a protector, rejoicing amidst the faults of the night.

May the Lord Janārdana, whose abode is the Śrīvatsa mark, who is the supreme beyond the other [worlds], the joyful Lord, the Siddha, Dāmodara, the All-pervading, the Lord of the Universe, the Blessed One in the form of Time, grant us prosperity at dawn. 55.
O Discus, with its rim blazing like the fire at the end of an eon, revolving on all sides and endowed with the three-fold splendor,
burn, burn the enemy army quickly, just as fire, aided by the wind, consumes dry grass.
O Lord of the Earth, O you whose sparks are intangible, O Unconquered One, crush, crush the enemies who have seized my beloved;
grind to powder the Pāṇḍavas, Nāyakas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Bhūtas, and Grahas. 57.
May you protect us from the Dhānas, Pramathas, Pretas, Mātṛs, and Piśācas who have terrible fangs and are seized by madness;
and may you, O Bhīma, whose roar fills the quarters and who stands unshakable at the heart of the enemy host, destroy the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas.
O Lord, you who are the source of the forest of arrows, being employed by me, cut through my enemies' vital organs;
destroy the eyes of those who wish to harm us, and take away the evil sight of our foes.

Having eaten from both [the householders and] you, O King, he eats with freedom from fear from all beings— whether they be those with fangs, those that cause terror, or those that devour— at home and abroad.
O Lord, by the chanting of Your names, may these serpents who obstruct our welfare go to their immediate destruction. || 61 ||
May Garuḍa— the Lord who is the essence of the meters, the destroyer of pride, the stambhana (paralyzer), and the master—
protect us from all remaining hardships and misfortunes by means of his own names.
The names of all the weapons of Hari, which are devoid of form, are the intellect, the senses, the mind, and the vital breaths, while His attendants are His ornaments. (63)
Just as the Blessed One alone is, by his very nature, both existent and non-existent, may we all be protected from calamities by this truth. 64.

Just as one's own self is free from conceptual constructions regarding the experiences of the three times, so too does it assume powers known as ornaments, weapons, and signs through its own nature. 65.
By that very truth, may the omniscient Lord Hari protect [us] with all His forms, with all His powers, and with all His movements.
The Blessed One has arrived here from all directions— the intermediate points, the cardinal points, above, below, and within—
dispelling the fear of the world with his roar, having swallowed up all other splendors with his own majesty.
Oṃ. This Bhāṇḍa consists of twenty-three verses;
it is the form of the Ekaviṃśati-stotra, which bestows splendor. (68)
This armor, whose essence is Nārāyaṇa, should be recited aloud; it bestows its fruit, destroys all accumulated sins, and annihilates every obstacle. (69)
It bestows the fruit of all sovereignty, is always free from the fear of poverty, removes all calamities, and grants the fruits of all branches of knowledge. (70)
This divine Vaiṣṇava hymn, which removes ignorance and bestows the fruit of the four goals of human existence, grants victory everywhere.
On an auspicious day, during the bright fortnight and at a favorable time,
one should first go before the pair of feet of the preceptor.
Having worshipped with various offerings, including garments and excellent ornaments,
as well as female and male servants, elephants, horses, and so forth, he indeed [attained] the auspicious Vaiṣṇava armor.
By obtaining [this] through the grace of the teacher, one shall be eternally victorious;
[one obtains] the supreme eight-syllabled mantra, which is the beloved of the gods and the bestower of glory.
With palms joined in reverence, he first [received] from the lotus-face of his preceptor the Vaiṣṇava six-syllabled great mantra of Vāsudeva.
Having taken that [skin], this supreme leather must be grasped;
she is Nārāyaṇa and Nārāyaṇī, the supreme one who embodies all the deities. (76)
The great vidyā known as Kavaca bestows the prosperity resulting from recitation;
this Vaiṣṇava armor is indeed a compendium of the Vedas and Vedānta.
The son, the Lord of the World, [praised] Nārāyaṇa, the supreme dharma of the great yogis, which brings glory, bestows auspiciousness, grants eternal victory, and confers perfection. || 78 ||
Having previously perceived this knowledge, he bestowed it, which grants all perfections, upon Brahmā, Śaṅkara,
and Vivasvat.
O Brahman, the venerable Bhāradvāja, the son of Brahmā, instructed Nārada, the best of divine sages, regarding the sin of killing a living being.
Having become liberated while living by means of this knowledge which bestows its fruit,
he then gave it to Prahlāda, the son of Hiraṇyakaśipu.

By the power of this very [goddess], the son of Prahrāda, the venerable Bali, though subject to poison, weapons, fire, and the like, attained eternal victory without ever being slain by the sons of Diti. (84)
Having performed penance for twelve years, you, the all-pervading Lord, gave the *Nārāyaṇa-ātman* to your disciple; though you are the devourer of the world, you remain the Self within yourself. 85.
The highly illustrious Viśvarūpa gave it to Viśvasūpa;
having been requested many times in the past, he bestowed it upon Maheśaya. (86)
By the power of Maheṃdra, having conquered the Suganas in battle, he attained the royal glory of the worlds of Nārāyaṇa. || 87 ||
Having sown universal sovereignty and Lakṣmī endowed with excellent qualities, the Lord,
having abandoned the envy of this [world], shines forth with glory.
From the teacher Rohāta, I incurred a terrible sin even greater than the thousandfold murder of a Brahmin; thus, like Śrī Rāma, I have fallen.
By the grace of Vācaspati, O leader of the Kāyāras, he performed a thousand horse-sacrifices with complete sacrificial fees.
Thus, for the king of the gods, there occurred a further decline in his prosperity;
at times he was overcome by the Daityas and Dānavas, and though he had lost his fortune, he regained his splendor once more.
Furthermore, according to the scriptures of Svāyaṃbhuva and others, this [decline] was due to the sin of Brahmin-slaughter.
The expiation for the murder of an Ācārya, a Vidyādhara, or a Guru, as well as for drinking liquor, is ten thousand [repetitions of the mantra] or [the performance of] a sacrifice. || 95 ||
Whether one is guilty of stealing gold or violating the teacher’s bed, the penance prescribed in the Dharmaśāstras beginning with those of Manu is declared in the Śruti. (96)
Whether I have spoken a falsehood to my teacher, or performed a forbidden act even once, or failed to perform what was required—even through ten thousand great gifts, I am not purified. (97)
This is true, this is the truth; there is no cause for doubt here.
Therefore, this purpose must necessarily be accomplished by you through action, thought, and speech. (98)
One who is self-controlled should always worship the boundary-mark (sīman) with great care;
he is indeed the Creator who bestowed [it] upon his own descendants. 99.
Brahmā taught his sons, Sanatkumāra and others of great majesty,
the Nārāyaṇī-vidyā, which brings about the highest prosperity.
Vasiṣṭha, the son of Brahmā, will tell it to his disciple Sūtra;
Nārāyaṇa, the great yogin, will be his son.
The great-souled Veda-vyāsa is named Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana;
his [spiritual] son is the Lord Śambhu, the master Mūrti of the right side.
O Ānanda, there will be one named Śuka who increases joy; I bow with reverence to him and to the great sages, such as Śaunaka and others, who are dear to me. (103)
Yoga will teach this knowledge to you;
therefore, all those highly wise ones shall know this knowledge by the name Ākha.
I bow to Śrutānanda-vardhana, the best among those who know the auspicious smile;
by Śukācārya himself, knowledge was made manifest upon the earth. 105.
Having studied this Vidyā, the Lord Śaṅkara, the Supreme Sovereign, became the Blessed Śiva after effecting the destruction of Tripura and other enemies. (106)
Then, having attained omniscience, he bestowed upon the youth the Raudra-mantra, which conquers the three worlds and is irresistible even by fate.
By the power of her who has conquered the stars, the son of Īśvara was born;
through the grace of her feet, he became a teacher on earth by the study of this [text]. 108.
O best of the twice-born, liberation may be attained in a single birth through the practice of great yoga,
or even during the transit of the sun.
On the eleventh day, or else keeping the command of the preceptor foremost in mind,
one should recite the venerable Aṣṭākṣarī-vidyā more than five hundred times.
Having become purified, one should recite the great mantra of Vāsudeva a thousand times in a secluded place, as well as the six-syllable mantra beginning with "apiśana."
Having recited the twelve-syllabled Śrīvidyā one hundred and eight times, and having recited the eighteen-syllabled Vidyā three hundred times, the wise man [attains success]. 112.
Then, having recited the mantra of Rājarājeśvarī one hundred and eight times,
and thereafter having recited this vidyā one hundred and eight times.
The wise one should recite the mantra forty-one times according to the rules over the consecrated fire, preceded by the command of his own preceptor.
Having offered five hundred oblations of clarified butter with the glorious eight-syllable vidyā,
one should offer one hundred and eight oblations with the vidyā of Vāsudeva.
Subsequently, he performed the *vaidyavyā* rite twenty-eight times with ghee,
using the twenty-one mantras of Śrīpati Avarmaṇ.
Having offered clarified butter twelve times with the fivefold *ghe-tana* mantra,
one should offer it one hundred and eight times with the twelve-syllable *vidyā*.
Having offered oblations twenty-eight times with the *rājarājā* mantra,
and having offered oblations twenty-eight times with the *prāyaścitti* mantra, he is purified.
Having performed the oblation dedicated to Brahmā with the Mahāvyāhṛtis,
the wise man, having prostrated like a staff with all eight limbs before the pair of feet of the Guru, [should proceed].
Having respectfully honored the preceptor with garments, ornaments, and gold,
one should offer food and wealth at his two feet.
One should offer half of that, or half of that again, or even three *niṣkas*;
then one should honor the preceptor with garments, ornaments, and woolen cloths.
Even twelve Brāhmaṇa women who lived on alms-food attained perfection through the grace of the Teacher; of this there is no doubt. (122)
Then one should constantly recite the *Jayonnati* mantra five hundred times in three ways;
by this, all diseases are destroyed and one becomes as powerful as a staff-bearer.
A science equal to this is difficult to find in all the three worlds, whether in a hermitage or in a forest crowded with tigers. 124.
O Lion among the Jagā, O Great Tiger! In times of distress, in the peril of malevolent spirits, and in the danger posed by Brahmarākṣasas, Vetālas, Yakṣas, and Kūṣmāṇḍas. (125)
Having recited just once this auspicious Vaiṣṇava Vedic armor (kavaca),
one who is thus liberated attains eternal freedom from all fear.
Wherever this auspicious Vaiṣṇava armor is constantly recited, the defects arising from the house, the planets, and the like, as well as those resulting from past actions, [are destroyed]. (127)
O twice-born ones, even extremely severe diseases caused by wind, bile, phlegm, and blood,
as well as fatal omens, perish through the recitation of this armor-mantra.
In that mass of water difficult to cross, that very water becomes like dry land;
even lions act like deer, and the lords of serpents act like necklaces.
Whether in a forest or at the edge of a mountain, surrounded by a forest fire;
or oppressed by bandits, or even being devoured by enemies. (130)
By the king, enraged and intent on killing or binding him, he was either whirled about by the wind or submerged in the great ocean. (131)
O twice-born ones, by remembering me, whose essence is Nārāyaṇa, even once,
one immediately attains victory and is liberated from all perils.
If one has lost all one's possessions or even one's life, having recited this five times during the two occasions of choosing one's own preceptor, [one is liberated]. || 133 ||
Or, having given whatever wealth one possesses, one may depart from there;
thereafter, the king shall become his slave, even at the cost of his life and his riches.
Constantly reciting it one hundred thousand times over fifteen days with diligence,
he attained the power of a thousand gods and performed auspicious daily recitations.

Having become a debtor [to the Lord] at his own will, one surely attains the supreme goal, as well as long life, great health, sovereignty, and the supernatural powers such as atomization (aṇimā) and the rest. || 136 ||
It grants death at one's own will, the recollection of past births, great majesty,
liberation from the three [worlds], and even the state of self-sovereignty.
There is no doubt regarding the greatness of this armor;
this Vaiṣṇava armor, known as the Vajrapañjara, is indeed a secret. (138)
Having recited [the mantra] daily, the practitioner, whose self is eternally pure, overcomes even immobile, mobile, artificial, and great poisons. (139)
Even the most intoxicating *hālāhala* poison that has entered his body becomes truly nectar and perishes; of this there is no doubt. (140)
There, even a mantra, a great yantra, or even a most dreadful magical rite (kṛtyā),
perishes upon entering that place, even if it has been incited by the foremost of the twice-born.
Having recited the fifteen kalās which are the essence of Bhava and Nārāyaṇa, there is no doubt;
being pure and alone, one should go forward with the face turned toward the village, [reciting] that which consists of the letters, the breaths, and the self. 142.
Having become the very essence of Nārāyaṇa, he encountered that army led by Mahiṣa in battle; having conquered his enemies, he was the destroyer of the foe.
The Yamaloka, Aprāṇa, and Panitara certainly do not go there;
the great enemies of the world continuously cause its destruction. 144.
Whether one is afflicted by great poverty or even struck down by a major disease,
by reciting this Vaiṣṇava armor-mantra, one shall indeed become filled with wealth, grain, and other riches.
Having attained all his heart's desires, he became one who remembered his past births for a long time, and he possessed unshakable prosperity, great majesty, and even sovereignty. || 146 ||

Having enjoyed all pleasures here in this world, one shall attain the state of Hari at the end. [The chapter on the purification of truth within the greatness of the Rājarājavidyā stands at the beginning of the excellent section on the essential meaning.]
The Blessed One said:
I shall now fully proclaim the sacrifice of the Great Vidyā, the Queen of Queens;
listen, all you yogis, who are united with Brahman and firm in your vows. || 1 ||
The King of Kings [should recite] the Great Vidyā constantly one hundred and eight times, or twenty-eight times, or even ten or twelve times. (2)
Having recited one thousand repetitions of the great mantra in a solitary place, and having subsequently recited once the mantra of the Lord, the Master of Śrī; || 3 ||
One should first perform the worship of the sacred seat (pīṭhapūjā) known as Ujjayinī, and then remember the thousand-syllable mantra of the Mother of the Goddess Śrī.
Having duly installed the Śrīcakra upon the great lion-throne,
and having first performed at least the worship of the limbs of dissolution (layāṅgapūjā), the knower of mantras should remain firm in his vow.
Afterwards, one should daily worship Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa, together with the Śālagrāma stone,
using fragrant flowers that bring prosperity, while honoring them with the Cakrarāja and other [Śālagrāma] stones.
At the time of the ninefold offering (navavedya), having carefully uttered "Bhama" for the venerable Goddess,
one should then recite the Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇī-vidyā, the Daśārāmā, the Lakṣmī-vidyā obtained from Bhūnolā, and the pair of mantras.
One should diligently learn from a preceptor the six-syllabled Vaiṣṇava mantra, "Vāsudevaṃ manuṃ," which is the vessel for the sacrificial oblation. || 10 ||
Having recited the *Rājarājeśvarī* mantra three times with devotion, and having recited the *Brahmavidyā* mantra over the *sālagrāma* stone, [he should worship]. (11)
Having invoked the divine couple Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa into the Cakrarāja,
one should offer twenty-four water-libations (arghas).
Having worshipped with the twelve-syllable mantra of Śrī-Śrīśa in five ways, one should then [recite] a hundred [times].
One should worship the pond with twenty-eight kinds of flowers offered by one's sons;
having performed this daily for a full year, one attains the state of being a Śambhu.
Whatever fruit one intends to attain, that very fruit one enjoys;
having first performed worship during the sacrifice of dissolution (layāga), one should thus worship with diligence.
One should exert effort daily for a thousand years of worship;
or else, having invoked the Lords of the World according to the previously mentioned procedure, [one should proceed].
Having worshipped with ritual services using the twenty-four names beginning with Keśava, he of firm vows offered oblations.
He constantly worshipped Keśava and the others with fifty pairs [of mantras];
thereafter, he worshipped Śrī and Śrīśa with the twelve-syllable mantra every single day.
One who worships Keśava with devotion once daily using pairs [of offerings] shall obtain every day the fruit of a thousand years of worship. || 20 ||
One should offer two [verses] to Keśava and Kīrti in pairs, or alternatively, one may offer them in three ways;
[this yields] the fruit of bathing in all sacred fords (tīrthas) and the fruit found in all sacrifices (kratūs). || 21 ||
Whatever merit exists in all forms of giving and whatever fruit exists in all forms of worship, one obtains that same fruit by undertaking this firm vow after death. 22.
One attains the recollection of past births and the eternal knowledge of Brahman; through the grace of the Daśikā, one directly attains the state of Nārāyaṇa. || 23 ||
Having first reverently worshipped the pair of sandals at the feet of the Teacher, Śrīpati then offered libations every day.

Having placed that pair of sandals at the aperture of Brahmā (Brahmavila), the practitioner, striving for the attainment of all goals, daily obtains the merit arising from the gift of ten million cows. || 25 ||
Having attained the fruit of the sciences and another eternal perfection, he possesses the most excellent King of Discuses (Cakrarāja) joined with the Śālagrāma stone. (26)
Having worshipped according to the prescribed rite with fragrant flowers and offerings,
he rejoices in the abode of the Blessed One together with thousands of his kinsmen.
In former times, Sundarī desired the fruit of the jujube tree for herself;
therefore, this sacred field of the Blessed One was declared by the sages to be like Lakṣmī.
Raṅgadhāma is a great sacred field (kṣetra), the beloved of the Self;
it is declared to be the field of the Lord of Lakṣmī, which immediately bestows all perfections.
The mountain named Añjanādri, known as Śrīnivāsa,
belongs to the Blessed Lord, the Consort of Śrī, whose very soul is his beloved Sundarī.
O Sundarī, even on the shore of the ocean, the sacred field of Puruṣottama belongs to Acyuta, the Lord of Śrī, who dwells within the heart of men. 31.
Ayodhyā, Mathurā, Māyā, Kāśikā,
Kāñcī, Avantikā, Dvārakā, and the beautiful city of Rāma— these seven are remembered as the joyful Satya-purīs.
These ten beautiful residences of the glorious Nārāyaṇa, who is dear to himself, have indeed become the bestowers of perfection upon those who behold them.
In these sacred fields that are the abodes of Rājarājeśvarī, the practitioner,
subsisting on milk or fruit, [should practice] day after day for five nights.
The practitioner, having worshipped the discus joined with a Śālagrāma stone, should chant the glorious eight-syllabled mantra a thousand times every day. (35)
Having purified himself and recited the Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā three hundred times, he should offer abundant sacrificial fees at the lotus feet of his own preceptor.
O Great King, behold with your own eyes the Lord of Lakṣmī, the Blessed One, the Lord of the World, the giver of boons, who is affectionate toward his devotees. (37)
Thereafter, I shall briefly proclaim the means for accomplishing the great siddhis, such as divinity and so forth; listen to them with joy, O noble ones! (38)
Having received the illustrious eight-syllabled Vidyā, known as Yājñāyanī and originating from Brahmā, from his preceptor, he remained firm in his vows.
One who desires perfection when [the time] is complete shall conquer kings, royal elephants, and horses;
he is Nārāyaṇa himself, the protector, born as the son of Daśaratha.
I, whose illusory human body is filled with the bliss of the void (śūnyatā), have thus been born upon the surface of the earth by a portion of that very [bliss]. (41)
"By his very permission, O sons of Brahmā, I shall speak;
let the months of Madhu and Mādhava, along with the spring season, be awakened. (42)
O delighters of the Brāhmaṇas, among all the seasons, this spring is the most excellent; therein, beginning from the first day of the month of Caitra, [the festival is celebrated]. 43.
The great festival ending on the ninth day, known as Navarātra,
is the swift destroyer of heaps of great sins and the shatterer of the core of worldly impurity.
It destroys all poverty and all great calamities; it removes all fear of distress and dispels all diseases. || 45 ||
When the constellation Aṇimā is joined with the Jayantī [nakṣatra], knowledge is embodied there;
at that time, at the hour of midday, the Lord Nārāyaṇa is manifest in person. (48)
For the welfare of all the worlds, Rāma, the son of Daśaratha—who is the supreme Brahman—manifested on the surface of the earth. 49.
On the tenth day, the eternal Janakī-devī manifested;
she is the conscious power (Cicchakti) herself, the virtuous lady, the very embodiment of auspiciousness, beauty, and the essence of nectar.
On this earth there was a king named Rāma, the son of Daśaratha;
he was the embodiment of the Supreme Brahman, a great and meritorious soul, and even among him, there was a daughter of Brahmā.
One attains the eternal state, which yields the fruit of millions of sacrifices, gifts, austerities, pilgrimages, and vows. || 53 ||
Even a hundred solar eclipses occurring on a parvan day are not equal to that [merit]; those who do not observe the holy Rāmanavamī, which is difficult to attain, are indeed blameworthy.
O sons of Brahmā, wherever there may be the practice of this knowledge during the Navarātra in the spring, one should reside there.
Beginning from the Pratipad and ending on the ninth day, one who desires the perfection of the sciences should perform the Mahāvrata, which bestows all fruits upon those who recite it. 58.
One who desires great perfection in the knowledge of Rāma-Vaiṣṇava and in the glorious eight-syllabled mantra should perform the auspicious rite described here.
Having recognized the preceptors there, one should communicate that vow;
on the auspicious first day of the bright fortnight of the month of Madhu.
Having risen at the time for the Brahmanical rites, he touched his feet with both hands;
then, recollecting the Brahmavidyā, he thereafter [recited] the Raśmipañjara Sūkta.
Then, having bathed and purified his soul during the daily twilight prayer (saṃdhyā) in the dark fortnight,
he should perform the daily fire-oblation (nityahoma) on the first day of the lunar month, and then bow with devotion to the Preceptor.
A pure person should recite daily one thousand three hundred and twenty times the glorious eight-syllabled mantra (aṣṭākṣarī-vidyā), preceded by the ritual placement (nyāsa).
If one is unable to perform the complete placement of the Mātṛkās belonging to Viṣṇu,
one must certainly perform the placement by placing the Mātṛkās whose nature is consciousness (cidrūpa).
One should daily recite the glorious eight-syllable mantra more than a hundred times, or otherwise, one thousand and eight times.
Having recited one hundred and eight times the six-syllabled Vaiṣṇavī Mahāvidyā of Vāsudeva, which consists of twelve parts, [one attains] the mind of Śrī.
One should constantly recite the Mātṛśata, and likewise the Rājarājeśvarī;
one should also constantly recite the Umā [hymn] one hundred and eight times, or twenty-eight times.
Having donned the Vaiṣṇava armor, one should recite [the mantra] five times every day;
having worshipped according to the previously mentioned procedure with the twelve-syllable mantra of Śrī-Śrīśa.
One should daily worship the pair Brahmā-Viṣṇu one hundred and eight times;
one should daily recite the Yajñanārāyaṇī-vidyā one hundred and eight times.
Or else, one should recite it twenty-eight times at evening;
for this [recitation] bestows one step toward the pair of feet of the Guru every single day.
Therefore, one should avoid deceit, whether it be full or half [of that measure];
for on the day sacred to Śrī Rāma, one should rise early in the morning.
One should first perform the worship of the glorious Aṣṭākṣarī and other mantras;
then, one should recite the Pañcaviṃśati-varmanārāyaṇa mantra twenty-five times.
Having risen early on the tenth day, he should offer oblations one hundred and eight times into the fire consecrated according to the rules, first with the Sāvitrī mantra.
Thereafter, one who desires success and possesses great majesty, having prepared one thousand three hundred oblations with the glorious eight-syllable mantra, should offer them into the fire.
Having offered twenty-eight oblations of pure cow-ghee, or the fat of a boar, with the Vidyā-mantra and also with the Vaiṣṇavī-Ṛgvedic mantra; || 75 ||
After the glorious twelve Āryās, one should perform the vow of three hundred oblations;
for the sake of the eight Siddhis and royal fortune, the vow is twice that.
Likewise, one should offer oblations ending with the words "to the Lord of Lakṣmī" (advau ga lakṣmīpataye); each individual oblation should be performed with the mantras of the Bhagavad-raśmi-vidyās.

Thereafter, the king [should worship] with twenty-eight [verses] according to his own tradition; then, having reached the twenty-first [verse], he should proceed further with armor-protecting mantras.
One should offer eight oblations of clarified butter, or specifically cow's ghee from a Kapila cow;
having offered these, one should subsequently perform expiatory rites through recitations and other such means.

Having performed the offering with the thought "this is an offering to Brahman," and having bowed to Vaiśvānara, he then prostrated himself before the pair of the teacher's feet with his eight limbs touching the ground.
Having offered a single Śālagrāma stone on that tenth day,
one should present sixteen measures of wealth as a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
O Gāgī, one must certainly make the teacher satisfied with various offerings, food, garments, and liquids. || 82 ||
Even if he is unable [to give more], the best of practitioners, having begged from the four castes,
should offer one *niṣka* every day, or half of that, or half of that again.
Having offered [the deity] into the lotus-feet of the Preceptor on the day of Śrī Rāmanavamī, having given two-fold dakṣiṇā and performed oblations again on the tenth day; || 84 ||
Having given a Śālagrāma stone to the Guru as a pair of earrings, and having given a pair of bracelets as an ornament for his arms, one goes to the stainless [abode]. || 85 ||
One should honor the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) with a substance measured by a cow's hide;
having abandoned the desire for wealth, one should give half of that, or even half of that again.
One must certainly offer three gold coins (niṣkas) to the Guru;
likewise, one should offer garments, ornaments, and so forth, with the understanding that they are as if seen directly by Śiva himself.
O best of the twice-born, he should certainly give afterwards to the preceptor’s wife;
and a hundred offerings of food, leaves, and flowers intended for the one observing the vow.
The wise man should worship Śrīpati and the others with perfumes, incense, and flowers;
likewise, he should honor fifteen married women and fifteen Brahmins.
One should satisfy them with handfuls of food, with sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā), and with the [offerings] beginning with the kalā;
and one should [drink] the auspicious water used for washing the lotus feet of the supreme teacher (deśika). 90.
Having drunk from the lotus-like hands of the teacher, one may then consume even his leftovers;
thereafter, one should be embraced by the hand of the supreme teacher.
Filled with a portion of the Blessed One, it is eternally established in accomplishment;
having been offered in twenty-eight ways, it is called the "Royal" according to the ritual procedure.

Having performed here the preliminary rite (*puraścaraṇa*) of the glorious eight-syllable Vidyā, there is no doubt that one becomes a performer of glorious and auspicious deeds and possesses omniscience. (93)
This all-pervading Lord, the destroyer of the demon Rāvaṇa, who is directly Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, is pleased and has become gracious, being solely intent on the protection of his devotees. 98.
It bestows the eightfold prosperity, endowed with tranquility and union; it grants incomparable longevity and health, and even removes the fear of death. 99.
He shall attain the leadership over his own servants, as well as complete perfection in every respect,
all imperishable enjoyments, and a most magnificent celestial chariot.
It bestows dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa; of this there is no doubt.
This is the second stage of the preliminary rite (puraścaryā), accompanied by its constituent parts and sacrificial fees.
The Lord of Śrī, having been offered oblations on that tenth day according to the meter of Vāsudeva, bestows upon him a thousandfold fruit together with its constituent parts.
On the tenth day, having offered clarified butter with the Vaiṣṇavī vidyā, the soul of Hiraṇyagarbha shall become the radiant Virāṭ Śrī.
Because it is the foremost among all prosperities, like the very end of the Lord of Fortune (Śrīpati),
one should offer oblations there with the twelve-syllable Śrī-mantra on the tenth day and perform the final consecration.
With his two eyes he beholds prosperity; he will certainly see this Jānakī, and by the grace of Sītā, [this city] shall be filled with great wealth and grain. (105)
Strewed with heaps of pearl-jewels and crowded with elephants, horses, and chariots, one attains great fortune within this year; of this there is no doubt. (106)
This Ramā-vidyā, the mother of all sciences, which takes the form of consciousness itself—
O Vyāsa and Vālmīki, may it grant success to you who have served her.

In the house of this man, who is esteemed by the earth and who showers down a flood of jewels, there reside auspicious things such as the conch, the discus, and others, along with the goddesses of prosperity and fortune. (108)
The lineage increases like a balance-beam, and the two moons appear;
of this there is no doubt, for he will be filled with every fortune. 109.

One should not perceive separation from the conch-sons through the delusion of [seeing them as] husbands; for one who casts off this [delusion] with the lotus-hands of devotion, there shall be supreme liberation. 110.
On the tenth day, one who is free from fear, having offered clarified butter with the Śrīśā mantra,
obtains the merit of a thousand horse-sacrifices and ten thousand Vājapeya sacrifices.
When the [lunar day] is full, one certainly attains the fruit accompanied by a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
On that auspicious tenth day, it should be presented there with royal splendor.
Having offered some oblation with clarified butter as the means of progression, the practitioner,
having offered ten million oblations with clarified butter by means of the glorious eight-syllable vidyā, [attains success].
Having offered that fruit there, one will certainly attain it; of this there is no doubt, whether by means of the Agniṣṭoma, the Vājapeya, or even a thousand [Vājapeyas]. (114)
The fruit of the Vidyā known as Rājñī is not equal to a single oblation;
the fruit of the Vidyā of the Queen of the Queens of Kings is equal to a fire sacrifice (homa). || 115 ||
O twice-born ones, it cannot be said there whether it is the tenth day or otherwise; therefore, the birth of Śrī Rāma occurred on the ninth day when the tenth day had arrived.
By performing even a single oblation according to the ritual procedure known as Rājarāja,
one attains the sovereign power of qualities such as atomization (āṇimā), as well as prosperity consisting of sons, grandsons, and so forth.
O Brahmins, those who dwell here do not experience even a moment's rest from the bliss of Brahmananda, due to the offering of individual oblations through the vidyās of the rays of the Lord. 118.
One attains the perfection of all the Bhagavadraśmi-vidyās by offering oblations five times with the mantras beginning with "Vam," uttered with the nasal sound ṅa.
He meditated upon the Lord Nārāyaṇa, the all-pervading one who possesses the splendor of ten million moons,
the Supreme Lord who assumes forms such as Nṛsiṃha and Kūrma.
He beholds with his own eyes, without a doubt,
that every day the discus and other weapons appear in embodied form before him.
The yogi protects [the world] like a servant and satisfies those who look upon him with favor; having accomplished his goal in Nārāyaṇa, he shall become the lord of the three worlds.
The yogis, the seers such as Bhṛgu and others,
the Siddhas, and the Sādhyas, together with the Maruts, protect that [place] daily from falsehood and evil.
"This Lord Janakīpati, who is free from all bonds, makes this son of the Wind his companion or his servant. (24)
[He grants] the mastery over qualities such as *aṇimā*, the most excellent perfection of speech,
the eightfold beneficial yoga, and the auspicious memory of ten million births.
Victory over death at its appointed time, great splendor of taste, inexhaustible prosperity, and the most exalted increase of sons and grandsons. || 26 ||
The Lord of Śrī grants him a single supreme realization;
or else, this vow dear to the Blessed One should be performed for three days.
The great yogi Nārāyaṇa, the lord of matted locks, manifested for the welfare of all the worlds that were being observed, and for the sake of their restraint. || 128 ||
Requested by Brahmā, Rudra, Īśa, and all the hosts of deities,
[he appeared] at midday on the ninth day of the bright fortnight in the month of Caitra.
The formless Lord became possessed of form as the supreme son of Kauśalyā;
on the tenth day, Bharata was born, the Lord of the World in the form of a conch.
On the eleventh day of the month, both Ananta and Cakrāṅśa were born as lords of the waters;
they became the two lords of the gods, Lakṣmī and Arā, who were together with their friends.
On the tenth day, Jānakī herself, whose abode is the lotus, appeared directly before Mahānandī’s eyes,
having descended from the surface of the earth.
O beloved, beginning from the ninth day for a period of three days,
one should respectfully perform the *puraścaryā* vow dedicated to Jānakīrāma.
On the tenth day of the month of Caitra, under the constellation of Daivata, the supreme King Kattora was consecrated with the royal inauguration by great lords.
On the eleventh day, at the break of dawn, Rāma was delighted and his devotees were filled with joy. 135.
Therefore, the great sages and the perfected ones (siddhas) proclaimed this triad— the glory of recitation and the great yoga— as that which brings about the imperishability of the devotee.
For that devotee who performs this three-day vow dedicated to Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa,
the All-pervading Lord becomes directly attainable.
One should take refuge in Kaivalya, which is the singular consciousness of the bliss of Brahman. || 138 ||

On this day, O twice-born ones, the noble ones should recite the *managīti* joined with the *gārthā*, mixed with the ancient *vardhamānagīti*; and on these three days of Śrī Rāma Vaidra, they should be accompanied by the power of the vow.
When the five planets are situated in the exaltation signs, on the ninth lunar day (navamī) in the asterism Ārdrā, and when the Sun is in Cancer conjoined with the Punarvasu nakṣatra,
the sages— possessing wealth, free from disease, and endowed with splendor— offered oblations of palāśa wood, clarified butter,
and fuel into the sacrificial fire for the sake of manifesting the unborn Bhava. Then, having offered a certain portion of ghee, they attained their desired goal.

The Śrī Rāma-Janmanavamī is the destroyer of the cycle of rebirth, the accomplisher of all goals, and the bestower of liberation; those who are intent on fasting on this day and offer wealth at the pair of feet of Brahmā and Viṣṇu attain the state of Hari and Īśa. 141.
Having offered libations at a sacred ford with single sesame seeds for the sake of his sons and others, he satisfied the lineages of his paternal and maternal ancestors;
then, having bestowed infinite bliss upon them, he placed his head at the pair of lotus feet of the Guru.

On the birthday of Śrī Rāma, having offered gems, seeds, pearls, and fruits at the pair of lotus feet of the Preceptor, one who is born of the lineage of Vakva obtains the fruit of giving a hundred cows. || 143 ||
O Lord of Sages, you have described the birth day of Śrī Rāma as being equal to ten million lunar eclipses and solar eclipses.

On this occasion, one should not look upon anyone other than Nārāyaṇa, the preceptor of the gods, through the recitation of the eight-syllable mantra, fire-offerings, and worship. During this vow, which lasts for three days beginning from the ninth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Rāma-janma (Rāmanavamī) and ending on the eleventh day—
Having performed the recitation, fire-oblation, and worship of the eight-syllable mantra, one should then perform the consecration with the royal mantra as prescribed by the authorities. || 145 ||
Then, having given the *deśika* his wealth for a year’s sustenance—
measured as one, two, three, four, or five *karṣas*— the disciple who is capable of ten [tasks] is then employed. || 146 ||
Having offered a flawless garment along with ornaments for the Guru's wife— who is worthy of worship even by the world—
and having completed the rites born of the ancient sacrifice equivalent to the offering of ten thousand golden mountains, one should become absorbed in the Blessed One together with one’s lineage.
O Brahmins, this song was sung by the mother of Jāsmān and his father;
having been told by them on the third day, I shall now proclaim the vow. || 148 ||
On the day of Śrī Rāma’s birth-ninth (Rāmanavamī), which bestows all perfections,
having risen during the Brāhma-muhūrta and prostrated at the feet of the preceptor, || 149 ||
Then, having taught the supreme Brahmavidyā of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, Śanaiścara, mindful of Manu, purified himself and subdued his senses. (150)
Having bathed, performed the twilight devotions (saṃdhyā), and completed the daily fire-oblation (nityahoma),
he then prostrated with reverence before the pair of feet of the teacher.
Having recited the glorious eight-syllabled mantra (aṣṭākṣarī-vidyā) known as Vāsudeva one thousand and one hundred times,
he should then recite the Vaiṣṇava mantra one hundred times.
One should subsequently recite four hundred times either the twelve-syllable mantra of Māyā,
the vidyā of Prasannalakṣmī, or the six-syllable mantra of Śrī.
One should recite the Rājarājeśvarī Mahāvidyā twenty-eight times;
one should indeed offer oblations to Vaiṣṇava and Varma twenty times every day.
Whether subsisting on milk, or subsisting on fruits, or even consuming the five products of the cow;
with his senses subdued, he should eat sacrificial food (haviṣya), having abandoned betel and salt.
One should daily offer one karṣa, or half of that, or even a third, at the pair of feet of the Guide of the World. (156)
Having bestowed [the initiation] upon one who is incurable even in the presence of the Preceptor, O Acyuta,
the Preceptor should then perform the wearing of ornaments and other rites for Māyā with a mind focused on Śrī.
Free from greed for wealth and possessions, one should strive to attain the goal;
having risen early on the twelfth day and completed the daily obligatory rites. || 158 ||
In the presence of the teacher, having performed the purificatory rites according to the rules over the fire, he should offer twenty-eight oblations of cow's ghee with the Sāvitrī mantra. 159.
With devotion, one should offer a thousand or a hundred oblations of cow's ghee— or even ghee from a sacrificial feast— into the fire while reciting the glorious eight-syllable mantra.
Having offered oblations twenty-eight times with the four-syllabled mantra of Viṣṇu, which belongs to Vāsudeva, and with the twelve-syllabled mantra of Lakṣmī; 161.
Then, with a serene mind and free from disease, one should offer one hundred and eight oblations of ghee;
having offered twenty oblations, one should thereafter contemplate the Lord of Sacrifice.
Then, by the command of the Great Queen, they offered twenty-eight oblations with their feet;
having first offered each individual oblation of clarified butter with the rays of the Blessed One.
Having offered oblations five times with mantras while the fire is blazing,
and having performed the offerings with the *japa* and other rites, one should subsequently perform the *brahmārpaṇa* oblation.
Having made Agnipradarā the guardian, he should offer eightfold oblations;
and having adorned the preceptor with perfumes, flowers, and garments, [he should honor him]. (165)
One should place a pair of beautiful earrings upon the ears of the preceptor;
then, one should offer to the preceptor the ornament that adorns his chest.

One should offer [the gift] to the preceptor’s wife with the thought, "May it be Śrī, Budhī, or Lakṣmī. For a Brāhmaṇa, a Vaiśya, or a Kṣatriya, the merit of giving a moving gift [such as a cow] is inexhaustible and equal to a thousandfold reward. (169)
Ten million times ten million great vidyās, and ten million times a thousand hāmajambhūs; by circumambulating [this], one obtains a thousandfold auspicious and inexhaustible fruit. || 170 ||
Having reached the further shore through the grace of his preceptor, the brahmin attained the Lord Nārāyaṇa— the unborn, all-pervading one, endowed with splendor.

Necessarily, within that year, one shall indeed behold [the deity] with one's own eyes, provided one performs the preliminary rite (puraścaryā) ten thousand times accompanied by the ancillaries and sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā). || 172 ||
Whatever kind of accomplishment is said to result from the glorious eight-syllable vidyā, that same [accomplishment] arises from the power and grace of the Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā. (173)
One who possesses such devotion here for three days attains that very same perfection as one who has completed a hundred-fold *puraścaraṇa* of the Vaiṣṇavī Varma-vidyā. || 174 ||
Whatever kind of supreme accomplishment has been described here by the ancient and highest sages, such a great accomplishment arises for him; of this there is no doubt. (175)
By offering oblations here with even a mere *lakṣa* of clarified butter, or with the twelve-syllable *Śrīvidyā*, one shall attain the perfection arising from a hundred rounds of *puraścaraṇa*.
If the prince is wealthy, let the preceptors accept a hundred thousand gold coins,
a thousand cows, and even a hundred thousand niskas.
Or, O Blessed One, having offered a thousand ornaments made of gold to the presence of the Ācārya, or else having promised a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
Within a month, one should not give false testimony, nor should one cause a cow to wander, nor should one take up debt;
for at the end of the kalpa, these are the duties of the wise, pure, and great-souled teacher.
The debt acknowledged does not perish; it must be paid with respect as double the amount within six months, for it is a sharp-edged sword of hellish suffering. (82)
One should perform the preliminary rite (puraścaryā) which bestows the bliss of Brahmananda; this was spoken by his wise father and maternal grandfather.
The Queen of Queens of Mantras, who bestows all perfections, is difficult to attain even for the gods; therefore, one should observe this vow for three days or even during the Navarātra.
O twice-born ones, he who performs [this] out of the grace of a pure preceptor is indeed the foremost among all Brahmins, a great lord. (187)
He is the most excellent among those who strive, liberated from all striving, and beyond the reach of striving; the vow of three days is superior even to the Navarātra.
Having performed the auspicious *puraścaryā* vow for three days, he is liberated from heaps of sins and becomes endowed with the merit of all virtuous deeds. (189)
Even a dull-witted person becomes a great poet, a master of speech comparable to Jīva and Bhārgava, swiftly through the grace of Sītā and Rāma. (190)
He certainly attains stable and perpetual prosperity that extends through his lineage, abounding in pearls, great jewels, wealth, grain, and other riches. 191.
Sons, grandsons, and great-grandsons become endowed with long life and health, as well as knowledge and prosperity, just like their father. (192)
Old age, death, and disease were destroyed; life and health became inexhaustible; and she attained exalted prosperity equal to that of the King of Yakṣas and the Lord of the Immortals.
Having attained a disease-free body, a birth in the Vṛndāvana forest, auspicious memory, and being joined by a thousand divine maidens as well as Savarbhānu, [he remained]. 194.
Having ascended a celestial chariot, accompanied by thousands of his kin,
he becomes beloved by the gods in heaven and honored by all the hosts of prosperity.
Worshipped by yakṣas, kiṃnaras, gandharvas, siddhas, and vidyādharas,
you have become a body of light consisting of twenty-five suns.
And Attaraścamara was constantly adorned with divine ornaments;
having come to wear divine garments, he was endowed with the happiness of divine enjoyments. || 197 ||
Having performed the vow for two or three nights, she attains the eternal Brahma after piercing through the falling shell of the universe, and realizes the all-pervading Lord Nārāyaṇa.
She gazes with her eyes upon Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, accompanied by Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa, and the others, as Revatī gazes upon her calf. || 199 ||
By this very means, there is no destruction of the identity with the vow;
one should meditate that it resides in one's own hand, and thus achieve the state of having attained one's own goal.
O sons of Brahmā, due to the greatness of this three-day vow,
there exists nothing unattainable for him, whether in the mortal world or even in Pātāla.
Gaurī, Lakṣmī, Mahāvāṇī, and others are His principal Śaktis;
and Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, and the lords of the directions are the manifestations of Maheśa. (202)
By the power of this three-day vow, even those who are under control protect the form of Nārāyaṇa himself day and night. (203)
"This very Mahāyogin is the all-pervading Hari Nārāyaṇa;
thus everything has been ascertained with certainty, O sons of Brahmā. (204)
The great vidyā of the king of kings bestows all desired objects upon mere remembrance; it is for this reason that the glorious accomplishment of the eight siddhis has been proclaimed for us. (205)
They are the most excellent among the twice-born; how much more, then, do you wish to hear?

[Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter, titled "The Great Glory of the Rājarājā-vidyā," in the latter portion of the *Śrīmad-anuttara-brahma-tattva-rahasya*, the *Dāśarathīya Tantra*, which is a compendium of the essential meaning of the Vedas.]
They spoke to the yogin.

O Blessed One, Teacher Kapila, Nārāyaṇa, Lord of the World, Protector of Sītā; in the presence of the Blessed One, out of an excess of compassion, this divine means (sādhana) has been established for the sake of the welfare of all beings. || 1 ||
Facing [the enemy] with one's mouth leads to death; having heard this, there is no great doubt. || 2 ||
The thousand-syllable great vidyā of Nārāyaṇī has been declared by you;
however, the thousand-syllable [mantra] of the goddess Śrī has merely been indicated, not fully revealed.
"O Lord, that pair of sciences is for the sake of great majesty. The Blessed One said:
O sons of Brahmā, listen with self-restraint as I shall proclaim the Nārāyaṇī, which possesses a thousand rays, bestows vigor, and grants the attainment of fruits.
When the great yogi-muni Nārāyaṇa is remembered by oneself, one becomes wise.
The deity is Gāyatra, the meter is Chaṃdas, and the all-pervading Lord is Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa;
the presiding deity is Jāganātha, whose essence is the Supreme Self.
The seed-syllable of the three Vedas (*trayī-bīja*) is *namaḥ*;
then the word *bhagavate*, followed by *keśava*, *nārāyaṇa*, and *mādhava*.
"O Govinda! O Destroyer of distress! O Trivikrama!
O Vāmana! O Śrīdhana!"—uttering these words, he then opened his treasury with joy.
Pūjanā, Bhayadaṇḍā, Mohanā, and Saṃkarṣaṇā;
then the word Vāsudeva, and also the word Pradyumna. (9)
O you whose feet are unshakable, O Supreme Being named Puruṣottama, O Adhokṣaja, Narasiṃha, Acyuta, and Janārdana! 10.
Then, after *upekṣetihāne*, one should recite *śrīkṛṣṇapada* as well;
thereafter, the pair *jaganmūrti jagannātha*. (11)
"O protector of the world, O you of divine and auspicious form!
You are the god of gods," saying this, she addressed the sovereign of all deities.

The state worthy of praise by the gods, the source of all prosperity, beyond the foot [of the world], O Soul of the Universe, the manifestation of the universe, and thereafter the state of the Lord of the Universe. (13)
Having joined the pair of recitations while assuming the universal form (viśvarūpa), one should then utter the word "Om," which is praised in the Vedas and the Upanishads (vedānta). || 14 ||
Then, having become fourfold, he then became fivefold;
here, from the fourfold [state], there arose a pair of female energies (prasrī). || 15 ||
O Lotus-eyed One, whose eyes are like lotuses, O You whose name is Vayupka, O Supreme Self higher than the highest, who are beyond even the Prana! Salutations to You, the Supreme. 16.
In the Śūdra-brahmavarūpāṭa, one should utter the name of the Supreme Lord; I shall deposit this Hayagrīva-tantra, which is a pair of secrets and a treasury of knowledge. || 17 ||
O Lord of all masters of speech, O you whose name is "Compassionate toward Devotees," thereafter protect me, who am sinking in the ocean of worldly existence, O treasure-house of mercy! 18.
Having joined "Kāmetejana-ketu," [one says] "Kāmaprada," "Kṛpālaya," and then the word "Nāśana" at the end of the sound of the word "Kṛtāntabhaya. (19)
Then, for the sake of what was desired by Kṛtānta, who is the soul of all causes, Mucukunda spoke thus to Mukunda regarding the pair of prayers: "tat etat. (20)
"O giver of boons, [the name] 'Mucukunda' and the name 'Protector of the World' (Jagatpālaka) were uttered;
then, having spoken of death for Jamadagni, he said 'devoid' (rahita) thereafter. (21)
Then, having bowed to the ground with the words "jālātmaka," one should then recite twice the mantra ending with the word "bhūṣaṇa" for the daughter of the Earth (Sītā).
Then the word *hā matsya-rūpa*, then *kūrma-āloke*, then *yajeti atha varāha iti padam*; it is not there, nor is it there, O Hari. (23)
O Rama, you who possess the splendor of the subduer of Madhu;
O Rama, having abandoned the supreme state of being known as the son of Dasharatha, you are called "Rama" by those who know you as the Supreme.
Regarding the form of the Buddha, it is said that "form" (rūpa) means "consisting of sacrifice" (yajñamaya);
having spoken thus, one should recite the two names of the Lord of Sacrifice (Yajñeśvara), who bestows the fruit of sacrifice. || 25 ||
Then the words "sahasrāsya" (thousand-faced) and "sahasretikyaṇa" (having a thousand rays), then the word "sahasraṇīṣa" (thousand-crested), and then "sahasrākṣarpi" (thousand-rayed). || 26 ||
The thousand-rayed one is equal to the Omniscient One; likewise is the name of the Lord of the Gods (Indra).
