He who effects the withdrawal is also the name of the Jewel of All Happiness. 27.
Having worshipped "Sarvadevamaya," then "Sarvapadam," then "Bhūtatakṣapadam," O Lord, and then "Suṇīlasulābha."
Then, having become free from resentment, he said, "O Savitri, O Goddess of Wisdom, reveal the word of the Teacher of all the worlds. (29)

Be gracious, O Lord of the Three Vedas, you who are the protector of the three worlds; O Leader of the three realms, at the end of the sound of the syllable *kara* (the letter 'ka'), you are the pair (*yugala*) and the subsequent savior. 30.
Then, O Leader of the Three Worlds, [recite] the pair beginning with "trautyamaya," then the pair of mantras beginning with "sītāpate" and "rādhāpate."
Then, one should recognize Nīlā, Patañjī, Rukmiṇī, and Satyanāmā;
after that, one should utter Bhāmā and the others as the eight queens. || 32 ||
O Lord of sixteen thousand, captivator of the hearts of the cowherd women, O Supreme One whose mind is fixed on the son of Daśaratha, [I offer] a pair of recitations. 33.
Born from the womb of Kauśalyā, refuge of Śrī Rāma,
called "O Child" and "O Compassionate One," whose lotus feet are worshipped by Śaṅkara.

O soul of Bharata, O soul of Lakṣmaṇa, O slayer of Śambara, O son of Manu—having been saluted for the sake of the Lord’s purpose, [the sage] spoke to the son of Añjanā, the preceptor of the mountain-dwellers. 35.
"O Great King, O Man of Great Renown!"—thus Vibhīṣaṇa addressed him;
and as he ascended the celestial chariot, he was called by the name Vanadeva-varīyas.
Having abandoned [the world], he became known as Prahādavarada, meaning "the one who grants boons to Prahlāda" and "the destroyer of all enemies";
and then, O son of Diti, he became known as Brahmaṇyadeva, meaning "the god who is devoted to Brahman. || 37 ||
Having said, "O son of Vasudeva," and then, "O son of Devakī," [he addressed him as] "O you who bear the conch,
discus, mace, and lotus, and are marked with the Śrīvatsa."
At the end of the word Gaṇādadhvaja, one should utter the name Maheṃdrāvajana;
[he is] Maheṃdra, whose feet are worshipped, and who is praised by Maheśa and the lords of the gods.
O Lord of the gods such as Mahendra, who are supported by the Mahopaniṣads; [the mantra is] "u" twice, followed by the word "gokale," and then the word "saṃrakṣaka. (40)
Having said, "O Pārtha, you are my protector," he who consists of true bliss then spoke:
"You are the form of eternal bliss, consisting of consciousness, O Lord of Consciousness."
Then the word "cidākṛte," then the word "viraṃtana," then "paramānandarūpe," and after that the word "parameśi. (42)
O Ancient One, O Person of Pure Form, O Purifier!
Having joined [the prayer] with praise of the Purifier, with devotion, and with words that please Your feet; 43.
The word *vigitāre*, the name *Vimalākāśa*, the term *Vīrarāghava*, and then *vīra* and *puruṣa*. (44)
Then [the names] Jayayugma, Mana, Tālun, Anantaśayana, Anantarūpa, Ananta, Saukhyada, and Bhadanāma. (45)
Then the title "Lord of Great Yogins," then the title "Teacher of Yoga," and then the title "Dattātreya"—these two titles were bestowed for the sake of the dual lineage. (46)
Having attained mastery over the sciences and wealth, he [surpassed] the yakṣas, rākṣasas, and kinnaras;
furthermore, he reached the status of a great ṛṣi among gods, asuras, and divine seers.
One incurs the slaughter of a Brahmin-ṛṣi by stepping upon his lotus feet;
beyond that, O tiger among the highly exalted, is the pair of recitations (japa). || 48 ||
He who performs creation, sustenance, and dissolution beyond that— O Yogi,
for the sake of attaining the state of a Yogi, meditate upon his lotus feet.
"O bestower of all accomplishments! O sovereign of all worlds!"—then [he says], "consisting of earth and water," and then "consisting of fire and air. (50)
Then, having abandoned the space-like body consisting of the individual soul and vital breath,
as well as that composed of all the principles (tattvas), one should abandon the body composed of all the senses and the mind.
Beyond this, one should recite the pair of mantras: "O you who possess all the qualities of sentient beings," "O stainless and unsullied one," "O eternally constant and pure one. (52)
Having joined the words "in the form of fire," "the sun," and "the moon," and then "I am born from that," he should utter the word "possessing the fragrance of incense. (53)
Then, after the pair of mantras and the word "śeṣaśayana," there follows the phrase "sāketanagarādhīśamathurādhipate. (54)
Then the station Kāśī is called Nāyakī;
likewise, Kāñcī is called Punnīnāyakāntī, and Avantī is called Nāyakī. (55)
Then, after the word "Nāyaka," [he spoke] the syllables "dvārakā-nāyaka-sīṇa-cchi-śāpi-nya-da-ma-sya-tha," followed by "śveta-dvīpāt viśat-vānte. (56)
O Lord of Satyaloka, thereafter O Leader of the city of Vaikuṇṭha, Sovereign of the city of Ayodhyā, who is solely intent on satisfying Your devotees! 57
And at the end of the Caturveda-maya [section], his name is "Seated upon the Lion-throne" (Siṃhāsanārūḍha);
his chest is adorned with the Śrīvatsa and Kaustubha, and he is decorated with a forest garland (vanamālā). || 58 ||
After the words "divyābhūṣaṇa" (divine ornaments), the word "bhūṣitā" (adorned) follows; then the word "divyamālya" (divine garland), and after that the word "virājita" (resplendent). || 59 ||
Recite the two mantras "Divyacaṃdana" and "Carcita," followed by the words "Suprasanna" and the name "Vadanāmbuja. (60)
Adorned with divine yellow garments, a crown, bracelets, armlets, a beautiful necklace, and two earrings; || 61 ||
O you who ward off all that is harmful, you are at the end of the refuge of all the lords of the world; may all your devotees enjoy sovereignty, pleasures, heaven, and liberation.
Then, reciting these two pairs of names: "Jānakīvaktrabhayadam" (the giver of fear to the face of Jānakī) and "rucciṇīvalkabhettha," as well as "Rādhāvallabhabhū" and "nīlāvatkṛbha. || 63 ||
The station of Mahāmaheśvara is beyond the Great Couple; at the end of Puruṣa is the Great Couple, and the two great [stations] named Rāja and Nāma. || 64 ||
Then, O God, when the word "Vibhūti" was uttered, there arose the station of Caṇḍāṇa;
and from the one proclaiming "Bhūtanātha," the station of Lokanātha arose thereafter. || 65 ||
The state that encompasses Viśvanātha, Ananta, and infinite millions of Brahmāṇḍas is beyond the words "Lord of Lakṣmī" and "Lord of Mahālakṣmī. (66)
Having uttered the pair of mantras "O Lord of royal fortune" (rājyalakṣmīpate) and "O Lord of prosperity" (padaṃ paścī śriyaḥ pate), one should then recite the name of Śrī Nārāyaṇa.

Salutations to You, the triad; thereafter, this [prayer] has been uttered: O Lotus-eyed One, O Teacher of the Gods, whose fame is equal to millions of suns and lightning, who are stainless and adorned with the Śrīvatsa on Your chest, and resplendent with armlets, necklaces, earrings, bracelets, and other ornaments.
I worship Nārāyaṇa, whose left side is eternally embraced by Lakṣmī. || 69 ||
"Holding [the weapons] with his hands"—thus [is the mantra] for the leader of the five-faced [form]. (70)
At the beginning, one should remember Viṣṇu Nārāyaṇa at the time of the end of grace;
it consists of three hundred and twenty-eight syllables.
This thousand-syllable Nārāyaṇī Vidyā has been narrated by me;
it is the destroyer of all sins and the remover of sorrow. (73)

This great vidyā, which bestows the fruit of prosperity along with ministers, is the destroyer of great obstacles; it belongs to the King of Kings and should be recited day after day at the conclusion of the mantra-japa. (74)
The wise person who constantly remembers this thousand-syllabled Mahānārāyaṇī Vidyā even once, for him all obstacles shall vanish.
The supreme practitioner, who is the progenitor of the thousand-syllable Vidyā, can turn what is not divine into divine, and even what is divine into non-divine. (76)
If one were to go to all sacred fords and perform every sacrifice, those thousands of great sciences would constantly extend [their benefits]. (77)
There is no consecration, no ritual refinement, and no Vedic rite of initiation;
the supreme sages have declared that for him, the compassion of the Teacher alone constitutes initiation. (78)
The earth, possessing the island of truth, is crowded with wealth and grain;
it is said that on this earth, the lotus feet of the Guru are the sacrificial fee for the pair [of deities]. (79)
Having reached this place, which is free from fear and delights in the waves of its waters,
one should recite five times the Vidyā that destroys [obstacles] and bestows the fruit of the conch.
A great rain indeed pours down immediately upon the entire surface of the earth;
when there is excessive rain, one should recite [the mantra] five times in the presence of fire.
Just as a sudden rain immediately pacifies that terrible forest fire, so too does the supreme, glorious eight-syllable mantra, the Queen of the Kings of Queens. 82.
The compendium of Vedānta known as Nārāyaṇīyā bestows supreme success even without the preliminary ritual (puraścaryā).
If one performs this rite with compassion and purity upon the surface of the earth, this thousand-syllable Vidyā shall become perfected for him. (84)
O sons of Brahmā, there is nothing unattainable for him on this earth;
even the abundant prosperity of Mahendra’s city and Sarasvatī herself [are his]. (85)
In that very temple, as long as the moon and stars endure,
this [mantra] is the deathless one, the warder-off of all calamities.
This [goddess] bestows all prosperity and grants enjoyment, heaven, and liberation;
O best of the twice-born, having abandoned stinginess regarding wealth, seek refuge at the feet of the Teacher. 87.
Having gathered together wealth, grain, a multitude of fame, pearls, and gems, and having given much as a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), he recited this thousand-verse hymn with devotion.
Having received it day by day from the lotus-face of the Guru, one should either remember it once daily or recite the King of Kings' Vidya; there is nothing superior to this. (89)
One attains continuous great sovereignty, all sciences easily mastered, great fortune to be acquired as a flower, and the glory of possessing sons and grandsons. (90)
Having become a Jātismara for a long time, and having attained a body composed of light, he reached the eternal Brahman, the supreme state.
These thousands of hymns to Nārāyaṇī which have been proclaimed;
hereafter, I shall proclaim thousands of hymns to the Goddess Śrī.

[Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter, titled "The Majesty of the King of Kings’ Vidyā," in the latter portion of the *Śrīmadanuttarabrahmatattvarahasya*, the *Dāśarathīya Tantra*, which is a compendium of the essential meaning of the Vedas.]
May the body of Lakṣmī, O Puṇḍarīkākṣa, grant us prosperity—she who holds in her hands the conch, the discus, knowledge, and a lotus in the lake of the world;

whose eyes possess the play of lightning and a golden complexion; whose waist is adorned with a girdle; whose breasts are like two peaks; and whose form has become one with the entire universe through her insatiable longing.
The Blessed One said:
O venerable Brahmins, I shall describe the thousands of glories of the Goddess Śrī,
by the mere knowledge of which one is honored even here and throughout the three worlds.
Then [the mantra] is: "Oṃ" (the three Tārās) followed by "Namaḥ Tripurāsundari," then the word "Hṛdayadevi," and thereafter the word "Śiro Devī. (2)
After that, the word "Śaśidevī," then the word "Pāda," then "Pāda," then "Kavaca," then "Devī," then "Netra," then "Devī," then "Astra," and then the word "Kāmeśvarī. (3)
"Bhagamālini," ending with "niśabdānto," then the word "nityaklinne," followed by "bheruṇḍa" and "vahni," ending with the great word "vāsinī. || 4 ||
O Vajreśvarī, O you who have transcended the cry of the jackal, O beautiful one!
O Nityā, O Nīlapatākā, O Vijayā, O Sarvamaṅgalā! || 5 ||
Having become Mālinī in Citra and Mahānityā thereafter,
she is Parameśvarī at the end of the corpse (śava), and Parameśvarī is beyond the corpse (śavātīta).
Then there is the practice consisting of Mītreśa, Ṣaṣṭhīśa, and Māḍḍīśa;
and then that consisting of Nātha, Avipra, Tyaloya, and Madrāmāyī.
Then, at the end of the Kali age, she will be known as Agastyā;
likewise, having pleased Dharmāvārya, she will be known as Muktakeśīśvarā.
Having addressed the Lord of the Arts (the Moon) as "O servant of dissolution," and then having spoken the words "Prabhākara" and "Paṭṭadevī," [he said] "Mayī. || 9 ||

Having joined the word *devamayī* with the word *pada*, and then [the word] *tejodevamayī*, even when the word *deva* has reached the state of being produced by the mind (*manojāta*), it is [so] from the word *kalāṇa*. || 10 ||
Then, having offered a foot [of worship] consisting of the deity, and then one consisting of jewels;
and then [an offering] to Vāsudeva consisting of Śrī Rāmānanda.
Following that, when the perfection of aṇimā is attained, laghimā is also perfected;
after the perfection of mahimā, the perfection of īśitva is considered the next stage.
When mastery is accomplished, there is the accomplishment of sovereign power (*prākāmya*); when sovereign power is accomplished, O Mother, the state [is attained].
When the enjoyment of others is accomplished, the state is accomplished according to one's wish; having passed beyond that state, one goes to the supreme state. || 13 ||
And after "Siddhe" and "Sarvakāmānte," [the word] "Siddhe" follows; thereafter comes "Brāhmī," and after the words "Māheśvarī," "Kaumārī," and "Vaiṣṇavī. (14)
Then Vārāhī, Māhendrī, Cāmuṇḍā, and the word Śabda; then the term Mahālakṣmī, and "O All-Agitating One" (Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī) which follows thereafter. (15)
Having joined [the mantra] with *sarvavaśīkaraṇī* and *sarvākarṣiṇī* according to the sound, one should place *paraṃ sarva-vaśī-karaṇī* after the word *pada*. || 16 ||
The word ending with "sa-vonmādini" is [the mantra] for Aṅkuśa;
then follows the word "sarvakhecarite sarvabījī. (17)
Then, in every Khaṇḍa, [one should utter] "Trailokyamohana," followed by "Nipada," then the word "Cakrasvāmini," and finally "Prakaṭayogini. (18)
"O attractor of desires! O you who attract speech! [The syllable] *haṃ* by way of sound; then the word 'attractor' (*ākarṣiṇi*), and then the word 'revealer of speech' (*vāgāviṇī*). || 19 ||
After *sparśākarṣiṇī*, [one should worship] *śabdākarṣiṇī*; after that, *rūpākarṣiṇī*. After *sākarṣiṇī*, [one should worship] *śabdākarṣiṇī*; after that, *gaṃdhākarṣiṇī*.
By means of the *citākarṣiṇī* [mantra], sounds are drawn forth; by means of the *dhaurya*, those being drawn are attracted;
by means of the *parastṛtyākarṣiṇī*, one draws forth the supreme name at the end of the sound.
Then, after the words "seed-attracting" (vījākarṣiṇi) and "sound-attracting" (śabdākarṣiṇi), one utters "hair-attracting" (bālākarṣiṇī);
then "formless-attracting" (amūrtākarṣiṇī), "weapon-attracting" (āyudhākarṣiṇī), and "refuge-attracting" (śaraṇākarṣiṇī). || 22 ||
Then, [worship] the Mistress of the Wheel who fulfills all hopes with the mantra "Oma";
then salute the Guptayoginī with the mantra "Namaḥ" and the Flower with the mantra "Anangamekhale."
After *anaṅgamadane*, [there is] *danagaṃmadanātūre*;
then the word *anaṅgarekhenaṅgādyaveginī*. (24)
Having uttered "Anaṅgaukuśa," and having uttered "Padve cānagamāliṃ," and having uttered "Sarvaṃ saṃkṣobhaṇe," one should then recite "Cakrasvāminī. (25)
Having joined the word *pada* with *gatyantare*, one should then say the word *yoginī*; then, having uttered *sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī*, one should then say *sarvavidrāviṇī*. (26)
At the end of the eight [syllables] of the Siddha-mantra, one should utter "Sarvokarṣi";
then, having joined "Sarvasaṃmohinī," after that comes "Sarvastambhinī. (27)
One should utter: "O Sarvajṛmbhiṇī, O Sarvavaśaṅkarī, O Sarvarañjinī, O Śabditā, O Sarvonmādinī! (28)
Bestowing the vision that accomplishes all aims, she fulfills all prosperity;
being composed of all mantras, she brings about the destruction of all duality.
"O giver of all auspiciousness and excellence!"—thus four times;
"O mistress of the wheel, O eternal one, according to the tradition, O Yoginī!"—thus thirty times.
She is the supreme pacifier and the warder-off of all obstacles. || 32 ||
Having said, "O beautiful one in every limb! O bestower of all good fortune!
O accomplisher of all aims! he should then churn the Lord of the Cakra.
Then follows the word *yoginī* for one who has transcended the family (*kulottīrṇa*), and then [the words] *sarvajñā*, *sarvaśakti*, and *sarvaiśvaryapradāyinī*. (34)

Having joined [the breath] with that which consists of all knowledge, which is all-pervading and imperishable, one should then cause it to enter the abode of Hari through the channel of all the veins. 35.
She who consists of all bliss, she who bestows all protection, she who causes all desires to bear fruit, she who grants all that is desired, she who is the truth of all. (36)
Then follows the word *rakṣākarapada*, then the word *vakrasvāminī*, then the word *nigabhādhogiṃ*, and after that the word *vaśinī*. (37)
After the word *Kāmeśvarī*, the word *Mohinī* follows; then [the word] *Vimaleśa*, and after that, *Marūṇejami*. (38)
After the word *sarveśvarī*, one should then utter the word *kaulinī*;
having joined [the mantra] with *sarvarogaharā*, one should then recite *cakreśvarī*. (39)
Then [the word] *rahasyayoginī*, followed by *padaṃ*, then *vāṇini* and *vapini*; having joined *vāśinyam* and *kuśinī*, [one says] *mahākāmeśvarī* thereafter. (40)
Having joined [the mantra] with "Mahābaloptari," then "Māhāśrībhagamālini," then "Māhāśrīsuṃdarī," and then "Sarvasiddhimahā. (41)
Then follows the word "Rahasyayoginī," the mistress of wealth; thereafter is the venerable "Śrīmāhāpadambhadryarikeya. 42.
Having joined [the mantra] with "sarvānahaṃ mayai," one should utter it as Vakrasvāmī;
then, for the sake of the supreme and secret [mantra], one should heat the word "yoginī. (43)
"O Tripura! O Queen of Tripura!"—this is the phrase, O Tripurasundarī;
then follows the phrase "Dwelling at the end of Tripura," O Tripurāśrī. (44)
At the end of "Tripurā," [place] "Mālini" and then the word "Tripurasiddhaḥ";
after that, the word "Tripurām" and then "Mātripurasundari. (45)
Māhāmāheśvarī, Mahāmāhārājñī, the abode of the feet;
Mahāmāhāpūrvaśakti, and thereafter Mahāpadā. || 46 ||
In Mahāgupta there is the Great Sound (Mahāśabda), and in Mahājñapti that which is beyond it;
in Mahāmahānanda there is the Great Sound (Māhāśabda), and beyond that [is the next]. || 47 ||
One should utter "Mahāmahe mahāmūrve mahāmāye" here, followed by the words "Mahāśrīcakranagasāmrājñī. (48)
Salutations to you three; if you are indeed the beloved and the triple-savior, then let this mind play for the sake of prosperity—this has been told by me to you all. (49)
Consisting of thirty-one thousand syllables, it is capable of enchanting the three worlds;
Dakṣiṇāmūrti is said to be its seer, and the omniscient Lord is its deity.
The meter is declared to be Paṅkti, and the deity is remembered as Śrīdevī.
[Her attributes are] the noose, the goad, the sugarcane bow, and the Aśoka flower, among others.
He was holding five flower-arrows, was reddish in hue,
resplendent with manifold brilliance, and endowed with hundreds of divine ornaments.
He creates a sublime frown upon his brow that causes [the enemy] to flee;
I take refuge in this supreme sovereign glory consisting of majesty. (53)

Having meditated daily upon the goddess Mahāśrīsundarī, who is supreme splendor consisting of radiant light, within the thousand-petaled lotus of the heart, one should recite the mantra of a thousand syllables.
The goddesses of the nine obstacles are the glories of the gods, consisting of the three Vedas; they exist as a single collective form, encompassing the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas.
This great queen of vidyās destroys the suffering of recollection;
she bestows the secret meaning of all limbs and grants a portion of all merit. (56)

One who performs the worship of the Śrīcakra constantly and in detail becomes most meritorious; by reciting this daily even once, one obtains the fruit arising from its complete performance along with all its ancillaries. || 57 ||
Within the supreme great kingdom, all the Śrīvidyās are empowered; they have been revealed, yet remain well-guarded secrets, which shatter the bonds of worldly existence through mere remembrance.
O Auspicious One, by the mere recollection of these [names], may there be prosperity at every step for those devoted to you. (59)
It brings men under control, it surely brings women under subjection, and it bestows the sovereignty of qualities such as command; it is a source of delight and a destroyer of sin.
By the recollection of this thousand-syllable Vidyā, one obtains the vehicle;
it is praised as the secret, supreme abode consisting of a thousand phonemes. (61)
O Great Queen Śrī, this supreme Manu is your protector;
he is constantly devoted to you, even at the cost of his own life.
At the conclusion of the recitation of the Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā,
one should daily offer a thousand prostrations to Nārāyaṇī and likewise a thousand prostrations to Śrī.
Having realized this pair of knowledges once, one shall undoubtedly achieve the goal;
it must not be given even to a disciple, nor to a wife, nor to a kinsman.
This thousand-syllable Vidyā is more exalted than even the goddess Śviti;
it is the mother of long life and health, and the destroyer of all sins.
Ayodhyā, which abides in the wheel, is the supreme goddess consisting of all powers; she removes all diseases and wards off all fears and calamities.
Through its recollection, all sins are destroyed; it bestows the fruits of all sacrifices;
and it grants the fruits of the four aims of human life, known as virtue, wealth, desire, and liberation.
Five alone are said to belong to the Goddess Ciñciṇī, and five are said to belong to the Puruṣa;
these two groups of knowledge are thus declared to be fifteen in sequence.
Beginning with the pure name [of the deity], ending with *namaḥ*, *svāhā*, *tarpaṇa*, or *jaya*, and preceded by the pure vocative case—this is said to be the first mantra. (69)
In the two Vidyās, the word "namas" occurs at the end of the dative case, and likewise the word "svāhā";
the fourth mantra ends in the accusative case with the words "tarpayāmi" (I satiate).
The pair of mantras ending with the vocative case is the praise; thus, the fifth [mantra] has been stated.
In this way, fifteen garland-mantras that bestow fruit have been proclaimed. (71)
Or else, Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa, or both Bhavānī and Śaṅkara,
should be worshipped here with the Cakrarāja and the monthly mantras by those who are wise.
Because it consists of all obstructions, and likewise because it consists of all vidyās;
because it consists of all dharmas, and because it consists of all siddhis. (73)
Therefore, in the house of Śrīcitkatvā at Ayodhyānāracakra, Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa are to be worshipped by the one known as Rājarāja.
Bhavānī and Śaṅkara, inflamed with passion, approached one another;
they cast forth the five-fold garlands of mantras, which are the ten Vidyās. || 75 ||
Whether every six months or every year, one who is pure should remember Viṣṇu,
the Great King, the Lord of the Bhāgavatas, accompanied by Śrī.
Behold Nārāyaṇa, the descendant of Daśaratha, who is compassionate toward those who have sought refuge;
O two wives, you shall see Rāma—this is the truth indeed, there is no doubt. (77)
Having mastered the ten syllables and possessing a mind focused on the sixfold path, he should recite them daily in solitude, having conquered his senses and freed himself from sin.
To Nārāyaṇa himself, accompanied by Śrī Devī, [I offer this]—whether for divinity, immortality, or even for the state of a celestial being. (79)
Whether it be the state of a yakṣa, or the state of a kinnara, or even the state of a dvīpavāsin; or the state of a khecarā, or the state of a maharṣi, or even the state of a brahmarṣi. || 80 ||
There is no doubt that for others as well, through the grace of the Lord of the East (Indra),
the sword, sandals, and the ointment bestow the perfection of invisibility.

The eight siddhis, beginning with the power of extracting [substances] from the earth—namely speech, body, iron, and the rest—as well as subjugation, attraction, delusion, and immobilization, are all [attained]. || 82 ||
Now, Savarṇi, Arthaśva, Nityānanda, and Muktātman—
these fifteen are declared to be the perfections (siddhis) of the vidyās in their respective order.
Having respectfully touched the full water-pot with fragrant waters,
one should perform the recitation of the Satyaṣṭamālā mantra once every day.

By reciting the *Satyāhaṃsa* mantra, a barren woman shall become possessed of sons; likewise, by wearing a garland of *Satyā* beads, even a woman who is like a saline wasteland shall become fertile within a year.
The Blessed One, possessing the splendor of the sun and the brilliance of the full moon,
then pressed down upon the eight guardians of the directions, beginning with Indra, as well as upon the oceans and the mountains.
One who is unable to perform the recitation of the eightfold knowledge daily should recite the Mahāvidyā of the Goddess Śrī, namely Śraddhā itself, three times.
By studying this compendium of the Vedas and Vedānta, which contains thousands of verses from the Goddess Śruti, one daily obtains the fruit of the eightfold path of truth. 88.
This supreme [mantra] consisting of the true names of the goddesses of the Cakrāvaraṇa is such that,
even in this present age, all accomplishments (siddhis) are attained by reciting it but once.
Neither initiation nor the like is required here for those who have already received the consecration;
the compassionate Teacher has taught the thousand-syllable mantra for the sake of instruction. (90)
It is traditionally taught that one's entire property is the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) for the gods;
or rather, the prescribed amount of grain is considered the fee. (89)
In this Ayodhyā, worship has been previously described for the Lord Lākṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, who is united with the Śālagrāma stone. || 91 ||
By the mere remembrance of this, the fruit of all the Vedas along with their limbs is accomplished for him;
of this there is no doubt, and moreover, he shall become one with Brahman.
O sons of Brahmā, by the recollection here of the goddesses Aṅgāraṇa and Śrīdevī within this Vidyā, you shall become their [servants]. 94.
Just as those more compassionate than Māra protect their son out of affection for him, these [goddesses] do not protect one in the pursuit of knowledge like their own sons. || 95 ||
The illustrious Goddess, the sovereign of all, eternally accompanied by Bhagadatta,
protects his house like a mother, as long as the moon and stars endure.
And being intent on performing worship, he should recite the thousand names of the goddess Śrī—the Great Knowledge (Mahāvidyā)—along with oblations, libations, and hymns of praise. 97.
By one who desires the accomplishment of all sciences, with a self-restrained mind, this [vidyā] of Śrī, which bestows all fruits, should be recited a thousand times. 98.
"O Brahmins, this pair consisting of the root *śri* and the goddess Śrī, totaling one thousand syllables, has thus been narrated. What more do you wish to hear? (99)

[Thus ends the fortieth chapter in the Uttarabhāga of the *Śrīmadanuttarabrahmatattvarahasya*, the *Dāśarathīya Tantra*, which is a compendium of the essential meaning of the Vedas, concerning the majesty of the *Rājarājavidyā*.]
The yogins said:
The Nārāyaṇī, consisting of a thousand syllables, the embodiment of truth, and the supreme Śrī—having heard it from the lotus-like mouth [of the Lord], she was revealed even in ancient times. || 1 ||
We wish to hear once more that unsurpassed knowledge of Brahman which grants all desired things; please deign to speak it out of compassion. || 2 ||
The Blessed One said:
O foremost sons of Brahmā, Sanaka and the others, who are firm in their vows, listen:
this is the great practice (*sādhana*) of the Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā, which bestows all that is desired.
Formerly, at Vaikuṇṭha, Hari spoke to the goddess Śrī concerning the river Nirañjanī, which bestows yoga upon those who possess it. || 4 ||
That goddess spoke to the high-souled Kardama;
he too was her father, the yogi, the venerable sage Kardama.
Thus it was spoken by me to my disciples, the great yogis:
"The Lord of Lakṣmī, the Lord of the Raghus, the ascetic Hari, who is the goal of those [devotees]. (6)
Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of the three worlds, whose nature is bliss, is Rāma, the son of Daśaratha; he is the letter *U* and the Yavana.
Out of respect for King Jarāsandha and others, he related this means of accomplishment, the medicine for existence, which destroys the king of old age and death.
In private, I shall declare that secret sādhana,
which, when proclaimed after observing the proper place and time, enables one to cross over the ocean of existence.
He who bestows upon his own disciple the singular knowledge of the bliss of Brahman, which is the fruit of the Queen of Queens (Rājarājeśvarī), is declared to be a true Guru.
I pray to that Lord who teaches the conduct of a resident disciple as described by Svāyambhuva and others.
The wise know him to be an Ācārya who respectfully teaches the procedure for the Śrīmatvāśā-vidyā, along with its constituent parts, to his disciples.
He who shall proclaim to his disciples the hymn of the Bhagavadraśmi, the eternal Brahmavidyā, the glorious eight-syllabled lore (vidyā). || 13 ||
They describe that all-pervading Lord Hari as the one who sustains him, the one of great wisdom,
who is accompanied by all his rays and is the very essence of the nectar of the feet of Śrī.
Śiva will tell that which is of the nature of Nārāyaṇa;
they call him the Supreme Ācārya, the radiant Brahmā and Śaṅkara.
The auspicious Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā, known as Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇī,
is secreted within all the Vedas and also within the sixty Āgamas.
The wise one who shall speak it into the ear of a disciple of pure soul— that teacher is the most excellent, a wise man who is the very embodiment of the Lord himself.
Having worshipped that very Śaṅkara, the Supreme Lord, who is omniscient and the creator of all, they know him alone as the all-pervading Nārāyaṇa, the most excellent.
Because he is worthy of reverence in every respect, the Great Sage is called "Guru"; he is more venerable than even the gods such as Brahmā and Rudra, owing to his being worshipped by them. (19)
"The teacher is said to be the one who bestows the fruit of devotion;
yet, without knowing the proper time and without considering a suitable place," (20)
He who bestows the Great Vidyā shall not fall from his status as a true guru;
in the month of Madhu there may be suffering, but in Mādhava there is the abundance of jewels.
In Jyeṣṭha, death is proclaimed; in Āṣāḍha, the destruction of wisdom; in Śrāvaṇa, there shall be the constant attainment of one's desired goals. (22)
In the month of Bhādrapada, there will be great affliction to the body;
in Āśvina, there shall be prosperity such as wealth and grain at every step.
In the month of Kārttika, the singular realization of the bliss of Brahman arises;
in Mārgaśīrṣa, the fortune of recitation (japa-lakṣmī) comes to him—of this there is no doubt.

O wise ones, when the moon is in the constellation Jyeṣṭhā, knowledge perishes; during the commencement of rituals, there is sorrow; and in the month of Māgha, there is the sight of the bull [the Sun] in the Aśleṣā constellation.
The complete accomplishment of all undertakings occurs in the month of Phālguna;
specifically on the second, third, eleventh, or likewise the tenth lunar day.
The fifth, the full moon day of the twelfth month, and the thirteenth lunar day—these are the three tithis that constitute great meritorious periods (mahāpuṇya). || 27 ||
There may be the defects of the nine months and the eclipses of the moon and the sun; thus one should examine the place and time, as well as the virtues and vices of the disciple. (28)
The wise, compassionate, and all-pervading Guru should reveal the Vidyā even at the cost of his life; it bestows sovereignty and prosperity, and should be protected at all times. (29)
With a mind full of devotion, she offered her lotus feet even her husband, sons, and others;
likewise, Śacī offered her husband Kaikaya, the son of Pradhāna, along with his attendants.
He who acts with great wisdom is known as the most excellent disciple;
even when struck with the hands by one whose faults have been removed and subdued.
He who, though severely beaten by those who are deceitful and harsh, considers it a great favor that [the teacher] has come to him—[he is a true disciple]. (32)
With a mind free from all parts (nirvikalpa), that disciple is said to be liberated;
likewise, for such a learned disciple, [this knowledge] is the means of crossing the ocean of worldly existence.
There is no doubt that the Goddess of Liberation (Mukti Lakṣmī) is held in the hand [of the Guru];
having performed service, one whose mind has come as a servant to his lotus feet [attains her]. 34.
Having daily recited the Śrīmadaṣṭākṣarī Vidyā with devotion,
one should daily recite the Rājarājeśvarī Vidyā according to the prescribed method.
I shall proclaim the means of accomplishment; listen, O you who praise Brahman! By merely hearing them, unsurpassed perfection arises for you. (36)
I shall now further describe that most excellent vow of nine nights and so forth, known as Vāta; may the supreme sages listen. (37)
As it has been said: "One who observes the vow for nine nights during the three days [of the month] in the month of Madhu attains the granting of all perfections. (38)
Having spent either nine nights or three days in the cow-pen,
with his mind entirely focused on the calves, he remained there.
Having become composed of the Supreme Brahman, his own body consisting of splendor,
the Blessed One, like the bull of his own nature, beheld the Lord who was agitated.
He beholds the Self by means of the self as the locus of the essence of Brahman-bliss;
or else, in the month of Madhu, he protects the footless from the very beginning.
Having performed three hundred thousand recitations with the permission of his teacher,
he completed the daily fire-oblation for the Mother of the Vedas, who was afflicted by hunger.
O Ujjayinī, one should sit with palms joined in reverence, meditating upon Nārāyaṇa situated in the center of the solar disc, while reciting the Nārāyaṇa-sūkta.
Having chanted daily in solitude the glorious eight-syllabled vidyā— the great mantra of Vāsudeva— one hundred and more times.
Thereafter, one should recite the mantra consisting of three hundred syllables;
having recited the twelve-syllable mantra of Ramā one hundred and eight times.
Having thus constantly recited this mantra of Rājarājeśvarī for subjugation,
one should then recite it twenty-eight thousand times twice over.
Having performed the recitation of the *Atharva-vauma* mantra, one should recite the *varma* mantra five times every day;
and before the pair of feet of the preceptor, one should daily offer a smile first.
The wise man should offer gold—either a single *niṣka* or even more—daily with devotion, casting aside any greed for wealth. (48)
Sleeping on the ground, having conquered anger, eating only fruit or sacrificial oblation (havis), or even eating only one meal during the three days beginning with the ninth day. (49)
Subsisting either on milk or on *phalaka* fruits, one should mutter the *Sāvitrī* as before, as well as the glorious eight-syllabled mantra (*vidyā*) and the other deities beginning with Viṣṇu. (50)
Having first designated that armor,
one should constantly recite the mantra twenty-five times during each of the three periods of the day.
One should offer a pair of *raṇa* sounds to the Preceptor, along with *savarṇaka*, *simi*, *rgani*, and *pha*;
or alternatively, one may offer each of these individually for three days.
With the thought that she is Mahālakṣmī, one should respectfully offer a single ornament each day to the wife of the preceptor as well. || 53 ||
Or one should offer a single *niṣka* or even half of that,
or whatever excellent ornament is available, on the birthday of Śrī Rāma.
On two days, one should offer a *niṣka* or half of it [of gold],
which possesses the splendor of a hundred Indras at the festival of the birth of Śrī Rāma and other such occasions.

This is declared by those who know the Vedas and the Vedāngas to be the gateway to great gifts (mahādāna). On the tenth or eleventh lunar day, it is performed by the wise for the sake of the ancestors.
There, twelve pillars were erected one by one;
they say that the twelfth pillar was equal to the peak, bestowing great prosperity.
On the twelfth day, when the sun has risen, in the presence of the best of teachers,
having consecrated the clarified butter (ghṛta) according to the ritual rules, [he should offer] the essence of the cow's milk.
Having offered one hundred and eight oblations with the venerable Aṣṭākṣarī Vidyā,
one should offer the clarified butter of Kapila into the fire one thousand and one hundred times.
Alternatively, one should offer pure cow-ghee with the eight-syllable Vidyā,
or with the six-syllable Vaiṣṇava mantra of Vāsudeva.

Then, having offered twenty-eight portions with the *Śrīsūkta* into the twelve-petaled [lotus], and having likewise offered one hundred oblations into the fire with the *Tryaddhagavya* mantra with devotion; 61.
Having offered oblations twenty-eight times for the Vidyā known as Rājarājeśvarī, one should thereafter offer oblations five times with the Mantras of the Armour (Varman). || 62 ||
Having performed the oblation with recitations and other rites, and having subsequently made the offering of the sacrifice to Brahman (brahmārpaṇa),
he should prostrate himself with all eight limbs before the fire at the conclusion of the rite.
Having prostrated with devotion before the pair of feet of the teacher,
he established two auspicious sacrificial pits even while living as a householder.
The preceptor should place upon his ears either other ornaments,
or a rosary of rudrākṣa beads, or even an ornament of pearls.
Having given a jewel-ornament or another gift to the ears of the preceptor,
one should present a Śālagrāma stone along with a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) to the Guru.
May I not obtain the fruits of the ikṣurā and śivā, nor even those that are sweet like sugarcane; likewise, may I never obtain a heap of plantain fruits, nor sugar, nor molasses.
One should offer excellent sandalwood paste to the pair of feet of the Preceptor and to Hari;
then, twelve well-attired women and twelve Brahmins [should also be honored]. (68)
He should be dismissed with sweet foods and fruits such as those from the south;
then, accompanied by his kinsmen, he himself should eat the remnants of the preceptor's meal.
I shall speak another secret; listen, O sons of Brahmā!
By the knowledge of which, both the mobile and immobile worlds are worshipped.
Or, on every fortnight, or six times a month, or twelve times a year,
or on special days when the sacrificial fire has been kindled.
The auspicious hymn beginning with "Keśava" and consisting of twenty-four couplets has been sung by Gautama;
having first offered oblations, one should perform the Śrīdhā offering.
The earth, fifty koṭis in extent, becomes the domain of that supreme practitioner;
he attains unimpeded movement as a perfected one (siddha) and becomes a treasury of all fortune.
Having become the abode of all fortunes and the object of worship for all prosperity,
one should then become a witness to Nārāyaṇa, with all duties fulfilled.
In the month of Madhu, having performed the great initiation and the twelve [observances],
he became manifest as Brahman himself and was liberated from heaps of sins.
The great poet and eloquent speaker Maṇdhva is a treasure-trove of knowledge;
he is a practitioner who has mastered all learning even without formal study.
Through the grace of the spiritual guide, having become free from all misfortunes,
he [attained] a multitude of wealth consisting of pearls, gems, elephants, horses, and other such riches.
Having attained great prosperity accompanied by sons, grandsons, and others,
and having reached a long life, he is liberated from all diseases.
Having enjoyed all pleasures here, both divine and human, he attains the supreme state, for [through this] a thousand members of his lineage [are likewise saved].
In the month of Madhu (Caitra), on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight,
the practitioner who has performed this *puraścaryā* becomes a perfected master (*siddha*) who destroys his enemies.
Within a year, she will certainly give birth to a son who will be a lord of the earth,
the high-souled Nārāyaṇa, accompanied by Bharata and others.
One who beholds him indeed attains a very long life; moreover, through the sight of him, one obtains supreme and great power. 82.
The mastery of powers such as *aṇimā* and others, the supreme perfection of speech,
freedom from disease, long life, and the nine treasures beginning with the conch (*śaṅkha*).
Having obtained a heap of wealth, a heap of jewels, and divine maidens,
he attains that supreme abode and enters it himself at the end of his body.
O Brahmins, even in a hundred years I am not able to describe the supreme fruit of the merit of that person who has heard this most excellent benefit for the soul. (85)
He who performs this most purifying vow twice is that high-souled and all-pervading Nārāyaṇa, Rāma, the son of Daśaratha.
The Lord, the benefactor of Jānakī, accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa, Rāma, and others,
was joined by Brahman-sages such as Vasiṣṭha and attended by the physicians.
When the Lord of the World, Śrī Rāma, the Supreme Self, is directly perceived, one becomes a witness to Him three times over with one's own eyes for all eternity.
O you whose self is Nārāyaṇa, all accomplishments—though otherwise impossible—become Brahmic on this earth, in heaven, among mortals, and even in the netherworld. 89.
What in this world could be unattainable for me, since my abode shall be Śrī, the singular realization of the bliss of Brahman, and the supreme recollection of past births? (90)
The power of entering another's body and so forth, as well as the [eightfold] powers such as atomization (aṇimā) and the rest,
are difficult to attain even for hosts of gods and difficult to attain even for supreme sages.
For him, nothing remains unattainable in heaven, among mortals, or in the netherworld;
he who performs this most purifying vow three times over. (92)
Month after month, he beholds with his own eyes the Lord of the World, the husband of Jānakī, the infallible Nārāyaṇa, who is the very self of Brahman.
Having first sought the supreme state of sky-faring through the garland of the eightfold yoga, he became equal in splendor to Kandarpa by means of those divine maidens.
He who performs this most purifying vow in five ways shall, by means of this very body, be freed from old age and death. (95)
Resplendent with brilliance like the sun, appearing twenty-five years of age,
he was surrounded by Siddhas, Gandharvas, Kinnaras, and the hosts of the gods, who shone like the moon.
Having been praised, I have directly beheld Lakṣmī, the consort of Nārāyaṇa;
by her grace, I have indeed attained great perfection that is difficult even for the gods to obtain.
Having ascended a celestial chariot accompanied by hundreds of divine maidens,
his body becoming composed of radiant energy, he is endowed with divine enjoyments.
The hare-marked moon and other such things, which according to worldly convention are considered eternal,
attain union with Hari at the end of the kalpa, having been surrounded by ten million crores of evil beings.
One attains this here, there is no doubt; this is the truth, the truth, O best of the twice-born!
Have no hesitation and do not lack faith, O sons of Brahmā. 100.
Herein, the Jātha sung by Atharvan and Aṅgiras will now be fully explained. || 101 ||
During the days of the month of Caitra in the spring season, by the grace of his guru,
the king of the earth recited for three hundred and ten days the eight-syllable mantra, which is the essence of the Śrīvidyā, one thousand times each day.
Having first recited [the mantra] more than a hundred times, one should then recite the name of Śrī Vāsudeva three hundred times;
having respectfully recited the Śrī Viṣṇu-vidyā, one should praise Indirā by her twelve names. (13)

O King of Kings, having respectfully recited the Manu-mantra three hundred times daily, as well as the armor-mantra eight times, one should then offer salutations with five-fold prostrations to the Witness of all the worlds and proceed to conquer.

Then, on the three days beginning with the birthday of Śrī Rāma, having wandered here for twenty-five times during the day, he offered his great beloved to the Preceptor of the Day at the Priyaga [temple]. || 105 ||

Having prostrated, one who is capable should give a *karṣa*, a *niṣka*, or half of that; however, on the three days beginning with the birthday of Śrī Rāma, one should give a *karṣa* or indeed a single *niṣka*.
Desiring the accomplishment of all goals, one should offer a small gift during the Bharaṇī [nakṣatra];
likewise, during these three days, one should worship the wife of the preceptor with the thought that she is Lakṣmī herself.

On the day of Hara, as if in a blazing fire, having respectfully offered a thousand oblations of clarified butter with the two eight-syllabled mantras, and likewise having offered one hundred and eight more here; || 108 ||
Then, having offered three hundred oblations of clarified butter with the *Śrī* mantra, the king of kings should likewise offer oblations with the *Vajra* mantras;
having also offered oblations with the armor (*varman*) mantras, he should bow before [the deity], worship him extensively, and prostrate himself.
One should certainly give two forest-earrings made of excellent gold and jewels; or one should worship with garments and groups of golden necklaces, or, if unable, with even a single ornament. (110)
Having offered the clusters of flowers and presented the fruits and the fragrance,
one should certainly give to the preceptor, who is a knower of the Veda, an excellent milch-cow together with her calf.

One should diligently observe this vow called the Nala-vrata for the sake of Nārāyaṇa, the cause of all worlds; it bestows satisfaction, grants worldly enjoyment, is highly praised, and bestows the supreme state of the birds (liberation).
Having performed worship here, those of great majesty, endowed with the powers such as *āṇimā* and having attained supreme glory,
together with their fathers, mothers, and kinsmen, ascended to the meditation that is joined with all purposes.
Having regained the memory of their former births and attained the fulfillment of their goals, they proceed to the abode of the Lord of Lakṣmī. Now,
in this month of Vaiśākha, which bestows the essence of Brahman-bliss, the twelve-night vow is sung in the Atharva Veda.
Having performed for twelve days the vow known as Japalakṣmīprabha, one becomes the very self of Nārāyaṇa; of this there is no doubt.

[Thus ends the forty-first chapter, titled "The Greatness of the King of Kings' Knowledge," in the latter portion of the *Śrīmadanuttarabrahmatattvarahasya*, the *Daśarathīya Tantra*, which is a compendium of the essential meaning of the Vedas.]
The Blessed One said:
O sons of Brahmā, I shall again fully proclaim the majesty of the Great Vidyā of the King of Kings, which bestows all desired objects upon those who practice it. 1.

The third lunar day of the waning moon in the month of Vaiśākha, falling on a Saturday, is the beginning of the Tretā Yuga; it is the auspicious birthday of Rāma, a sister-like lunar day that bestows all desired blessings.
The lords declare that Akṣayā, which bestows complete fruit when fulfilled, is the inexhaustible lunar day (tithi) at the end of the month;

she is the giver of imperishable enjoyments in heaven and liberation, and the destroyer of even great sins. Even by giving a mere morsel of food, or performing acts such as recitation (japa), one obtains here the fruit of all virtues, as well as the state of enjoyment and happiness that is inexhaustible.
And absorption into the Supreme Brahman. || 4 ||

There, the knower [of reality], having bathed with a well-composed body according to the conduct of the virtuous, and having bowed to that which is the essence of the three times, received its command upon the tip of his head; then, with a purified mind, he performed the twilight devotions. || 5 ||

Then, having performed the fire-ritual with the supreme eight-syllable mantra (*manu*) in a purified fire, one should offer oblations a thousand times with the solar seed-syllables (*saurabīja*) mixed with the three sweets (*madhutraya*) and clarified butter; or one may offer oblations of equal measure mixed with the three sweets and clarified butter, a hundred or a thousand times. Thereafter, having offered oblations with cow’s clarified butter to Śrī Vāsudeva...
And not by means of a modification. || 7 ||
O Lord, having offered three hundred oblations of excellent cow’s ghee with the Śrī-dvādaśākṣara mantra,
the King of Kings, the Lord of Māra, [attained] the supreme ghee of the best cows during the Manu-period.
Having respectfully offered a hundred oblations with *purāḥ* mantras, the best of the twice-born performed the *atyakartṛ* rite three times;
then, having offered five oblations with the *harivarma* mantras, he offered oblations of cow’s ghee with the *jaya* and other mantras.

Having circumambulated the kindled fire and offered the most excellent oblation, and having prostrated himself, he should present a pair of golden earrings, beautiful to the gods and heavy with gems. || 10 ||

If he is unable even for that, having offered his own annual food to the preceptor’s wife and at the lotus-feet of the Guru, he should then give a hundred or a thousand pieces of wealth as an offering.
Or else, one should worship with two niṣkas at the pair of the Guru’s feet, or one should offer three niṣkas of wealth;
however, one who desires the perfection of the mantra should not give that which is the entirety of one's own wealth to the lotus-feet of Śiva. || 12 ||

Having thus honored the Guru with a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) and having respectfully completed the fire-oblation (homa) and other rites, [he should offer] the three fruits—known as the *phalāvalaka*, *vārāmaya*, *bahusūla*, and *malamari*. 13.
Having offered the beautiful kandalī fruits with great devotion,
she then gave excellent sandals and garments to those practitioners who had attained the state of siddhas.

Having offered sixty palas—or at least twenty palas—of excellent *śrīcandana* to the preceptor, and having gratified the Brahmins and married women with delicious food, fruits, and monetary gifts; || 15 ||

Having attained supreme and imperishable great supernatural power through the grace of the Guru, one becomes liberated here; and for as long as an eon, one remains endowed with prosperity, possessing a glory that surpasses even that of Mahendra and Viṣṇu.
Having attained long life and health, and having acquired knowledge equal to that of Vācaspati, O Lord,
one shall possess a splendor equal to a thousand moons and obtain sons who are like the gods.
Having enjoyed pleasures here on earth and obtained two hundred crores of kinsmen, he was submerged in the burden of existence;
then, uplifted by divine and excellent lotuses as his ornament, he ascended a celestial chariot shining like the sun.
Resplendent with divine ornaments and accompanied by excellent young maidens,
he— who is difficult even for the best of yogis to attain— afterwards reaches that abode of the Lord of Lakṣmī.
On the third lunar day in the month of Vaiśākha, the Kṣayā is said to bestow success;
every year, rites such as recitation and fire-offerings should be performed for the sake of subjugation.
Having performed [the rite] according to the prescribed method and having given the fee (dakṣiṇā) to the preceptor,
one should perform the offering of fruit and the salutation to Hari.
One attains imperishable success that bestows the three goals of life;
there is inexhaustible long life and supreme, undecaying health.
O Indra, [he attains] inexhaustible and great fortune, resembling the Lord of the Mind (Kāmadeva),
and inexhaustible and great knowledge, resembling the surging waves of the Gaṅgā.
He obtained inexhaustible and most abundant prosperity consisting of sons, grandsons, and so forth,
as well as imperishable divine and human enjoyments.
At the end of their enjoyment, they attained a great and powerful abode;
having satisfied the one who grants inexhaustible desires, they reached that state which is praised by Dakṣa. || 25 ||
They call this third [lunar day] "Inexhaustible," which brings about inexhaustible glory;
it is the most supreme among the sixty-three lunar days. (26)
On this third day of the bright fortnight in Vaiśākha, there is the attainment of success through destruction;
the auspicious Vidyā of Rājarājeśvarī, conjoined with the fire-oblation (homa).

O twice-born ones, having obtained the permission of the preceptor, a pure person should perform this *puraścaryā* of the glorious eight-syllable mantra on the third lunar day that falls on a Tuesday.
One would not attain great accomplishment in a single day;
however, he who performs this *puraścaraṇa* every year [does so]. (29)
One always obtains only auspicious gains and inexhaustible riches, and indeed satisfies one's ancestors;
even for those submerged in hells, this [attainment] occurs at the end of the kalpa, which is difficult to obtain even for a yogi.
The supreme abode is *ghamā*, joined with a thousand lineages;
by this alone, in two days, the *puraścaryā* arising from the *śāta* [mantra] is accomplished.
The emaciated state of the Lord of Lakṣmī is declared to be the great, perfect Siddhi;
now, another Siddhi will also be described here on a certain day.
In the bright fortnight of the month known as Nabhasya, she is indeed endowed with that [lunar mansion],
even when joined with the Gaṇḍa yoga or with Sukarman.
If the eleventh lunar day (Ekādaśī) is conjoined with the moon on the morning, or at twilight, or at midday, or at evening; || 35 ||
At the hour of Brahma or at midnight, they call this auspicious Great Yoga by the name Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, the King of Yogas.
The supreme sages declare that Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, when joined with the Muhūrta and Tapa or with the Ṛkṣa and Vāruṇa, is endowed with yoga.
Whoever on this earth performs even a little recitation, fire-offering, or other rites here, the Lord of Mahālakṣmī himself, that ocean of compassion, becomes pleased. (38)
One who diligently practices this for ten thousand years, remaining constantly amidst five fires, shall attain great perfection that destroys death itself.
Even more than that, by giving even a small amount at the lotus feet of the preceptor here, he attains double the siddhi; of this there is no doubt.
Pure, having chanted the glorious eight-syllabled mantra ten thousand times every day for a thousand years, and having offered oblations a thousand times every day; 41.
Whatever fruit one obtains through the science known as Rājarāja,
even by offering a single oblation, the fruit from this [other practice] is twice as great.
Through this yoga, one attains Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa; of this there is no doubt.
One should recite the mantra of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa a thousand times with the Brahma-vidyā.
By worshipping daily with lotuses and water-lilies mixed with *tulasī*,
and by offering even a single flower there, one obtains twice that much fruit.
O best of the twice-born, the wise man inevitably attains these sixteen great gifts, of which the Tulāpuruṣa is the foremost. (45)
Whoever gives to these twice-born ones every day for a thousand years, even if it be only a single *nikā* of gold, that gift is truly bestowed upon Atri and Āpidaubja. (46)
By giving even more than that, one necessarily attains double the fruit;
this great yoga is obtained through great fortune and not otherwise.
Bestowing the fruit of vows and sacrifices, and granting the merit of ten million gifts at sacred fords, Yoga has arrived here this very night, shining like the sun. 48.

Having prostrated before the pair of lotus feet of the Teacher, which bestow both worldly enjoyment and liberation, and having bathed in a sacred ford or a lake while remaining pure, by the permission of the Preceptor; 49.
One should drink the water used for washing the lotus feet of the preceptor;
[this was done] in the city of Ayodhyā, which is endowed with Śālagrāma stones.
Having worshipped Lakṣmī and the Lord of Lakṣmī according to the previously mentioned rite,
one should worship them one thousand three hundred times with the Brahma-vidyā.
For ten thousand years, worship [Him] daily with ten million oblations of *kuma* flowers, accompanied by the three-thousand-plus-verse *Brahmavidyā*.
One attains the fruit of well-performed deeds by offering even a single flower to this leader of yoga while reciting the Brahma-vidyā. (53)
One obtains the fruit [of that] for half of ten thousand years; there is no doubt in this matter.
Then, in the presence of the preceptor, when the *nala* has been consecrated according to the rules...
First, the wise should offer one hundred and eight oblations with sesame seeds smeared with cow's ghee and mixed with the "triple honey," while reciting the Sāvitrī mantra.

Then, one should offer into the fire one thousand oblations, plus a hundred more, using the milk of the eight auspicious substances, sesame seeds, the products of the cow (gavya), and clarified butter.
Having offered one hundred and eight oblations for each into the sacrificial fire with the mantra of Vāsudeva and the six-syllabled Vaiṣṇava mantra, || 57 ||

Then, having offered five hundred oblations of pure clarified butter into the fire with the twelve-syllable Mahālakṣmī mantra, one who has performed good deeds should offer oblations with the [mantra's] rays.
Having become pure through that supreme knowledge which bestows the sovereignty of kings,
one should diligently offer twenty-eight oblations of cow-products into the fire with devotion.
Thereafter, the practitioner should offer oblations five times into the fire with pure clarified butter, using the twenty-one armor-mantras (varma-mantra).
Having subsequently performed the oblation with recitations and other rites, and having made the offering of the Brahman-surrender (brahmārpaṇa),
he then prostrated with reverence before the pair of feet of the preceptor.
One should present a pair of earrings made of sixty *māṣakas* of gold and adorned with rubies to the two ears of the preceptor.
Then, having offered two garments that are very fine, soft, and stainless,
he should place a small fragment of a Śālagrāma stone into his hand.
One should give one's entire property as a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), or wealth sufficient for a year’s subsistence,
or twenty-four nikaṇas, or twelve nikaṇas.
One must certainly give the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā); one should not offer it deficiently.
A single cow that yields much milk, accompanied by her calf, should be given as a gift.
Accompanied by sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā) and measuring four cubits on all sides, these vessels, when filled with water, should be sent to his residence by one desiring success.
One who desires prosperity must perform the obligatory giving;
however, for those who possess power and are wealthy, I shall describe the *vakṣyotāddī* [offering].
One should present to the preceptor two khārīs of salt-earth, together with its increase, accompanied by abundant sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā). || 68 ||
O sons of Brahmā, a pair of earrings must certainly be given;
one should also present ornaments such as rings, waist-bands, and so forth. 69.
One should give twelve cows along with their calves and accompanied by ritual fees (dakṣiṇā),
as well as a Śālagrāma stone with a fee of one hundred thousand niṣkas.
Having given [the gift], he should afterwards offer a heap of sesame seeds along with a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā);
or else, one who possesses wealth should give other great gifts (mahādānas).
Even by one who is incapable, the aforementioned supreme gift should be given here in this great Yogarāja, which is designated as Nārāyaṇa and characterized by the hundred thousand [recitations].
Having performed even a single oblation with sesame seeds soaked in honey and ghee,
one enjoys twice the fruit of ten million sesame seed oblations.
Having given even a single *niṣka* of gold to a spiritual teacher (*deśika*), one obtains the eternal fruit of giving the entire mountain Meru in gold. (74)
Having offered cow’s ghee twenty-eight times by the king of kings,
the merit of ten million *gāyatrī* oblations is secured, which is imperishable along with its scriptural authority.
The fruit that is declared to be inexhaustible by the ancient supreme sages, resulting from twelve million oblations of the glorious eight-syllable mantra—[that fruit one shall enjoy]. (76)
Whatever fruit is obtained by ten million oblations with the twelve-syllable mantra of Rāma, accompanied by complete sacrificial fees and a horse sacrifice, [is attained by this]. (77)
Whatever fruit is ordained by the Vedas, even that fruit is doubled through the yoga of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa; this is certain, there is no doubt.
Even by a hundred killings of Brahmins, or ten thousand drinks of liquor, or even by a hundred thefts of gold, or a hundred murders of gurus; || 79 ||
Even one who has performed [meritorious deeds] for many thousands of births is not liberated from it;
having attained supreme good fortune, one should worship the ten-fold splendor of Kanda.
Having obtained on the surface of the earth eternal sovereignty, filled with wealth, grain, and the like, and strewn with heaps of jewels; || 81 ||
Having become one who has reached the state of being, resembling the life-force of all sciences, he is liberated, possessing all fruits, and free from all diseases. || 82 ||
Having extracted the essence of millions of flower buds— long life, all manner of enjoyments, both divine and human— he attained the abode of the flavor of Brahman-bliss.
One who is essentially Māra-yaṇa attains the eternal state directly;
this is the practice of the Great Vidyā of the King of Kings, which grants all desired objects.
O Brahmins, this has been briefly stated; hereafter, more shall be spoken on this matter.

[Thus ends the forty-second chapter in the Uttarabhāga of the *Śrīmadanuttarabrahmatattvarahasya*, the *Dāśarathīya-tantra*, which is a compendium of the essential meaning of the Vedas, concerning the majesty of the *Rājarājavidyā*.]
The Blessed One said:
O best of yogis, sons of Brahmā, firm in your vows, listen!
O King of Kings, this is the supreme, unsurpassed Great Knowledge (Mahāvidyā) known as Śeṣa-mahāhya. || 1 ||
In the previous Brāhma-kalpa, the recollection of the Teacher was performed day after day, followed thereafter by the contemplation of the knowledge of Brahman according to one's capacity. || 2 ||
Then, there is the recollection of the birth of the garland of rays of the Blessed One,
and after that, the recollection of the Śrīdevī and the Rāśmi-vidyās.
Then follows the Lalitānusmṛti, either twenty-eight times or twenty-four times;
then the Gāyatrī, the Āsana-mantra, and the Abhitya-homa thereafter.
Every day, he performed the worship of the sixteen-syllable mantra of Śrīdatta accompanied by its auxiliary sciences (aṅgavidyās), as well as the worship of the fifteen-syllable mantra of Śrī.
Then, day after day, [he recited] the Rājarāja Mahāvidyā;
thereafter, the two thousand-syllable Mahāvidyās, and beyond that, the three.
Whether at the time of Brahma (midday), or in the morning, or at midday, or during the two twilights,
one should likewise perform the daily construction of the Vaiṣṇava armor.
O Lord of Sacrifice, that which is known as Yāti is considered the great knowledge (mahāvidyā) beyond the mind;
it is called the complete Yāti, the auspicious bringer of all accomplishments.
The recitation of the Brahmavidyā at the Brāhma hour, the remembrance of the Śrīpādukā, and thereafter the recollection of the Bhagavadraśmisūkta. || 9 ||
Then the twilight worship (saṃdhyopāsti) is prescribed, followed by the daily fire-oblation (nityahoma);
thereafter, the constant recitation of the glorious eight-syllabled mantra (aṣṭākṣarī-vidyā) a thousand times.
Then, whether it be five hundred or even a hundred,
[he taught] the Vidyās beginning with Vāsudeva, just as Rātryājamaujava did.
Or else, there is the recitation of the glorious twelve-syllable vidyā, the mark of sovereignty,
four hundred, five hundred, three hundred, or even one hundred times.
We perform the recitation of the fifteen-syllable Śrīsūkta three hundred times daily,
or one hundred and eight times, or even twenty-one times.
Then follows the recollection of the unsurpassed knowledge of Brahman;
thereafter, at evening as well, the recollection of the great knowledge of the Lord of Sacrifice.
This other Yakṣī-mantra has been proclaimed as bestowing the attainment of complete fruits; it is the constant recitation of the Brahma-vidyā, which is superior to all other mantras. 15.

Then follows the daily fire-oblation (nityahoma), as well as the worship of the glorious eight-syllable mantra and the seat (āsana) of Vāsudeva; according to one's capacity, one should perform the recitation of the Vaiṣṇava mantra.
Or, with a serene mind, one should daily recite the twelve-syllable mantra of Lakṣmī one hundred and eight times, or as many times as possible.
One should recite twenty-eight times every day. || 19 ||
Even for one who is incapable, these two [mantras] are said to be complete when there is constant remembrance of the Great Vidyā of the King of Kings. || 20 ||
Whether it be twenty-eight, ten, or twelve times, by whatever [number] the cavity is completely filled, the fruit is produced from that very seat. || 21 ||
There is no doubt that this is attained; for this very purpose I speak.
Even one who has not studied the scriptures, or even one devoid of sacrifices, [attains it] day by day.
Although he had fallen away from the Vedic Agnihotra, the sovereign of kings and queens, having practiced the Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇī-vidyā according to all the Śrutis, [attained the highest state]. (23)

Then, having made the proclamation according to his ability, the one devoted to his guru and firm in his vows daily attained the fruit of reciting the entire Veda along with the Āgamas, as if he had mastered them all.
Even one who has not studied other sciences will [attain mastery] here every day; of this there is no doubt.
By offering even a single oblation with the *rājarājya* vidyā, [one gains such power]. (25)
By remembering this great vidyā of the King of Kings with daily devotion, one constantly obtains the full fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice along with its complete sacrificial fees.
Ten million great mantras become perfected here even without the preliminary rites (puraścaraṇa) such as recitation (japa) and fire-offerings (homa);
of this there is no doubt. || 27 ||
The eleventh day of the bright fortnight, conjoined with the second [tithi], joined with Friday, and associated with the Citrā asterism. || 28 ||
This yoga of Prasannalakṣmī is difficult to obtain on the surface of the earth;
this eternal yoga is attained only once every twelve years. (29)
Among the yogas, Vyatīpāta is the most excellent, bestowing all accomplishments;
among the days of the week, the day of Bhārgava (Venus) is supreme, and among the lunar days, the eleventh and the fourteenth are foremost.
This yoga, which inspires awe in all directions, is difficult to find on earth;
it bestows the nature of Brahman, grants complete perfection, and fulfills all desires.
For him who, with senses subdued, performs here fire-offerings, recitations, and other rites,
Nārāyaṇa becomes his master, endowed with the fortune of sovereignty.
There is no doubt that she is the truth itself;
it is said that Lakṣmī, the goddess Kamalā, is pleased with the devotion of her entire host.
She who grants desired objects becomes indeed the beloved of Hari, the creator;
she is the mother of all the worlds, Nārāyaṇa himself. || 34 ||
He himself declares this once and for all to his devotees in the abode of Vaikuṇṭha,
when he is united with the gracious Kamalā in the state of eternal union.
Whether it be the eight-syllable mantra of Yoga, the Rājarāja-mantra, ghee, excellent sacrificial fuel, fire, or even whatever else made of gold, he offers it as an oblation.
Having placed [this] at the feet of the Guide, one becomes the foremost among the perfected ones (siddhas) today;
moreover, O Supreme One, I shall grant you the highest honor, surpassing even me.
This power of consciousness, inseparable from me, is Mahālakṣmī, who possesses both Śrī and Umā;
she truly becomes gracious toward this devotee—of this there is no doubt. (38)
Having bathed in the Gautra [tirtha], which bestows serene fortune and grants the attainment of all perfections,
and likewise having completed the daily rites after honoring the preceptors, || 39 ||
Afterwards, into the consecrated fire, one should offer a thousand three hundred oblations of Kapila cow's ghee with the eight-syllable vidyā of Śrīmat.
Having offered as oblation either the ghee of a blue cow or pure cow's ghee, one should then recite the mantra of Vāsudeva one hundred and eight times.
Then, having offered oblations with the Viṣṇu-mantra, one should perform one hundred and eight offerings for Śrī using that twelve-syllable mantra, or else for Śrīrājyalakṣmī.
Having offered five hundred oblations into the fire with the mantra known as Rājarājeśvarī,
one should then offer one hundred and eight, or even twenty-eight, more.
The venerable brothers of Dharma should perform the vow by means of fivefold oblations;
having offered with recitations and lamps, they should perform the final oblation to Brahmā.
Having circumambulated the fire clockwise and bowed at the feet of the preceptor,
one should respectfully offer two bows with perfumes, flowers, and jewels.
It should be joined with the goddess Vahakṣmī, accompanied by a calf, and provided with a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā). || 45 ||
In that case, one should offer a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) consisting of wealth acquired through desire.
Or half of that, or half of that again, or even two gold pieces;
one should cause her to be clothed in garments and honor her with ornaments.
One attains great accomplishment; what is the use of much further talk?
If on the full moon day of the month of Puṣpa, it should be a Sunday, [then one attains success]. (48)
If the asterism is Puṣyā, that yoga is named Rāja;
this one, named Bhūteśvara, is for those who possess the wisdom of the Lord of Great Fortune.
O sons of Brahmā, if there should be the extraction of Soma therein,
this yoga is a great cintāmaṇi jewel, difficult to obtain on earth.
Therefore, for three days prior to that, having subdued his senses,
sleeping on the ground and eating sacrificial food (haviṣya), he [should recite] the glorious eight-syllabled mantra.
He constantly recites the Prajāpottanā mantra one thousand five hundred times;
Vāsudeva is the great vidyā, the six-syllabled [mantra] that destroys the Bauddha heresy.
Having recited the great twelve-syllable mantra one hundred and eight times,
and then having propitiated the gracious Lakṣmī, one should recite [the mantra] five hundred times.
One should recite the Rājarāja Mahāvidyā one hundred and eight times,
or twenty-eight times, when the moon has reached the asterism of Citrā.
Having bathed there, with his soul purified, he honored the feet of his preceptor; then, having offered water for the feet and other services, he sat there surrounded by his kinsmen.
Then, one should offer cow’s ghee twenty-one times at the beginning of the Veda-measures;
likewise, sesame seeds mixed with ghee five hundred and ten thousand times.
Having offered oblations with the Śrīmad-atharvaṇa mantra, and having offered twelve times with the Vidyā of Vāsudeva, he should then likewise offer with the Vaiṣṇavī Vidyā.
Then, one should offer clarified butter either twelve hundred times, or three hundred times, or even just one hundred times, for the sake of attaining sovereignty or the marks of royalty.

Having offered oblations twenty-eight times, one should bind the *bhāra* as in the case of Sundarī; then, having performed the sacrifice with the *yājyā* and other mantras, one should offer the *brahmārpaṇa-homa*.
Having prostrated with the eight limbs and performed circumambulation, he then bowed down before the two feet of the preceptor, who was like a blazing fire.
Having gathered gold, one must certainly offer a pair of earrings, weighing six, four, or three mānas, to the preceptor.
Then, having worshipped the preceptor with divine offerings and fragrant substances,
the wise disciple should offer his entire possession, whatever remains as he stands before him.
Then one should offer wealth amounting to sixteen varṣas to the preceptor;
or one should present twenty-four niṣkas, or half of that.
One must certainly give land abounding in grain for many years to a worthy family; one should give even a stone from the foot of a *śāla* tree to a person who is destitute of food.
The king should bestow the ten gifts, beginning with the cow, upon those learned in the Vedas; he should also give the Tulā-hiraṇya-garbha and other such gifts.
In this yoga known as Cintāmaṇi, which is not difficult to obtain even in the three worlds,
whatever one desires is traditionally held to yield all results.
Then, with the thought that she is Mahālakṣmī herself, the best of practitioners should worship the beloved of the Guru with garments and ornaments as well. (67)
Though powerless and unfortunate, having cast aside even the Śūdrakas,
he went as far as Alaṅkā to the ears of the two preceptors.
Having offered a single new, fine garment for the Śūdra,
one should give twelve suvarṇas, or otherwise offer one niṣka for a Vaiśya.
Having personally given a very pure dwelling and abundant ornaments to the wife of the preceptor— who is like Lakṣmī herself— the most excellent woman should give as much as she is able.
At that time, one should also honor the teacher’s son, grandson, and others; then, having gained confidence, one should give a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) to the Brahmins.
After that, one should release the boar from the snare and thereafter perform the rite with the weapon.
On the following day, Brahmins and an equal number of married women (suvāsinyas) should be fed.
On the occasion of a lunar or solar eclipse, or on the day of the rising of Jupiter,
a Śālagrāma stone along with a portion of the earth from Mount Aśelā should be given, accompanied by a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
Having done this, whether during an eclipse of the sun or moon,
one would obtain the merit of giving away tens of millions of worlds and universes.

When the preliminary rite (*puraścaryā*) has been completed one hundred times accompanied by the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), the glorious eight-syllabled mantra surely attains its most exalted perfection. (75)
Even that which is difficult for the gods and great sages to attain, such as sovereignty over all desired objects and the like, they obtain. (76)
The practitioner becomes one whose command is unimpeded everywhere and who has attained perfection;
even Śakra and the other guardians of the directions, along with the great sages, honor him. (77)
She bestowed upon him a body possessing a splendor equal to that of the King of Kings, Kāmadarpa,
and a knowledge comparable to that of Bṛhaspati.

Death at one's own will, the recollection of past births, the power of moving through the air, and the attainment of sons, grandsons, and other riches, as well as all kinds of enjoyments—[these he shall obtain]. (79)
Having given [the gift] directly before the Lord of the World for as long as he lives, the Lord himself asks him: "Is this auspicious and firm [gift] given by you to us? (80)
The new moon day in the month of Puṣpa, conjoined with a Monday, occurring during a lunar eclipse and endowed with the Vaiṣṇava asterism (Śravaṇā), [is most auspicious]. || 81 ||
This ritual application for the sake of the Blessed Lady is known by the name Mahodaya;
however, if it belongs to one whose name ends in "arka," it is remembered as Dadhodiya.
This pair of yogas is difficult to attain even in the three worlds, even by those distinguished for twenty-four years or twelve years. (83)
The king of yoga, the twin-fold brilliance of the foremost of sections, is obtained;
this is the name of all things, and there is nothing on earth that exists apart from it, whether in sound or in form.
If the *abhraṅga-karman* were performed here by the most excellent practitioners, even a thousand suns would not be able to achieve such a result. (85)
In the great yoga of Ardhodaya, or even in Mahodaya,
it is impossible to describe the fruit of that person’s auspicious deed.

Whether during the Ardhodaya or Mahodaya, it is impossible even for the Lord of the Gods himself to describe the infinite merit gained by one who performs recitation, meditation, or the act of giving with the prescribed qualities.
Is he the thousand-headed Blessed One, or the Infinite, or the five-faced one, or the Lord of the worlds?
Is he the four-faced one born from the lotus, or the six-faced son of the wielder of the thunderbolt? || 88 ||
At Mahodaya, all the gods are capable of proclaiming the fruit of merit;
having properly bathed in the excellent Yoga at Mahodaya and having bowed to the true teacher. (89)
Śrī Viṣṇuvarmā, too, having recited [the name] once, beheld Nārāyaṇa in the yoga known as Mahodaya, which is called Vārddhīdaya, during his universal sovereignty.
Whatever auspicious act one performs, such as a fire sacrifice (homa) or giving gifts (dāna), one obtains the eternal fruit of ten million times ten million preliminary rites (puraścaryā). || 91 ||
In this matter, by certainly offering a golden coin (niṣka) at the pair of feet of the Guru, one undoubtedly obtains the fruit of giving a thousand cows. 92.
O Brahmins, there is no such great conjunction anywhere on the surface of the earth;
nor is there any merit equal to even a single oblation offered here. (93)
The gift of Mount Meru and the gift of a coin are not equal in this world, nor do they differ in their benefit;
I shall not speak further—listen, O sons of Brahmā! (94)
In the yoga called Mahodaya, or even when there is the rising of Saṃśraya,
one should perform a bath with ocean water there with great care.
Then, for the sake of removing all sins, those who are composed in mind should bathe in the waters of the Bāgīrathī, Godāvarī, Yamunā, or others.
There, having risen early in the morning, he should apply a foot-cloth (*daśikā*) to his feet;
then, having bathed and purified his self, he should always perform the twilight devotions (*saṃdhyā*).
Then, having returned to his own house and properly installed the sacrificial vessel,
he should take either the clarified butter from a tawny cow (kāpila-ājya) or pure, unadulterated clarified butter.
Having offered [the oblation] eight hundred times with the Sāvitrī and other mantras at the beginning,
