one should offer ghee twenty-eight times with the Brahmavidyā mantra.
Having invoked there the Lord of Lakṣmī, the Master of the World, the flawless Nārāyaṇa, [one should offer] more than a thousand oblations into the kindled fire.
Thereafter, one should offer oblations of cow-derived clarified butter with the *śrīmad-aṣṭākṣara-vidyā*,
with the mantra of Vāsudeva, and then with the six-syllabled [mantra] of Viṣṇu.
Having offered oblations twenty-eight times individually into the fire (jātavedas) with the Śrī-dvādaśākṣarī mantra, or else with the Rājya-lakṣmī mantra; || 102 ||
One should offer three hundred oblations of clarified butter with the Rājarājeśvarī Vidyā;
having offered twenty-eight oblations with the mantras, one then bestows the water.

One should offer oblations five times into the fire; having offered there with recitations and other rites, and having performed the expiatory oblations, one should perform the oblation of "offering to Brahman. (104)
Having circumambulated the fire and bowed with devotion to the preceptor, the wise one should then offer his entire being as an oblation into the fire. 105.
Subsequently, with garments and ornaments, he gave a cow yielding much milk along with its calf, in a place certainly free from danger and endowed with abundant crops.
One must certainly give land, for it is superior to the ten types of gifts;
having given this to the best of the twice-born, one should then give the beloved wife to the preceptor.
One should certainly adorn it with golden ornaments and offer it; [it shall be] endowed with abundant crops. (106)
One should certainly give gifts of wealth, food, and clothing; thereafter, having given to the best of the twice-born, one should then give what is dear to the preceptor.
One should adorn it with golden ornaments and collections of garments, and then one should personally offer great gifts. 108.
Alternatively, having bowed to the preceptor and offered ornaments according to one's capacity, as well as fine garments and wealth sufficient for a year’s food and clothing; || 108 ||
Having abandoned greed for wealth, the preceptor should place four, two, or even one-quarter of a *viprātinika* at the feet [of the disciple]. (109)
With supreme devotion, one should offer the auspicious fourfold set to the preceptor’s wife;
likewise, a vessel of bell-metal, half of that size, or accompanied by fruit.
The best of practitioners must certainly give as a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) a golden ornament accompanied by fine cloth. || 111 ||
Having spread out from the various fields as much as possible,
he gave twenty-one beautiful women who were well-adorned.
Then one should feed fifteen of the most excellent brahmins, and after that,
satisfy them with appropriate portions of sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā).
One should satisfy the sons, grandsons, and other descendants of the Guru with offerings of food;
thereafter, with the permission of the Preceptor, one may eat together with one's kinsmen.
Thus, having performed the worship of Mahodaya with devotion at the four junctions (saṃdhyās), or likewise at the half-junction (ardhodaya), one attains eternal [bliss]. 15.
Even by those who have committed sins arising from thousands of millions of births, one is immediately liberated; [the enemy] becomes submissive and shall become as if joined with one's own power.
In that month, for the welfare of the worlds, he beholds with his own eyes Acyuta, who is accompanied by Lakṣmī and is honored by Brahmā and the other gods.
Endowed with well-performed merit, he was filled by a portion of the Blessed One; that which is unattainable even for the gods was attainable for him, as was [the state] of the yogins. 118.
Having attained all desired prosperity and even greater majesty,
he entered into a city crowded with wealth and grain, and teeming with jewels.
Having attained an unshakable and all-pervading continuity,
he reached the further shore of both the sciences and the scriptures.
Having attained a long life and even enjoyments that are very difficult to obtain,
he was born for a long time as Smara (the God of Love) after having beheld the eternal Brahman.
At the time of death, he shall be accompanied by a hundred divine maidens;
having uplifted ten million members of his lineage, he goes to the supreme state.
O best of the twice-born, the means for accomplishing the Rājādhirāja-vidyā and the glorious eight-syllabled mantra cannot be described by me at the end of this [treatise]. || 123 ||
O best of the twice-born, by the command of Śrī Rāma, all the great sages who are yogis shall explain those various scriptures with their intellects.
O twice-born ones, even though it must be kept strictly secret from you, that which pertains to the Rājādhirāja-vidyā and the glorious eight-syllabled mantra has been told to you. (125)

[Thus ends the forty-third chapter in the Kāpila-tantra, in the latter portion of the Śrīmad-anuttara-brahma-tattva-rahasya-īśvara-saṃvāda-tantra, which is a compendium of the essential meaning of the Vedas.]
The Blessed One said:
O sons of Brahmā, I shall also describe the practice that must be kept strictly secret;
by hearing which, O twice-born ones, one becomes liberated while living and attains happiness.
He who is the ancient one, the source of all beings, possessed of great ascetic power, the sage, the bull among sages, the yogi, the eternal, Śaṅkara, and the infallible. || 2 ||
Out of a desire for the welfare of all the worlds, including those in the nether regions,
he likewise [acted] for the people of the Vindhya region and upon the surface of the earth.
The great yogi Śrī Puruṣottama has become manifest in this sacred field; he bestows liberation upon men merely by being seen, and thus his fame is spread far and wide. || 4 ||
From Mathurā up to Dvārakā,
Hari himself became the bestower of liberation and all goals of life even by his mere sight upon the earth.
The Naranārāyaṇī-vidyā,
which destroys all sins and produces immediate conviction, was previously proclaimed in this Tantra.
Whether in the city of Ayodhyā, or in Mathurā, or even in the city of Dvārakā, or in the sacred field of Puruṣottama; || 7 ||
I shall proclaim a single means of accomplishment that grants all perfections;
having come to any one of these sacred sites, one should remain there under a vow.
Having brought the teacher into his presence and preceded by his permission,
having bathed in the morning with a purified soul, and having performed the daily twilight devotions (saṃdhyā), || 9 ||
Having recited the Gāyatrī mantra many times, or three thousand one hundred times,
and having completed the daily fire-oblation (nityahoma), [one should then recite] the auspicious and glorious eight-syllabled mantra.

Then, immediately thereafter, one should recite the *Sahasraprajāpati* mantra more than a hundred times; and one should recite the *Vaiṣṇavī*, the great knowledge (*mahāvidyā*) of Vāsudeva, one hundred times.
One should daily recite five hundred times the mantra of Prasannakamalā,
or likewise that of Śrī, or the Rājarājeśvarī, consisting of twelve syllables.
Having recited the armor-mantra (varma) consisting of Nārāyaṇa twenty-eight times,
one should daily recite it twenty-five times with devotion for five days.
Having beheld the Blessed One in the temple of the Blessed One,
one should then recite the Nara-Nārāyaṇī Vidyā one hundred and eight times.
Then, one should perform all this daily in your temple;
one should always eat only one meal a day, or subsist on fruits, or consume sacrificial food (haviṣya). || 15 ||
Having thus performed the Caṇḍīvrata, on the sixth day at dawn, the observer of the vow,
having bathed, should wash his face with water brought by the preceptor.
Having completed the twilight rites according to the rules, and thereafter having performed the daily fire-oblation (agnihotra),
he should, with a concentrated mind, install the preceptor’s fire along with the sacrificial hearth.
Having taken either cow's ghee or pure ghee from a Kapila cow,
[he should offer it] twenty-eight times into the fire kindled with the preceding Sāvitrī mantra.
Having offered the twelve-syllable mantra in the same manner into the fire,
he who is firm in his vow should thereafter invoke Śrī and Nārāyaṇa.
Having worshipped this [deity] with services, or with auspicious couples, having performed each [rite] for the Arhat with the glorious eight-syllable vidyā.
Thereafter, one should offer more than a hundred oblations of clarified butter, a thousand times over,
with the mantra of Vāsudeva and the six-syllabled Vaiṣṇava mantra.
Having offered one hundred and eight [oblations] for each individual born into this world, he should afterwards satisfy them with food, water, or even with a pleasing gift.
Then, one should offer three hundred and twenty-eight oblations of clarified butter;
subsequently, one should offer each of these individually according to the specific Vidyās of the Lord’s rays.
O King of Kings, Manu also offered ghee twenty-eight times;
then, with mantras, he offered it five times.
Then, after that, having performed the fire sacrifice (homa) with the great vidyā of Nara-Nārāyaṇa, one should offer one hundred and eight oblations along with recitations (japa) and other rites.
Having performed the oblation of the *brahmarpaṇa* as prescribed for the atonement rite,
he then prostrated before his own preceptor’s two feet in the sacred fire.
Then, having prostrated before him at the edge of the lake with the eight limbs of the body like a staff, she,
being pure and well-dressed, removed her improper attire along with the garments of Kudraka and the others.
Having given a heap of wealth at the lotus-feet of the noble lady Dakṣī, and having offered the earth as well, he then surrendered it. || 28 ||
Even a small ornament, whether subtle or gross, becomes his pure adornment when conceived with the thought that it is Mahālakṣmī herself, even in her absence.
One should offer even one's male and female servants, goats, horses, and so forth to one's own guru;
or, if unable to do so, one should prostrate at the lotus feet of the ācārya.
Having given her earrings adorned with all their ornaments, and having offered auspicious garments for both her lower and upper robes, he bestowed them upon her. (31)
One should give wealth amounting to one hundred niṣkas at the feet of the preceptor;
or half of that, or even half of that, according to one's financial means, being free from stinginess.
Having given that sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), there is eternal satisfaction for those who have attained perfection;
it is like the joy of holding a beautiful golden lotus in one's hand.
Then, according to one's capacity, one should offer an ornament to his wife,
or a piece of auspicious gold accompanied by cloth, having risen for that purpose.
Then, according to one's capacity, one should give a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) to the brahmins who have spread out [the grass];
twenty-five arrows, or even fifteen.
Then, having performed a great festival there with the permission of his own preceptor, he should feed married women and the foremost of the twice-born for the sake of Hari. (36)
Thereafter, one should eat only after receiving the permission of the preceptor;
this applies whether one is in Udantapura, Mathurā, or even elsewhere. || 37 ||
In the city of Dvārakā, at the Śūtra lake, or at Puruṣottama, this meritorious vow known as "Iha" produces immediate conviction. || 38 ||
For three days from today, he shall behold Hari directly, even in a dream— Nārāyaṇa himself, the unborn and all-pervading Lord, accompanied by Nara.
[He saw] the one accompanied by Lakṣmī, joined by Queen Nīlā,
the beloved of Sundarī, surrounded by Brahmā, Rudra, Śakra, and the other gods.
From that time on, there has been no doubt that the Lord of the Universe was seen mounted upon the son of Vinatā, bearing the conch, discus, and other [emblems]. (41)
A divine portion of the Blessed One enters this body; it possesses the powers such as atomization (aṇimā), is the source of all qualities, and is auspicious by birth and origin. 42.
Prosperity endowed with wealth and grain, immovable and adorned with jewels; great power, health, and splendor, as well as excellent elephants and horses. (43)
The prosperity of one who is devoted to Hara increases in whatever way it may be;
there is an increase in sons, wives, and worthy vessels, as well as unshakable knowledge of Brahman. 44.
There is no doubt that the fortune of this man will remain in his body for twenty years;
this is the boon granted by the yogi Dattātreya to him year after year.
They will see him directly and he will grant them boons; of this there is no doubt.
This son of Daśaratha is the Lord Acyuta himself, the all-pervading one.

Viṣṇu, the Lord of Lakṣmī, who consists of the Brahman of sound, the bull-bannered one (Śiva), and the son of the Earth (Viṣṇu), manifested on the bank of the Suvarṇamukharī in order to favor the world. 47.
Requested by the hosts of sages and deities, as well as by all the sustainers of the world,
he who rests upon the infinite couch of yoga remains unmoving upon the serpent Śeṣa.
The Creator of the universe appeared together with Jānakī and Puṣpānuta;
Oṃ, the sons of Vāyu and others [praised] the Leader of Janācala. 49.
She went to serve the one renowned as Vikaṇṭheśa; today, that Āryā resides at the seat (pīṭha) of the city of Ayodhyā on Mount Añjana. || 50 ||
Regarding that which is called the abode of Śrīraṅga, there too this Blessed One is remembered as Rāma, Udāśathisvāmī, and Raṅganātha. || 51 ||
There also is the auspicious lion-throne, the wheel of the python of Ayodhyā;
there resides the leader of the serpents, Vidhviśoṇamosaura.
That city named Ayodhyā bestows liberation upon being seen;
the second is Naimiṣāraṇya, which grants the fruit of immediate liberation.
The third is called Śrīnivāsa, which brings liberation from the bondage of existence;
the fourth is proclaimed as the field of Bhukri, known as Ragadhāma.
In Śrīnivāsabhikṣu resides that Vidyā consisting of the three Vedas;
she consists of all sacred seats, and she consists of knowledge, dharma, and austerity.
If anyone, firm in their vows, should constantly mutter this mantra—ending with the eight-syllabled Śrīvidyā and preceded by the word "Śrī"—anywhere at all; || 56 ||
Even one who has died among the Sakīkaṭas shall be born in the city of Ayodhyā;
he who is pure and worships Śrīnivāsa in these sacred fields [attains the same]. || 57 ||
Or by performing it for one night according to Prajāpati, he certainly becomes successful;
this Mahāvidyā of Śrīnivāsa produces immediate conviction.
It should be known as the bestower of all success and the destroyer of the obstacles of destiny;
[this] Great Vidyā of Śrīnivāsa emerged from the lotus-face of the Ācārya. 59.
Whoever, having taken hold [of this], recites it, becomes a sovereign lord of the Siddhas.
O Śrīnivāsa, this Great Vidyā is the liberator from the bonds of existence. 60.
She who bestows longevity and health, and grants all perfections through her assembly—let one remember even the mere name "Śrīnivāsa" every day. (61)
For him, all perfections are attained without the need for recitation, fire-offerings, and the like;
Śrīnivāsa is the sacred field, and Śrīnivāsa is the Lord of the Universe. 62.
This triad of great vidyās concerning Śrīnivāsa is very difficult to obtain; yet, by the constant remembrance of Śrīnivāsa, it is attained anywhere at all. 63.
O best of the twice-born, by worshipping the Abode of Śrī for three days, one who is liberated from heaps of sins beholds that Supreme Reality.
Even by Brahmā, Rudra, Maheśvara, Indra, and others, he is worshipped there;
by beholding Śrīnivāsa, one is liberated from heaps of sins.
Through the daily recitation of the Mahāvidyā of Śrīnivāsa, one perceives with one's own eyes the Self in the form of Brahman; such is the power of this mantra.
Having enjoyed the splendor of Indra even here, he rejoices in the supreme abode;
likewise in this city of Ayodhyā and in the great forest of Naimiṣa.

O twice-born ones, even though he is Śeṣa himself, this glorious and all-pervading Lord Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, who consists of the Supreme Brahman, resides in the sacred field known as Śrīraṅgadhāma.
In Nārāyaṇa resides the Lord of the Universe, accompanied by Śrī and Vāsava;
she is auspicious, constantly bestowing all perfections in these sacred fields. 69.
O Śrīnivāsa, this great lore (mahāvidyā) should be chanted; it bestows subjugation and desired objects.
At the beginning is the seed-syllable consisting of the three Vedas, known as the Prāṇava, which is most exalted. (70)
One should utter the great seed-syllable of Śrī, which consists of the wind (ya) mounted upon fire (ra), joined with the left eye (ī), and followed by the letter ta. (71)

The seed-syllable of Śiva (H) with the long vowel (Ī), followed by Vavāhni (Ra), endowed with the bindu (M)—this is the Māyā-bīja (HRĪM). Then, from the Yamvra [group], the fourth syllable (Va) and likewise the next syllable (Pha). (72)
The seed-syllable of Śrī is devoid of the letter *ra*, joined with the abode (*va*) and the heart (*ha*), followed by the thirteen vowels, and endowed with the three folds (*valī*). (73)
The Great Queen is a true friend who bestows all fruits;
she grants the sovereignty of powers such as *aṇimā* and increases longevity. (74)
In former times,
the venerable Nārada, the son of Brahmā, obtained this knowledge from the lotus-mouth of the Infinite One (Viṣṇu) through his great power.
Having attained omniscience through recitation and being honored even by the gods,
he attains the power of atomization twice over and wanders through the three worlds.
Therefore, the venerable Nārada became the seer (ṛṣi) of this [hymn];
the connection with Śrī Devī, who is the very essence of existence, is the subject matter for the world. 77.
When "Śrīnivāsa" is uttered, he is the Lord of Lakṣmī and Rāma;
this Śrīnivāsa, the abode of liberation and Lakṣmī, is higher than the highest.
He is known as Śrīnivāsa because he is the abode of the glory of universal sovereignty, the Lord of the World who dwells with Śrī,
and the abode of Mahālakṣmī.
This abode of royal splendor is called Śrīnivāsa;
it is the great mantra of Śrīnivāsa, the essence of the three Vedas, and the source of great prosperity.
One who, with one-pointed concentration, should always apply himself [to this] is called Śrīnivāsa;
because he takes refuge in Śrīnivāsa, he is called the mountain Śrīnivāsa.
He who would cast off his body in these three sacred fields (kṣetra) [is liberated].
The great yogi Śrīnivāsa shall abide in the supreme state. || 82 ||
Whether one recites [the mantra] at the great altar of Śrīnivāsa or where there is a *kruñca* bird, Śrīnivāsa shall indeed be present; at the end, one shall attain the glory of liberation.
O Śrīnivāsa, this great lore (mahāvidyā) bestows manifest results;
it must be guarded as the giver of all auspiciousness, even at the cost of one's life-breaths reaching the throat. (84)
Whether reciting the Mahāvidyā of Śrīnivāsa here or anywhere else,
one obtains the full and desired grace of Śrīnivāsa.
The seer of this is the great yogi Nārada, the son of Brahmā;
its metre is said to be Jāgata, or it is remembered as Gāyatra. (86)
Śrīnivāsa, the leader of the three worlds, the Supreme Lord, Nārāyaṇa, the husband of Mahālakṣmī, is called the Deity. (87)
The seed-syllable of Śrī is said to be *vijit*, while the power (*śakti*) is the *bhuvanamātṛkā*.
The *kīlaka* is the *kāmarāja*; it is employed for the attainment of desired goals.

One should perform the six-limbed ritual (ṣaḍaṅga) accompanied by the Praṇava, joined with the Śrī-dṛṣṭi; the six-limbed rite is performed by repeating twice the seed-syllables of Lakṣmī and the others.
I worship Him who is seated upon His left lap together with Lakṣmī, who is adorned with a mace, sword, conch, and a flaming spear, whose waist is resplendent with a belt of pure jewels,
who is ever-gracious, whose feet are incessantly praised by Brahmā, Śiva, Indra, and other leaders, and who is the heart of the yogis.
O Abode of Lakṣmī, O you who grant fearlessness to the world, O destroyer of the wicked! 90.
For that high-minded one who meditates daily upon Śrīnivāsa, the great knowledge in this manner, there are no longer any remaining duties of the *puraścaraṇa* rite.
The great sages, the knowers of Brahman, have declared this to be the perfected science of inquiry;
O sons of Brahmā, I shall now explain its application, which destroys death.
In the most excellent field of Vatastha, being pure and attentive in mind,
having placed his head at the feet of the Guru and received his command, he should bathe in the morning with a concentrated mind.
Having restricted my diet and observed fixed vows, I recited the glorious eight-syllable mantra more than three thousand times. (94)
Afterwards, having recited the Vāsudeva mantra and the six-syllabled Vaiṣṇava mantra one hundred and eight times, as well as the mantra named Śrīhṛdaya; (95)
One should constantly recite the twelve-syllable Śrī-vidyā five hundred times;
one should recite the Rājarājeśvarī-vidyā twenty-eight times.
One should constantly recite the Vaiṣṇava mantra twenty-five times; at night, one should recite the Śrīnivāsa mantra one thousand three hundred times.
Having performed this most purifying vow for five days, one should rise early on the sixth day, bathe in the morning, and remain composed in mind. (98)
Having prepared one thousand three hundred oblations of Kapila ghee, the preceptor should offer them into the fire with the glorious eight-syllable vidyā.
Alternatively, having struck pure cow-ghee twenty-eight times with the Śrī-mantra by means of Vāsudeva Viṣṇu, thereafter—
Having slain five hundred in the fire by means of the vidyā called Rājarāja, and then having slain them twenty-eight times by means of the armor-vidyās as well; 101.

Having divided the mantra of Śrīnivāsa fivefold, one should offer three hundred oblations into the fire with that vidyā; then, one should likewise offer oblations with the letters beginning with *ya*.
Having offered the oblation with the realization that it is an offering unto Brahman, and having prostrated before the fire,
one should thereafter bow down like a staff before the pair of feet of the Guru with the eight limbs of the body.
Then, having adorned [the preceptor] with ornaments and excellent garments,
one should subsequently place a thousand gold coins (niṣkas) at the two feet of the teacher.
Or three hundred niṣkas, or even a pītaviṣka, or half of that, or half of that again, avoiding any stinginess regarding one's wealth. (105)
Having given garments, golden ornaments, and other gifts to the teacher’s wife, he gave five cows to the Brahmins who were well-versed in the Vedas.
In the *nyāyabhakṣya* era, at the end of the *anoka* period, he performed sacrifices with sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*) and oblations;
accompanied by his entire circle of kinsmen, he enjoyed the food of his preceptor. || 107 ||
Having received from the mouth of the Guru blessings that grant success, on that very day, accompanied by Bharata and others in a dream, [he beheld the Lord]. 108.
I bow to the great-souled Śrīnivāsa, accompanied by Jānakī,
the Lord of the Universe, Nārāyaṇa, who is praised by Hanumān.

O Lord of Brahmā, Śakra, and others, these [beings] will certainly behold with their own eyes the one who is worshipped even by heaven itself, whose face is serene, and who is born from the water-lily. 110.
Then, month after month, you shall see in a dream the Lord of the Universe,
the beloved of Jānakī, who bestows grace, appearing before you in person.
Though he was dull-witted and unfortunate, day by day he became a master of all branches of knowledge, even though he had been lacking in self-control.
Having become a great poet, eloquent, and possessed of superior intellect,
he attained inexhaustible glory from King Mahendra and Sudṛśī.
Having attained wealth, grain, a virtuous lineage, and an abundance of pearls, gems, and the like, as well as the eightfold sovereign powers, long life, and supreme health; 114.
Having personally seen with his own eyes the pure yoga endowed with its eight limbs and the recollection of his former births within the self of Nārāyaṇa.
Even now, he remains immersed in the ocean of a thousand lineages;
endowed with divine enjoyments and accompanied by hundreds of celestial maidens, he shall dwell in the celestial realm.
Resembling a hundred Kamadepas and bearing divine weapons,
he rejoices in the supreme abode in the presence of Indira and her ten thousand attendants.
O Śrīnivāsa, whoever, having conquered his senses, performs this vow in any one of these sacred fields—or even in all of them—[attains the fruit]. (118)
Jānakī-Lakṣmī herself goes to him every day as if he were her son;
even those who have been born from his loins attain the status of friends. (119)
The lords of the directions bestow jewels such as the cintāmaṇi and other gems;
Vasiṣṭha and others honor him who is devoted to the Lord of Janakī.
The highly fortunate ones, Nārada and others, who are knowers of Brahman and performers of penance, constantly bestow upon her the desired fruit; of this there is no doubt. (121)
The Godāvarī, Bhīmarathī, Kṛṣṇaveṇā, and Narmadā;
the Sarasvatī, Yamunā, and the Kāverī, the best of rivers. 122.
The Jāhnavī, the Candrabhāgā, and the great river Gaṇḍakī— at any one of these places, or anywhere else, being pure— (123)
He who performs this Śrīnivāsa-vrata according to the prescribed rules becomes a great ocean of wisdom, possessing the splendor of Bṛhaspati through his various branches of knowledge.
Resembling Kandarpa in beauty, wealth,
and fortune, he attained a long life and the yoga endowed with its eight limbs.
In a single birth, she, who is difficult even for yogins to attain, reaches the supreme goal from which there is no return. 126.
By whatever means possible, the twice-born should perform the preliminary rite (puraścaryā) one thousand times or even a hundred times under the guidance of a teacher. || 127 ||
Having performed the preliminary rite (puraścaryā) twelve times, or eight times,
or even three times, one should give the complete sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
One should always strive with diligence for the sake of beholding the Blessed One;
one should give a gift accompanied by a full sacrificial fee, neither too much nor too little.
There too, O Śakra, one should give a fee to the feet of the teacher, abandoning all deceit, for the sake of attaining the desired success. (130)
If a practitioner of vows performs a ritual for the public without following the prescribed injunctions, only his own ruin comes to pass. || 131 ||
Even if one performs a thousand times the auspicious rite known as *puraścaryā* without the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), one never attains success anywhere.
Having abandoned the deceitfulness of the learned, even while living as a mendicant on the surface of the earth,
he placed his right foot upon the pair of feet of the Teacher, impelled by the [divine] weapon.
Even without performing the preliminary rite (puraścaryā), one attains perfection in the vidyā here;
through it, manifold auspicious prosperity shall arise at every step. (134)
Even after giving away great wealth amounting to thousands of millions,
one should remain devoted to the service of the pair of the teacher’s feet.
Great fortune is indeed accomplished, as well as the imperishable sovereignty over all;
for him, the Great Vidyā is perfected, and even divinity is accomplished. (136)
Even with thousands of merits, perfection in the state of identity with Brahman is not attained at all, even by means of complete recitations or hymns of praise.
Having obtained the mantra from the command of the Guru, making that [mantra] his lotus-feet,
and thus constantly worshipping it, he attains the realization of identity with Brahman.
Having worshipped daily with faith, preceded by the command of the teacher of the glorious eight-syllabled mantra, one becomes a possessor of the attainment of identity with Brahman. 139.
Having daily recited, according to one's ability and by the permission of the preceptor, the fifteen-syllable mantra of Śrī, which consists of all vidyās; 140.
Endowed with the sixfold sovereignty, one attains the perfection of identity with Brahman by recollecting the twelve-syllable mantra of Śrī-Śrīśa, which is the Brahma-vidyā. 141.
At the time of Brahmā, one who is pure should daily worship Rājarājeśvarī with the *Yathāśarṣa* mantra; through this, one certainly attains perfection. 142.
Having remembered the identity with Brahman through the permission of the teacher,
one becomes a possessor of perfection on this earth, due to the causes for the complete realization of identity with Brahman.
These five have been proclaimed by the ancient knowers of Brahman who possess the eye of wisdom;
there are also other great vidyās, which are like jewels upon the surface of the earth. (144)
For the bestowal of godhood and such states leads indeed to rebirth;
however, through the glorious eight-syllable Vidyā, one becomes the Lord of the End (Śameśvara).
Even the giver of the fifteen-syllable Śrīsūkta is called Hari;
even the giver of ignorance to the king of kings is Maheśvara. (146)
He is declared in the worlds to be omniscient by the great seers who know Brahman best;
he is also remembered as Nārāyaṇa himself, the bestower of the knowledge of Brahman. (147)
These preceptors, the best among those honored by the earth, are of the nature of Nārāyaṇa;
the sovereign lady of all knowledge is called the Brahmavidyā. || 148 ||
Then follows the sovereign queen of Śrī with fifteen syllables; even beyond that, the glorious eight-spoked [mantra] is the sovereign queen, all of which grant true success. || 149 ||
Even greater than that is the Great Vidyā of the King of Kings;
for even a single Great Vidyā is obtained here from her lotus-like face. (150)
The wise declare that supreme state beyond all defects to be the very nature of Nārāyaṇa;
indeed, the worship of that pair of feet alone bestows the perfection of identity with Brahman. 151.
Whether he possesses two branches of knowledge or even three, that Brahmin whose mouth provides sustenance is indeed obtained by practitioners here. (152)
Who indeed is capable of describing the service rendered to that teacher, from whose mouth the fourfold knowledge is obtained on this earth? (153)
Even the gods, such as Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa, as well as the great sages, are not capable of describing even a fraction of that pair of feet. || 154 ||
For one who possesses the understanding that the deity consists of the Blessed One, even a mantra composed in a vernacular language is fully effective for them. (155)
The mantras beginning with Śrīnivāsa possess millions upon millions of virtues; by the mere recollection of which all perfections (siddhis) whatsoever are accomplished. (156)
O Śrīnivāsa, this Great Knowledge (Mahāvidyā), when recited by practitioners anywhere at the command of their preceptor, immediately produces conviction.
O Śrīnivāsa, having constantly recited even this Mahāvidyā on the surface of the earth with a restrained mind, by the command of the preceptor— (158)
Having attained great perfection, she beholds the Lord of Śrī himself;
I speak the truth, I speak what is beneficial, and I speak the essence again and again. (159)
One must daily and invariably attend upon the two feet of the Guru;
the glorious eight-syllable mantra, which bestows all perfections, should be recited. 160.
Then the fifteen-syllable Vidyā of Śrī should be recited;
this auspicious Vidyā, the Sovereign of the Kings of Kings, should be remembered every day. 161.
This fourfold [path] has been declared by the great sages to be the means for attaining the glory of liberation; all other methods are said to yield only the fruit of exhaustion. 162.
It is true that this bestows the fruit of identity with the Supreme Brahman;
for one who possesses the great siddhis such as becoming a deity and so forth, those four [powers] follow from it. (163)
This Rāma, son of Daśaratha, is the Blessed One, the Supreme Lord;
he is Nārāyaṇa, the creator of the world, consisting of bliss and consciousness. || 164 ||
For the sake of accomplishing this service and for the attainment of constant vision, I have declared four means of realization upon the surface of the earth. (165)

Having deliberated with the [wise] companions and having deliberated again and again, [the knowledge] is superior to that which was bitten from the very beginning by the pair of the Teacher’s feet. 166.
Then follows the second Brahmavidyā, and after that the glorious Aṣṭākṣarī; then the fifteen-syllable Śrīsūkta-mantra, and the auspicious Rājarājeśvarī. (167)
Without effort, this entire great accomplishment is seen;
previously, I [taught] the fivefold practice of Mukarekṭima. (168)
In this regard, the seed-syllable of Śrī is said to bestow liberation; through the cultivation of devotion to Śrī, one is eternally intent upon the attainment of liberation. 169.
"Know Nārāyaṇa, O Acyuta, who has assumed the form of a rogue man.
Having spoken thus, the blessed yogi Kapila, the son of Kardama, [departed]. (170)
O ascetics rich in penance, having heard that scripture of Kapila, the powerful son of Brahmā returned to his own hermitage there with the permission of Śrī Rāma.
Having praised Rāma, the lord of the world, together with Brahmā,
they were liberated from all doubts and descended to the Satyaloka.
The remaining sages, Vāmadeva and others, who were firm in their vows, having heard this unsurpassed scripture, the essence of all the Vedas; 173.
Delighted, joyful, and with faces beaming with smiles, they honored Rāma at his hermitage.
Then Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrti said:
The majesty of the Vidyā of the Queen of the Queens of Kings, which destroys the afflictions of the world. || 174 ||
Having heard it from the lotus-like mouth of Kapila, the great sages headed by Vasiṣṭha,
as well as the yogins led by Sanatkumāra, then observed their vows.
Having propitiated the Blessed One, those who subsist on his skull-ash,
having beheld the Lord of the World directly, thereafter became liberated while living.
O Queen, O Daughter of the Mountain, I have told you a little of this great Vidyā, which possesses great majesty and destroys all poisons today. 175.

[Thus ends the forty-fourth chapter, titled "The Majesty of the King of Sciences of the Arising of the Science of Good Fortune," in the latter portion of the *Śrīmanuttarabrahmatattvarahasya*, the *Dāśarathīya Tantra*, which is a compendium of the essential meaning of the Vedas.]
The illustrious Dakṣiṇāmūrti said:
In the city of Ayodhyā, the All-pervading Lord, having previously manifested as Rāma,
the son of Daśaratha, was born from the womb of Kauśalyā.
Resembling ten thousand gods of love (Kandarpa), I am accompanied by Utkī and am eternally served by the enemies of Bharata, such as the son of Añjanā (Hanumān) and others.
He was constantly served by the Brahman-sages, headed by Vasiṣṭha, and by his excellent ministers, such as Sumantra; he was the Lord himself in human form.
The restraint of those who are dear and the thorough protection of those who are not dear;
O Umā, [he taught] all these dharmas which bestow the perfection of the *khila* [supplementary] teachings.
While narrating the essence of the Vedānta, that king told the scripture which is the great seed of the knowledge of Brahman and is difficult even for the son of Daśaratha to obtain.
Herein has been declared primarily the eternal Gāyatrī and other mantras;
thereafter, the Brahmavidyā and the Śrī-Śrīśa Dvādaśākṣarī have been proclaimed.
The glorious, eternal Eight-Syllabled Vidyā, together with its secret, has been declared; it is said to be the cause of liberation when properly practiced, and the bestower of all perfections.
That very [knowledge] is proclaimed in the Vedas, the Śāstras, the Purāṇas, and the Āgamas as the cause of the sovereignty of liberation; no other is remembered.
O Dear One, the Śrīdvādaśākṣarī Vidyā has thus been declared primarily;
and first, the Lakṣmī Vidyā, which bestows all accomplishments, has been described.
The supreme Nārāyaṇī-vidyā has been thus described primarily;
then, the fifteen-syllable vidyā of Śrīdevī was proclaimed.
Furthermore, the complete perfection of royal fortune was told;
thereafter, the vidyā of the Queen of Queens (Rājarājeśvarī) was proclaimed many times.
Other great vidyās have also been proclaimed therein;
however, because this one consists of eight syllables, its majesty is the remover of even today's [sins]. (12)
In this *Daśarathīya-tantra*,
it has been briefly stated that Dattātreya is a great yogi who is born directly from a portion of the Blessed One.
Having heard that supreme tantra, a compendium equal to the Vedas,
the Lord of the World composed it for the sake of blessing the worlds.
The blessed Sanatkumāra, the omniscient treasury of ascetic powers,
fashioned a most great jewel in his own name, which bestows all perfections.
The powerful Raṅgukā, the direct partial incarnation of Nārāyaṇa and his son,
[composed] the tantra named Brahmavidyāvilāsa, which is equal to the Vedānta.
The son of Brahmā, Vasiṣṭha, whose splendor is great and who is the husband of Arundhatī, composed this most magnificent treatise, which brings prosperity to the entire world. || 17 ||
He related to the sages this scripture, a compendium of the meaning of the Vedas;
he was the son of Yājñavalkya, born directly from a portion of Śaṅkara.
With great reverence, he related that tantra named Sārasvata,
the root scripture called Dāśarathīya, which is a compendium of Vedānta.
The Pañcasamhitā was proclaimed by the venerable sages;
thereafter, Ajanātanaya became a servant of the Lord of Jānakī.
The Lord, the all-pervading one, who consists of the Vedic meters, then narrated the Saṃhitā, which is equal in authority to the Śruti, to the sages; he was born from Vinatā.
He taught this secret scripture, which is dear to him, even to the yogis;
for among all scriptures, this is the supreme root scripture. (22)
Whatever is stated in this tantra is remembered as equal to the Veda;
no lack of faith should be entertained here by one who desires the fortune of liberation. (23)
The pair of feet of the preceptor must certainly be served daily;
the glorious eight-syllabled mantra (Aṣṭākṣarī-vidyā) should be recited purely, for it bestows accomplishment.
These words of Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrtistava are this most secret scripture, equal to the Vedas and Vedānta; it was not spoken of old even to the high-souled Janaka by Nārāyaṇa.
Then Nārāyaṇa himself, the Lord and husband of Jānakī,
questioned me in the presence of the great sages headed by Vasiṣṭha.
The Blessed One taught that most secret and auspicious scripture;
by a portion of it, I, Rudra, the conqueror of death, Śiva, have crossed over.
O Goddess, O Daughter of the Mountain, you who possess a wondrous nature, [protect] me, Śrī Rāmacandra, from whoever on earth seeks to cause me harm. (28)
In the most terrible Saraurava hell, Satyā went to Candratīraka;
Rāma alone is the Supreme Brahman, the Seal, Viṣṇu, and the Creator of beings. || 29 ||
This supreme, auspicious, and most secret [teaching] within the Tantra was directly revealed by Nārāyaṇa, the Infinite One, to Vāmana, the Destroyer of Naraka. 30.
Having heard this most secret scripture uttered by the son of Daśaratha, the disciple, with a self-restrained mind, should cause it to be heard from the lotus-mouth of the teacher.
One should honor the teacher with wealth, garments, and even ornaments;
for one of deluded intellect who does not fully honor the teacher, who is the speaker of the weapons [of knowledge], [attains no success].
He who, though high-minded, does not honor the speaker of the scripture suffers a loss of action and finds no success in his undertakings. || 33 ||

One attains the eternal state from which there is no return, as well as a sacred pit (kuṇḍa) that increases prosperity, the increase of grain, and the increase of good fortune, along with constant auspiciousness. (34)
"Having attained this through the hearing of the scriptures, one shall thereafter go to the supreme state, the abode of Rati.
Thus spoke Śiva, the Supreme Self, to the goddess Girijā; so said Ṛṣyaśṛṅga.
The digit of consciousness (citkalā) begins with the Manu Āsya;
the former was spoken by Nārāyaṇa and the latter was uttered by Śaṅkara.
In this *Tantra* called the *Dāśarathīya*, which is a compendium of the essential meaning of the Vedas, even a single chapter [is sufficient] for one who possesses knowledge of its meaning. (37)
Whoever recites or even hears this, being liberated from heaps of sins, goes to the supreme, eternal, and unsurpassed abode. (38)
Having heard this from the lotus-like mouth of Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, the great sages realized themselves to be the Supreme Brahman, and [recognized] Rāma as the all-pervading Nārāyaṇa. (39)
Having addressed Ṛṣyaśṛṅga and understood the secret of dharma,
they then departed, having accomplished their purpose, radiant and with joyful faces.
In this matter, the Great Deed was performed by the Savior in the form of Brahman;
it was spoken by the Protector of Jānakī, who summarized the essential meaning of the Vedas, as the cause for the liberation of the world. 41.

[Thus ends the forty-fifth chapter, titled "The Exposition of the Secret of the Scripture on the Majesty of the Royal Knowledge," in the *Saubhāgyavidhodaya*, the latter portion of the *Vedasārārthasaṃgraha*, the *Dāśarathīya Tantra* concerning the secret of the supreme reality of Brahman.]
Salutations to Śrī Nārāyaṇa, who is accompanied by Indirā. Śrī Rāma is Śrī; Śrī Rāma is Śrī Vīḍvarāsaṃdalī.

He whose lotus feet are honored by the crowns of the heads of all the wise, he who is the ocean of Hari, he who is the Mother of even the most insignificant creature, he who is named Dharaṇī (the Earth), and he who holds the flute.
The lineage of Bhāradvāja, the family of Uśija, the effort [of the sacrifice], from whence [it arose], and also its name. || 1 ||

The Goddess Śrī Kamalā is the triple power (triśakti), and he is surrounded by Kamalā, Śrī, Rājyalakṣmī, Bhūnīlā, Vimalā, and the other powers; he is served by the Vedas, the directions, and Brahmā; this Lord of the Raghus is the inner light, the beloved of the beautiful Śrī, the teacher who is the refuge of the Sun, and by him this has been illuminated. || 2 ||

To him who has drunk the stream of nectar flowing from the lotus-face of the illustrious Great Daśarathi— the secret manual that plays with the brush of the *tilaka* mark— may I, with eyes moistened by the longing for service, go to the flute-player (Kṛṣṇa), whose essence is the mantra of the Queen of Queens (Rājarājeśvarī) and who possesses the pair of lips of the joy of the Raghus (Rāmacandra). || 3 ||

O Śrīdevī, toward Your feet, the younger brother of Hari, may this [devotion] be granted to us—those whose intellect is firm in the worship of the Śrīcakra and who delight in the True Play; for it acts like a mother’s lover, even toward one of crooked mind, until the end of life. 4.

In the Śaka year measured by the Guhas (nine), the eyes (two), and the earth (one) [1729], on the sixth lunar day of the dark fortnight of the month of Śrāvaṇa, Vaṃśīdhara has here written this *Raghuttama-tantra*, the essence of the Vedas, for the satisfaction of the illustrious Lord. || 5 ||
